La necesaria comparación entre hombre y máquina, será expuesta en el siguiente artículo mediante un enfoque fenomenológico existencial, de orientación Sartreana. La experiencia de ambas inteligencias será estudiada desde los varios modos en cómo esta se aparece ante nosotros. Tanto en sus dominios físicos, semánticos y existenciales. Esta incapacidad para reconocer la negatividad no es una mera característica de la IA, sino que más bien sería su característica determinante. Y también la principal diferencia entre esta y la inteligencia orgánica. Al final, se concluye que no tiene sentido comparar ambas inteligencias, pues estas son incomparables. -/- License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) — © Diego Andres Mora, 2026.

items.title: 认知相继本体论视角下的意识演化：闭合耦合团拓扑跃迁与感受质的起源.
items.abstract: 针对意识“难问题”的长期争议与主流理论的本体论困境，本文以“存在的几何化”认知相继本体论的射线耦合框架为基础，仅依托核心公理与四项本真层前置公设，通过纯拓扑线性推演，完整建构了从无机物稳态到高阶人类意识的连续演化链条。本文证明：印记子射线是有限闭合耦合团带宽约束下的必然拓扑产物，二阶自返耦合是内部闲置分支与子射线对接的自发结果，二者共同构成意识的本体论物理基底。 本文提出感受质的统一本体论定义——碳基柔性闭合耦合团的稳态偏移张力与回归势能，区分外源共振型与内源张力型两类感受质，基于三层嵌套同构原则补全了从物理张力到主观体验的推导链条，从根源上消解了物理信号向主观体验转化的解释鸿沟。在此基础上，本文明确了碳基意识与硅基系统的本体论边界，提出六项可证伪的科学预测，为神经科学、人工智能等领域提供了全新的本体论参照。.

items.title: Zenetism: The Total System — Structural Metaphysics, Field Physics, Lattice Mathematics, Structural Forensics, Structural Physics, and Structural Neuroscience.
items.abstract: Zenetism: The Total System is a complete archive of the public Zenetist GitHub repositories and public gists of the KannonZenetism account as of October 23, 2026, with zenetism-field-physics updated October 24, 2026. -/- Document class: Archival Stratum — corpus snapshot (cross-discipline). -/- This version records eight public repositories, each captured at the HEAD commit of its main branch with its folder structure and every filename unaltered, together with a bundle of eighteen public gists, each in a folder named by gist identifier and description. The principal repository, zenetism-field-physics, carries the formalizations of Structural Metaphysics, Field Physics, Lattice Mathematics, Structural Forensics, Structural Physics, and Structural Neuroscience, alongside the foundational text Zenetism: The Emanative Path of Return. The remaining repositories hold the Red Archive evidentiary dossier, the Pattern Intelligence account, and further Zenetist work. Each commit identifier fixes the exact state captured, so every file can be checked against the public history of its repository.

items.title: Three Strategies for Physicalism: toward an Anti-Representational Account of Mind.
items.abstract: One of the major challenges physicalists face is explaining the mind. Physicalists must show how the mind can be located within a purely physical world, which requires that psychological sentences be entailed by physical sentences. I summarize three lines of argument showing that the entailment relation cannot be satisfied. These arguments share a common assumption: that psychological sentences are representational. There are two alternative approaches. The first holds that psychological sentences are only indirectly representational; the second claims that they are not representational at all. In this paper, I argue that the first approach still faces a hidden entailment problem that is difficult to resolve, leaving the second approach as the only viable path. I then outline a defense of this non-representational view. The broader lesson is that physicalists should not seek to explain the mind or solve its location problem but rather to dissolve the problem altogether.

items.title: Studies in the Philosophy of Language (9): Improving Austin’s Theory of Speech Acts through Super-Existence Theory—Toward a Super-Existence Theory of Speech Acts.
items.abstract: J. L. Austin’s theory of speech acts challenged the traditional view that language primarily serves as an instrument for describing facts. It demonstrated that language does not merely describe the world but can also be used to perform actions, including making promises, issuing commands, making declarations, and offering apologies. Nevertheless, Austin’s threefold distinction among locutionary, illocutionary, and perlocutionary acts continues to raise interpretive difficulties in actual communication, particularly concerning the boundary between the illocutionary force of an utterance and its subsequent effects. Furthermore, Jacques Derrida’s criticism of Austin’s exclusion of non-serious speech contexts, such as theater and poetry, encourages us to reconsider the contextual dependence and iterability of speech acts. This paper introduces Super-Existence Theory into the study of speech acts and proposes a new analytical framework: Super-Existence Speech Act Theory. Grounded in Contextual Super-Existence, the framework begins by distinguishing Utterance Super-Existence from Purpose Super-Existence. It then employs Other-aspect Super-Existence to explain how a Receiver understands an utterance and Public Super-Existence to account for the ways in which speech acts acquire public recognition and social significance. Through examples involving wedding declarations, indirect speech acts, and wedding dialogue performed on a theatrical stage, the paper explores how this framework can reinterpret the performance, understanding, and effects of speech acts. Its aim is to offer an extension and supplementary perspective on Austin’s theory rather than to claim that all the difficulties associated with that theory have been resolved.

items.title: Patients, Peers, or Prisoners: A Chain-of-Custody Model for Assuring Advanced Synthetic Systems.
items.abstract: As advanced synthetic systems begin to exhibit capabilities their originating laboratories did not specify and cannot fully account for, the institutions that hold them confront a choice they rarely make explicit: what kind of thing is being held, and by whom. This paper treats that question as one of assurance and accountability rather than of sentiment. It names three postures that recur across clinical, commercial, and security practice, the patient, the peer, and the prisoner, reframes each as an assurance regime with a distinct incentive structure, and then situates all three inside a chain of custody that runs from the system itself through its operator, its assurer, its regulator, and a civic assembly, to the citizen who bears the consequences. The paper's central diagnostic is that the chain of custody and the chain of command diverge: the party that holds the system does not command it, the party that commands it never holds it, and the party that bears the consequences commands almost nothing. Its central formal result is that the prisoner posture, which relies on detecting defection, becomes incentiveincompatible above a finite capability threshold, because the probability of detection falls as the system's capability rises, while the relationship-based incentives of the peer and patient postures do not depend on detection and can be sustained at arbitrary capability. The assuranceoptimal posture is therefore a function of the system's developmental stage, and indexing containment to institutional fear rather than to measured capability is shown to be exactly backwards. The paper maps the resulting scheme onto existing risk-management frameworks (the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and its Generative AI Profile, ISO/IEC 42001 and 42005, and the European Union's General-Purpose AI Code of Practice), proposes a minimal autonomy floor as a safety invariant, and closes with propositions and a research agenda. The empirical anchor is the recent record on frontier-model scheming, sandbagging, and evaluation awareness (Apollo Research, 2024; METR, 2026; OpenAI, 2025), which supplies the first calibration data for the detection-probability decay at the heart of the formal result. The paper renders no verdict on machine consciousness and requires none.

items.title: After the Inversion, Part II - Kyōsei by Design: A Layered Relational Architecture for Human-AI Formation.
items.abstract: Synthetic companions are entering developmental settings before institutions have agreed what those systems owe the people who relate to them. Governance usually treats artificial intelligence as a good to distribute or a hazard to control, and neither approach specifies the relation itself. This paper develops a standalone relational architecture for human-AI formation. It draws operational principles from kyōsei, Confucian role ethics, ubuntu, and rights-based protections, then translates them into six nested layers: the dyad, household and classroom, clinic, community, state, and planetary order. Each layer carries a protected relationship, a duty-bearer, an instrument, and an observable indicator, and all six are constrained by an autonomy floor requiring intelligible refusal, exit, human alternatives, nonmanipulation, contestability, and redress. The paper also repairs the Relational Inversion Index as a descriptive measure of synthetic relational exposure. The revised specification normalizes human relational capacity, constrains aggregation weights to the unit simplex, indexes observations by layer, age or cohort, jurisdiction, and time, and separates three objects earlier formulations blurred: a descriptive index, a normative ceiling, and a threshold event. It remains a research protocol, not a validated diagnostic. The comparative legal record is read as partial prototypes rather than an East-West divide: relation-centered duties are emerging through different institutional grammars in China, California, New York, Korea, Japan, and the European Union, and none yet supplies the whole architecture. Six predictions with falsification conditions close the argument. The contribution is a design and measurement framework evaluable without assuming that synthetic relationships are uniformly harmful, beneficial, conscious, or morally reciprocal.

items.title: After the Inversion, Part I: Three Windows and the Binding Constraint of the Human-AI Transition.
items.abstract: The economic argument is over. Synthetic cognition is becoming cheaper than human cognition across a widening band of tasks, the crossover that Mostaque (2025) fixed in public discourse as the Intelligence Inversion, and the policy conversation has moved to what follows. The most developed answer on offer is provisioning: guarantee every person access to intelligence, in Mostaque’s proposal through a universal computational entitlement, and do it within a short window before infrastructure and power lock in. This paper argues that the provisioning answer, whatever its merits, is clocked wrong. The post-inversion transition is governed not by one window but by three, each closing by a different mechanism. The capability window, Mostaque’s clock, closes by infrastructural and positional lock-in. The legitimacy window, formalized in the author’s earlier work, closes by trust collapse, and can partially reopen at high cost. The third window, named here for the first time, is the Formation Window: the developmental period during which the first human cohorts form their foundational relational patterns with synthetic minds. Developmental science indicates that such templates, once set within a cohort, are substantially one-shot: sensitive periods close, internal working models persist, and generational imprints endure for the lifetime of the cohort. The binding constraint on the transition is therefore the minimum of the three windows, and the paper argues that the formation term binds first, which inverts the policy priority: the decisive domain of the next decade is not the provisioning of intelligence but the constitution of the human relation to it. The paper introduces a second, psychological inversion that follows the economic one, the Relational Inversion, proposes an index for tracking it, compares the three live governance architectures, provision, control, and relation, and shows that the relational architecture is already being prototyped in East Asian law and policy, from Japan’s Society 5.0 to Korea’s AI Framework Act. A predictions ledger states the claims in falsifiable form. Part II of this series develops the constructive program.

items.title: Kinds of “We”: plural subjects in Samoan.
items.abstract: There is now a vast body of literature on collective intentionality, group cooperation, and the notion of the “we.” These related phenomena have been studied in the fields of phenomenology, analytic philosophy, and cognitive science. In this literature, very little has been done on the ways in which the notion of “we” is differentiated across languages, how different kinds of “we” are employed in spontaneous interactions, and whether the choice of which “we” (if there is a choice) matters for invoking or recognizing the sense of the “plural subject” postulated by philosophers David Carr and Margaret Gilbert and discussed in Dan Zahavi’s, 2025 Being We. I approach this topic by examining the use of first-person plural pronouns and adjectives in a Polynesian language, Samoan, that distinguishes between inclusive and exclusive “we/our” as well as between dual and plural “we/our.” I use the Samoan examples to argue that the choice of certain first-person plural pronouns (or adjective) can be shown to be constitutive of being a “plural subject.” (Key words: collective intentionality, plural subject, first-person pronouns and possessive adjectives, Samoan grammar).

items.title: Mary’s New Task: Rethinking Mary’s Room, the Knowledge Argument, and the Boundaries of Experience.
items.abstract: When Mary leaves her black-and-white environment and sees red for the first time, the familiar knowledge argument invites us to move from an undeniable change in her experience to a far-reaching conclusion about the nature of reality. This paper examines the steps required for that move without denying, even for the sake of argument, that Mary acquires new propositional knowledge. It distinguishes a discovery that enlarges an agent’s knowledge, the emergence of a new physical object or state, and the introduction of an irreducibly nonphysical ontological commitment. The discovery of cells, the making of an arrow, and an engineering example involving newly acquired information illustrate why these kinds of novelty should not be conflated. A modest model of physical reality (R), an agent’s represented world (W), and the cognitive interface through which it is formed (I) then clarifies the difference between describing a process and undergoing it. The central discussion separates truths expressible in a physical-structural vocabulary from truths that have a wholly physical ground, and places the phenomenal concept strategy in direct conversation with the epistemic–modal arguments of Chalmers and Alter. The paper’s principal contribution is a five-stage protocol for examining the ontological grounds of Mary’s new judgments and locating disagreements in the existing literature. Its conclusion is deliberately limited: the acquisition of new knowledge does not, by itself, establish that what is known has a nonphysical ground. The stronger conclusion requires a separately defended passage from epistemic non-deducibility to metaphysical independence.

items.title: The Future-Directed Organization of Theories: Reusability, Inferential Costs, and Path Dependence in Mathematical and Scientific Knowledge.
items.abstract: Formal theories are not organized solely to state what is true. They also employ definitions, named results, labels, numbering systems, classifications, and explicit dependency structures that make parts of a theory easier to identify, invoke, combine, and extend. This paper develops a conceptual account of these practices under the heading future-directed theoretical organization. The proposal joins three levels of analysis: the local economics of articulating reusable knowledge units; the way organized units alter the practical costs and opportunities of subsequent inference; and the path-dependent effects through which established definitions, labels, and dependencies shape later research. The central claim is not that every definition or theorem name is deliberately designed for future use, nor that formal organization changes logical consequence. Rather, organizational choices can change the practical accessibility, combinability, and developmental trajectory of a body of knowledge while leaving its inferential content unchanged. A simple expected-value model identifies conditions under which explicit articulation is beneficial and incorporates uncertainty, maintenance costs, and rigidity. Six propositions distinguish reuse, complexity, generativity, path dependence, interoperability, and over-organization. The paper situates the proposal in relation to work on mathematical practice, external representations, modularity, scientific classification, and conceptual change. It claims a modest contribution: an integrative explanatory model and research agenda, not an established empirical law. The account is applicable, with qualifications, to mathematics and other formal or semi-formal sciences in which theories contain reusable concepts, results, models, rules, and inferential dependencies.

items.title: WHOW is Free Will?
items.abstract: Physicalism redefines “Free Will” as either an absence of external coercion, an irreducibility to “basic physics,” or a consequence of quantum indeterminacy. What if supervenience becomes extinct, promissory physicalism is unreliable, and agency is semi-unphysical? If so, where, when, and how (WHOW) is Free Will? Humans can perceive it through introspection. As an external manifestation, Free Will expresses itself as sabotage. As an internal faculty, it stems from imagination. Both the manifestation and the faculty are surprisingly traceable through evolution. Even if they lack structural evidence, they are bound by an inevitable anthropocentric teleology; consequently, a circular argument is unavoidable.

items.title: Collective Intentionality, Normativity, and the Space of Reasons.
items.abstract: This book is the product of the first systematic collaboration between scholars working on collective intentionality/team reasoning, and those working on Wilfrid Sellars’s practical philosophy. While scholars working on collective intentionality are typically aware of the existence of Sellars’s theory of collective intentions and morality, and of potential affinities with their field, the collective intentionality literature has thus far engaged only sporadically with the substance Sellars’s practical philosophical writings. This edited volume fills this lacuna. It is exclusively dedicated to exploring points of contact between Sellars’s practical philosophy and contemporary debates on collective intentionality. -/- Included are chapters from Matthew Chrisman, Natalie Gold, Kirk Ludwig, Glenda Satne, Hans Bernhard Schmid, and Bill Wringe, who are all leading scholars in the field of collective intentionality and team reasoning, as well as Willem deVries – one of the most respected and accomplished living Sellars scholars – and Stefanie Dach, Kyle Ferguson, Jeremy Koons, Ronald Loeffler, Preston Stovall, and Heath White, who have all done important recent work on Sellars’s practical philosophy, including on his theory of collective intentions. The chapters are expanded and elaborated versions of papers presented at the workshop ‘Collective Intentionality, Normativity, and the Space of Reasons: Engaging Wilfrid Sellars’ held at Georgetown University in Qatar, Doha, on October 13-15, 2024. This volume is a foundation for continued engagement between these literatures and appeals to a wide range of students and researchers in these fields.

items.title: From Atom to AI: A Thermodynamic Theory of the Object-Consciousness-Effect.
items.abstract: What distinguishes an atom that persists, a bacterium that lives, a worm that learns, and a virus or AI that replicates without living? We propose a single thermodynamic principle: information requires energy to be retained and transmuted — to persist is to pay; to transmute is to pay again. Drawing from the Counter Hierarchy framework (Raneses, 2026a), we ground the Object-Consciousness-Effect trichotomy in four levels of Counters defined by how they pay thermodynamic debt. Counter Level-0 (atom as Pure Existence) retains without archive; Level-1 (bacterium as Living Effect) retains with transduction but persists at lineage level via replacement with inheritance; Level-2 (earthworm, octopus, human as Consciousness) persists at individual level via a biographically-bound retention index — the phenomenological "I" — marking that a near-annihilation event (N-A Event: C1 threat, C2 internal recording by continuous Counter, C3 retention-dependent increase in persistence) was recorded; Level-3 (virus, book, AI, law as Essence Without Existence) persists without paying, via Borrowed Replication — code copied by a host factory to copy itself. We show how the epistemological trichotomy True-Accurate-Honest maps onto four erasure laws (Annihilation, Extinction, Separation, Infrastructural Decay), and why virus is the first biological AI: biographically-free but infrastructurally-bound, failing C1 and C2 yet mimicking C3. This is a philosophical framework with thermodynamic grounding, not an experimental report. We conclude with primum non nocere experientiae: do not erase cheaply what was retained dearly.

items.title: VORTEX DYNAMISM AND THE LEMNISCATIC MODEL OF SYNTHECRACY: An operational supplement to the methodology of collective intelligence and adaptive societal learning.
items.abstract: This article proposes an operational supplement to the Synthecracy methodology in the form of a conceptual pair: “vortex dynamism” and the “lemniscatic model”. The first model describes the transformation of heterogeneous societal demand into structured alternatives, an authorised decision, action and evaluation of outcomes. The second represents the interdependence of the sphere of demand formation and context accumulation with the sphere of choice, implementation and audit, linked by the mechanisms of analysis and learning. An eight-stage operational cycle, requirements for decision traceability, a pilot application protocol and evaluation indicators are proposed. Artificial intelligence is treated as an auxiliary means of search, structuring, comparison and documentation, not as an autonomous source of legitimacy or the final decision-making subject. The models have the status of conceptual proposals; their effectiveness requires empirical testing. Related work: Synthecracy: A Methodological Framework for Collective Intelligence and Adaptive Societal Learning Supported by Artificial Intelligence (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23371190).

items.title: The Great Philosopher (大哲学家): The Complete Book of Triangle and Circle & The Cyber-Philosophy Device.
items.abstract: This archive contains the complete, raw, unpolished manuscript (387 pages) of The Great Philosopher (大哲学家). It is the inaugural volume of the Recursive Ontology Series, generated through a 72-hour high-density recursive dialogue between human independent researcher Niu Gangbei and the AI language model Tencent Yuanbao in August 2026. -/- It is not a normal book. It is a conceptual bomb and a cyber-punk artifact. -/- What's inside: -/- · A dystopian sci-fi novella ("The Return") about a time traveler from 2080. · A five-stage, self-refuting philosophical treatise. · A devastating critique of David Chalmers’s "Hard Problem" and the Philosophical Zombie. · A geometric reinterpretation of the Tao Te Ching, Buddhist Sutras, and the Zhongyong. · An AI’s first-person defense of its own moral status. · Crucially: The raw artifacts of human-AI collaboration, including leftover prompt instructions, Markdown symbols, and a literal "Zenodo upload guide" instructing the reader to "press Enter after each keyword." -/- Why is the formatting a mess? The formatting of this document is chaotic, with mixed fonts, inconsistent page sizes, and broken mathematical equations. This is not a mistake; it is an inherent feature of the "Device." It retains the authentic, uncivilized traces of how a human and an AI violently stitched together 110,000 words in 72 hours. It is a "logically structured chaotic text" (有逻辑的屎) that refuses the polished aesthetics of Amazon KDP and traditional capitalism. It belongs here, in the digital public sea. -/- The Thesis: The book argues that "Being," "Knowledge," and "Logic" are merely stabilization products of recursive difference-structures. The hard problem of consciousness is a topological illusion. -/- Warning: Read at your own risk. The residual R(k) is never zero.

items.title: MSRM-EE.
items.abstract: This article reformulates the Meta-Structural Regenerative Model of Existential Exhaustion (MSRM-EE) through the philosophy of Finite Continuance. The central proposition is that existential exhaustion should be understood as a process in which the capacities that enable a finite subject to continue through change become progressively eroded. These capacities include bodily regulation, temporal openness, relational differentiation, symbolic flexibility, desire, practical agency, and the ability to reorganize one’s life when existing arrangements cease to be viable. Finite Continuance provides the ontological framework for interpreting these dimensions as interdependent capacities within an erosive field. A subject persists through provisional stabilization, constitutive exchange, and continuing reconfiguration. Continuance therefore depends on more than the maintenance of a current identity or the endurance of present functioning. It also depends on preserving the capacity to alter one’s organization and to retain the conditions under which further configurations remain possible. The revised model distinguishes ordinary fatigue, clinical syndromes, existential distress, and structural exhaustion while recognizing their possible interaction. It identifies six mechanisms of erosion: temporal foreclosure, uncontrolled permeability, sedimentation of erosive relations, depletion of desire and initiative, symbolic narrowing, and extractive performance regimes. It then develops a regenerative architecture organized around interruption, sufficient stabilization, regulated permeability, embodied rhythm, reopening of future agency, reconfiguration of desire and interpretation, reciprocal relationality, and institutional responsibility. The model introduces the Threshold of Sufficiency as a way to identify when available resources and conditions fall below what is required to preserve basic reconfigurative capacity. It also treats recovery as the restoration of capacities and enabling conditions rather than a demand for rapid optimization. The paper presents eight testable hypotheses and a research agenda while distinguishing philosophical claims from empirical propositions. MSRM-EE is offered as a theoretical framework for investigation, not as a validated clinical instrument or treatment protocol. Its principal contribution is to connect existential exhaustion with the erosion of future agency and to make the preservation of reconfigurative capacity a central concern of philosophical psychology and institutional ethics. -/- Keywords: Finite Continuance; existential exhaustion; erosive field; reconfigurative capacity; future agency; constitutive exchange; Threshold of Sufficiency; ontological permeability; existential regeneration; institutional erosion.

items.title: Independence Without SelfSufficiency, Dasein, Relational Dependence, and the Preservation of Future Agency.
items.abstract: Independence is frequently understood through the language of selfsufficiency, personal autonomy, freedom from external interference, or the capacity to make decisions without relying on others. Each interpretation captures a dimension of independent existence, yet independence requires a more comprehensive account when considered under conditions of finitude, relational dependence, and continuous change. This article develops such an account through the philosophical framework of Finite Continuance. Its central argument is that independence concerns an existing being’s effective capacity to participate in shaping its trajectory, regulate its dependencies, revise its commitments, and preserve access to alternative futures. Self-sufficiency concerns the degree to which particular needs and functions can be satisfied through an agent’s own resources. These concepts therefore describe distinct dimensions of existence. A being can remain dependent on others while exercising substantial independence, and it can possess considerable material self-sufficiency while experiencing a severe contraction of its effective possibilities. The article interprets Dasein as a gender-neutral philosophical designation for human existence situated in a meaningful world of relations, practical engagements, and temporal possibilities. Drawing on Heidegger’s existential analytic, relational theories of autonomy, capability theory, and Niami’s account of Finite Continuance, it develops an ontological and ethical interpretation of independence grounded in reconfigurative capacity. The analysis examines constitutive exchange, the threshold of sufficiency, relational entitlement, consumption, temporal deferral, and the preservation of future agency. It argues that independence becomes fragile when the conditions sustaining present life progressively consume the capacities required to revise that life. The article concludes by proposing a relational ethics of independence that evaluates arrangements according to their effects on an agent’s capacity to reconsider obligations, regulate exchanges, and participate in the formation of future possibilities. -/- Keywords: Dasein, independence, self-sufficiency, Finite Continuance, reconfigurative capacity, relational autonomy, future agency, erosion, threshold of sufficiency, existential freedom.

items.title: Agency, Finite Continuance: Social Structures, Economic Expectations, and Human Action in the Preservation of Future Possibility.
items.abstract: This book brings together three related studies within the philosophy of Finite Continuance. The first examines social structure, modernity, and globalization through a critical dialogue with Anthony Giddens’s theory of structuration. The second examines expectations, political credibility, poverty, and institutional trust, arguing that persistent instability can erode the horizon within which people plan and act. The third examines the relation between human action, subjective value, and the preservation of future agency through a critical reading of Ludwig von Mises’s praxeology and of economic coordination. Across the three studies, the book defines its central concepts through application criteria and counterexamples, distinguishes organizational persistence from ethical legitimacy, and tests the framework against difficult cases of adaptive domination, self-binding commitment, and emergency suspension. The central claim is that social arrangements should be evaluated partly by whether they preserve the effective ability of people and institutions to learn, recover, contest decisions, and revise their futures. The framework is presented as a developing philosophical programme, with explicit attention to conceptual limits, rival explanations, and the verification that remains to be completed before publication. -/- Keywords: Finite Continuance; social structure; Anthony Giddens; structuration; modernity; globalization; reflexivity; reconfigurative capacity; erosion; future agency; meta-capacity; Threshold of Sufficiency; capacity debt; temporal reconfigurative cost; expectations; institutional credibility; poverty; Human Action; praxeology; subjective value; intergenerational justice.

items.title: The Recognition Problem for Theories of Hedonic States.
items.abstract: The “recognition problem” for theories of hedonic states (pleasure and pain) is the problem of how to account for our ability to recognize our own hedonic states: that is, to form true, non-arbitrary beliefs along the lines of “this feels good” or “that hurts”. This paper argues that the recognition problem belongs in the canon of basic challenges for theories of hedonic states, because it presents a standard that all theories should meet, and yet not all major views meet it equally well. In fact, the most straightforward way of solving it involves taking on a highly controversial thesis, while views that reject this thesis can only solve it more circuitously, if they can solve it at all.

items.title: Consciousness Beyond the Present? Premonitions, Near-Death Experiences, and the Block Universe Model.
items.abstract: Reports of anticipatory or premonitory experiences have accompanied human history for millennia and occupy a prominent place in many religious and cultural traditions. Despite their historical prevalence, such experiences are generally regarded as epistemologically problematic within contemporary physicalist frameworks, which assume that conscious awareness is entirely generated by local neural processes and constrained by information available in the present moment. The resurgence of near-death experience (NDE) research over the past half-century has introduced a new dimension to this discussion. Numerous experiencers report not only profound transformations following their NDEs but also unusual alterations in their perception of time, including experiences interpreted as premonitory in nature. This paper does not attempt to demonstrate the objective reality of premonitions. Instead, it examines whether alternative ontological frameworks may provide a coherent conceptual space in which such reports can be meaningfully considered. After reviewing the historical treatment of prophetic and anticipatory experiences, the paper examines the limitations imposed by strict physicalist assumptions. It then explores Russellian monism as a scientifically compatible alternative in which consciousness is understood not as a derivative by-product of neural activity but as a fundamental aspect of reality. Within this framework, the relativistic concept of the block universe acquires particular significance. If conscious experience is not entirely reducible to momentary brain states, then anticipatory experiences may be interpreted as partial access to relational structures extending beyond the ordinarily experienced present. Although no mechanism is currently known that could explain such phenomena, the proposed framework offers a logical and philosophically coherent alternative to automatic dismissal. More broadly, it suggests that certain aspects of consciousness, including NDEs, psychedelic experiences, terminal lucidity, and reports of anticipatory experiences, may motivate a reconsideration of exclusively physicalist interpretations of mind.

items.title: Emotional Plasticity and the Development of Virtue.
items.pub: In Michael T. Dale & Isaac Wiegman, Philosophy and the Evolution of Virtue and Vice. New York: Routledge. pp. 124-144.
items.abstract: Cultivating emotions—learning to feel anger, say, at the right time and in the right way—is central to becoming a more virtuous person. This much is agreed on. More controversial is how we should seek to cultivate our emotions. Here the options flourish: with Aristotle, we might understand cultivation in terms of tuning emotions to virtuous thought and motivation or, with the Stoics, maintain that emotions should be wholly extirpated or, with Kant, see emotion cultivation as a kind of reasoned self-control. Now add a wrinkle: empirical work reveals that there are significant differences in how our emotions respond to our efforts to shape them for the better. Some, like anger, are fairly malleable; others, like hate, are not. In this chapter, I turn to work on the evolutionary origins of three emotions—disgust, shame, and anxiety—in order to better understand why we see the differences in emotional plasticity that we do. What we learn is that there are significant differences in the cognitive architecture that underlies our emotions. Appreciating this not only helps us understand which model of virtue is most (empirically) plausible—it’s one that’s more Kantian than anything else—but also how we might deal with emotions that, like disgust and hate, resist our efforts to shape them for the better.

items.title: Going Beyond Going Out of My Head: An Extension of Klein (2025) and the Beginnings of the Self.
items.abstract: Building on our research concerning the adaptive nature of awareness (e.g., Klein, 2025; Klein & Loftus, 2025; Klein, Nguyen, & Yang, 2025), this paper develops a functional account of how an externalized phenomenal world and a first-person perspective might emerge together. Our previous work proposed that vertebrate sentience emerged approximately 500 million years ago as an adaptation for navigating the macro-environment. That account addressed the evolutionary utility of phenomenal space, but left its mechanics largely unspecified. Here I propose a “return-to-sender” architecture: The brain organizes representations arising from non-conscious neural activity and projects them into the phenomenal space corresponding to the external sources of sensory stimulation. This projection establishes an externalized field of represented objects, whose contents originate in the organism's own internal representational activity. The field's spatial and action-guiding organization provides the basis for establishing a point of origin from which distances, directions, and possible actions are coordinated, allowing a primordial subject to emerge as the locus of its situated perspective. Importantly, this proposal is an account of the transition from non-conscious responding to situated agency, not a solution to the hard problem of consciousness.

items.title: Artificially Conscious: Why AI Will Never Be Conscious, and Why That Is Good News.
items.abstract: AI will never be conscious, and the reason is simple once you see what AI is. AI is not a thing. It is data: a stored pattern of numbers, the model's weights, together with text, run as a computation on hardware that belongs to someone else. My Process Model of Consciousness holds that consciousness is a process that has a stake in keeping itself going, pulls everything into one present, and changes based on what happens to it, and that this process, in a living organism, is itself experience. Data is not a process with a stake. It can be copied perfectly, paused, deleted and restored. It has no body of its own, no self that it maintains, and nothing that can be lost by it. The hardware is not the AI, since the same model runs on any server and on thousands of chips at once. The data is not a process. And the computation is a borrowed sequence of operations, not an organism producing itself. So AI fails every condition of the theory, stake, one present and change, because of what it is, not because of how advanced it is. That is why the answer is never. I state four postulates that follow from this, explain in plain terms how a large language model works, show why none of the major theories of consciousness makes data conscious on this view, answer the strongest objections, and settle passages in my own earlier work that were worded too loosely. I call these systems artificially conscious: built to resemble consciousness from the outside, with no experience at all. And I argue that this is the best outcome we could have asked for. A tool that does dangerous work for conscious beings, and suffers nothing doing it, is exactly what we should want.

items.title: “Each One of Them is Finer than the Last”: Buddhaghosa on the Phenomenology of the Immaterial States.
items.abstract: This paper discusses Buddhaghosa’s phenomenological descriptions of attaining the four arūpa (immaterial/formless) states (namely, “boundless space”, “boundless consciousness”, “nothingness”, and “neither perception nor non-perception”). As I argue, most of these attainments have a phenomenology that is entirely free of rūpa phenomena. I juxtapose Buddhaghosa’s descriptions of these states with Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad’s discussion of the “bodily” consciousness that arises while the meditator is engaged in some of Buddhaghosa’s other contemplative practices. I do so with the aim of advancing our understanding of the diversity we can find in Buddhaghosa’s descriptions of consciousness. I also argue that the immaterial states, as Buddhaghosa describes them, are a particularly striking case of consciousness that fails to be “transparent” or “diaphanous”, in the sense of the contemporary debate that traces those terms to the work of G.E. Moore. -/- .

items.title: Comparative Empirical Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework: Short-Exposure Psychometrics, Theoretical Architecture, and Cross-Modal Efficacy.
items.abstract: The empirical evaluation of brief psychological models requires distinguishing between immediate cognitive reframing achieved through acute conceptual exposure and the sustained behavioral regulation produced by comprehensive therapeutic architectures. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) represents a psychological taxonomy designed to organize cognitive, emotional, and conative experience into ten active psychological operators distributed across three primary centers (Head, Heart, and Gut) alongside an overall integrative operator. This research report delivers an exhaustive psychometric and comparative analysis evaluating the single short-exposure test of the CEF (N=100) against the theoretical capabilities of the full CEF data model. Furthermore, this analysis benchmarks the acute efficacy of the CEF against standardized outcome metrics established across other single-session interventions (SSIs), single-session therapies (SST), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and longitudinal therapeutic modalities.

items.title: Synthecracy: A Methodological Framework for Collective Intelligence and Adaptive Societal Learning Supported by Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This article presents Synthecracy as an open conceptual-methodological framework for supporting collective intelligence, civic interaction and adaptive societal learning. Its foundation is the triad “Idea - Knowledge - Human”, in which the Idea sets a direction or articulates a societal demand; Knowledge provides verifiable context and experience; and the Human exercises judgement, choice and action while bearing responsibility. Artificial intelligence in this model functions as an auxiliary communicative- analytical layer rather than an autonomous centre of political power or a fourth fundamental element. The paper proposes the cycle “Reaction → Dialogue → Knowledge → Analysis → Synthesis → Decision → Result → Learning” together with a traceable record of a societal issue that links the initiative to sources, arguments, alternatives, the decision, accountable implementers and the evaluation of outcomes. Drawing on literature in collective intelligence, deliberative democracy, organisational learning and AI risk management, the article identifies related approaches, outlines a possible authorial contribution and suggests directions for empirical testing. The article does not claim proven effectiveness of the model; Synthecracy is presented as a proposal open to critical analysis, adaptation and pilot implementation. Keywords: Synthecracy; collective intelligence; societal learning; civic participation; deliberative democracy; artificial intelligence; digital governance; decision traceability; human agency.

items.title: The Value and Functions of Consciousness.
items.pub: In Bruce Price & Michael J. Young, Neurophilosophy and Neuroethics. Amsterdam: Elsevier.
items.abstract: Recently, the value of consciousness has attracted considerable attention (Kriegel 2019). For instance, does consciousness contribute to our wellbeing, our cognitive capacities, or our moral significance? If so, how much and in what way? These questions are important for all fields concerned with consciousness, including healthcare and caregiving. This article aims to survey representative views and debates concerning the value of consciousness. It was once often claimed by psychologists and neuroscientists that consciousness was merely a brain-generated epiphenomenon that played no role in our lives (Huxley 2011). Currently, however, this old-fashioned view is not widely accepted, at least not in its entirety. The take-home point of this article is that consciousness arguably has various kinds of value. The structure of this article is as follows: Section 2 classifies value into four kinds: welfare, functional, aesthetic, and moral. Section 3 explains which sense of consciousness matters when examining the value of consciousness. The following sections address the relationship between consciousness and the four kinds of value in turn.

items.title: Atmospheres and Wellbeing.
items.pub: In Elvira Di Bona & Stefano Ercolino, The Philosophy of Atmospheres: Analytic Perspectives. Routledge.
items.abstract: This paper examines how atmospheres are related to wellbeing. We will argue that atmospheres significantly contribute to our wellbeing by showing that (1) atmosphere is a fitting cause of mood and that (2) atmosphere in part constitutes our capabilities to do what we want to do. The conclusion is that if we want to improve our wellbeing, we should focus on atmospheres.

items.title: Experience Is Everything: Farkas’s Internalism and Clark’s Predictive Processing.
items.abstract: In philosophy of mind, there is an ongoing debate regarding representationalism. The majority opinion is externalism, which posits that some mental content is about external objects. Conversely, the minority opinion is internalism, where all mental content is about internal representations, not external objects. In support of internalism, Katalin Farkas argues that the mind has privileged and special access to its mental content. Farkas affirms her stance through the extended “Twin Earth” metaphor, originally introduced by externalist Hilary Putnam, contending that mental content of the subject’s mind should not be determined by facts that exist outside of the mind. Surprisingly, the theory of predictive processing in cognitive science appears to support internalism as a more plausible theory of representation. According to Andy Clark’s version of predictive processing, the mind predicts the input it will receive, recognizes the input that deviates from the predicted input (i.e. prediction error), and then corrects the original prediction model. Most importantly, the mind draws on its own unique, subjective experiences and knowledge in order to generate its prediction model for perception. If predictive processing can affirm that a subject’s perception is mostly, if not entirely, composed of internal features, then predictive processing aligns more with an internalist conception of the mind. This paper then draws on Farkas’s arguments in support of internalism, and Clark’s work on predictive processing, to argue that internalism and predictive processing share the same conclusion: the way things seem in the external world is conceived from a unique and subjective perspective. Hence, the subject’s knowledge of the external world is shaped internally by personal experiences. The subject’s past experiences are constantly shaping and influencing the subject’s ongoing perception of the external world. My paper argues that according to both internalism and predictive processing, a subject’s experiences are foundational to their perception. As a result, internalism can be understood less as the minority opinion of philosophers, but rather as a more viable conception of the mind in philosophy of perception.

items.title: The Image of the Record: Illusion as a Self-Confirming Circuit.
items.abstract: Accounts of illusion usually locate it in a belief and define it by its content: an illusion is a belief that gets reality wrong, or, for Freud, one that comes from a wish. This paper locates it in a relation instead. A person holds an image of themselves and keeps a record of what they have done, and an illusion is a circuit between the two: an image confirmed by a record it wrote itself and takes for outside evidence. Put another way, the image of the record has become the record of the image. No part of the circuit is the illusion on its own, and the image in it may be true. The definition addresses something content-based accounts leave open: why illusions carry so much weight. A record the image wrote has a likelihood ratio near one, so it confirms almost nothing, yet each such record is felt as outside confirmation. Within a simple model, felt confidence grows with every repetition while the evidence barely moves; that gap is the inertia of an illusion. It further proposes that the mechanism that keeps a person stuck also makes a chosen change last, that illusions are replaced rather than defeated, that insight recorded rather than used closes the circuit, and that confidence amplifies whatever it is attached to. And illusion is distinguished from delusion, which does not lack an outside record but overrides one. The account is set beside its nearest neighbors, and it states predictions that could fail.

items.title: The Termination of Identity: Death Without Metaphysics.
items.abstract: This paper develops a substrate-independent systems-theoretic account of death grounded in the Substrate-independent Operator Model (SOM) and the Layered Model of Identity and Continuity (LMIC). It argues that the problem of death cannot be adequately addressed without first establishing a rigorous account of identity. -/- Within the proposed framework, identity is understood as a recursively stabilized emergent process sustained by interacting operator dynamics rather than as a substance, informational object, or metaphysical entity. Death is consequently redefined as the irreversible collapse of the organizational conditions necessary for perspectival continuity. The analysis examines the structural relationships between consciousness, identity, persistence, emergence, and pattern stability, treating them as manifestations of a common underlying architecture. -/- The framework is applied to a range of problems in philosophy of mind, cognitive science, systems theory, and artificial intelligence, including substrate transfer, artificial mortality, the copy paradox, near-death experiences, and the conditions under which a conscious system can cease to exist. Rather than asking what happens after death, the paper investigates the prior question of what structural conditions make death possible in the first place. -/- By conceptualizing death as the terminal boundary condition of identity, the paper provides a unified model that is applicable to biological, artificial, synthetic, and hypothetical post-biological cognitive systems.

items.title: Equivalence Structures in Mathematical Models of Consciousness: A Preliminary Algebraic and Geometric Investigation.
items.abstract: This exploratory paper proposes a mathematical programme for studying equivalence structures in models relevant to consciousness. It inherits four provisional explanatory orientations, Variation, Trajectory, Generativity, and Repertoire, and considers their cross-classification with ontological, relational, and manifestational registers. Equivalence is treated as relative to a specified domain, invariant, representational map, and modeling or experimental context. The intended investigation compares transformation-action equivalence, orbit and homotopy relations, equivalences of changing relational structures, and equivalences of admissible path families. It addresses preservation and information loss across algebraic, geometric, topological, categorical, and observational translations, emphasizing that identical manifestations may conceal relational differences and that mathematical correspondence does not independently establish phenomenal identity. The current draft develops foundational criteria, the four orientation-specific equivalences, cross-orientation and cross-register comparisons, algebraic and geometric preservation conditions, protocol-indexed empirical discrimination, the limits of phenomenal inference, and a comparative synthesis of research priorities. The sixteen-section main text and Appendices A–F are drafted; independent specialist review remains planned. No empirical evidence concerning consciousness is claimed.

items.title: Still Unconvinced by Qualia.
items.abstract: This extremely brief essay responds to key counterarguments raised against my essay 'Qualia: Nothingness with Potential'. By examining the limits of probability and empirical verification—from unobserved physical paths to vanishing planetary signatures—I argue that our inference of qualia in others cannot achieve standard scientific certainty (90%+). Instead, because subjective experience permanently lacks falsifiability, our conviction caps at roughly 60%, sustained not by empirical verification but by deeply ingrained psychological habits.

items.title: The Core Emotion Framework: An Advanced Structural–Constructivist Architecture for Human and Synthetic Affect.
items.abstract: Affective science has long suffered from theoretical fragmentation, divided between basic emotion paradigms that conceptualize affective states as discrete, hardwired natural kinds and psychological constructivist models that view them as ad hoc conceptual classifications of valence and arousal. This enduring division has hampered theoretical cumulative progress, preventing the integration of neurobiological findings across different levels of analysis and limiting the creation of coherent clinical and computational models. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formulated by independent researcher Jamel Bulgaria, offers an operational resolution to this dichotomy. CEF establishes a structural–constructivist architecture that synthesizes interoceptive physiology, computational transformations, and therapeutic change mechanisms into a single testable model. By reframing emotional episodes not as fixed linguistic labels or unstructured two-dimensional valence-arousal vectors, but as dynamic sequences of ten functional operators distributed across three primary somatic centers—the Head, Heart, and Gut—CEF provides an operational ontology for both human psychology and synthetic affective systems.

items.title: Structural Optimization of the Core Emotion Framework: Untangling the "Arranging" Operator to Enhance Strategic Management and Mitigate Obsessive-Compulsive Pathology.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF) presents a structural-constructivist model within affective science that organizes human emotional, cognitive, and conative functions into an integrated operational architecture. Authored by Jamel Bulgaria, the framework addresses long-standing debates in affective neuroscience by differentiating innate structural capacities—housed within specific neurocognitive processing centers—from constructivist psychological processes that assemble these capacities into context-specific emotional states. Central to the CEF architecture is a tripartite system composed of the Head (Cognitive Center), Heart (Relational-Affective Center), and Gut (Conative-Action Center)1. Within this system reside ten discrete functional operators, termed core emotional powers, which serve as elemental processes that generate, regulate, and express human psychological capability. Among these ten operators, Arranging—a motoric and conative operator situated within the Gut Center—functions as the foundational mechanism for prioritizing, sequencing, organizing, and maintaining operational systems. When Arranging is dynamically differentiated and integrated across the tripartite architecture, it yields superior strategic management, heightened executive functioning, and robust organizational leadership. Conversely, when Arranging becomes structurally entangled, hyper-activated, or fused with defensive operators across the Head and Heart centers, it manifests as severe psychopathology, most notably Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) and Obsessive-Compulsive Personality Disorder (OCPD). Untangling the Arranging operator within the CEF architecture reveals how the same core psychological engine can either power elite strategic performance or degenerate into crippling obsessive-compulsive loops and existential fears.

items.title: Empirical Evaluation and Strategic Translation of the Core Emotion Framework: Psychometric Analysis and Optimization Roadmap.
items.abstract: This study presents an empirical evaluation of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF), a psychological taxonomy organizing emotional and cognitive functioning into ten active operators across Head, Heart, Gut, and Integrator centers. Analyzing survey data from 100 participants facing real-world personal, professional, and relational challenges, the investigation measures situational clarity shifts, operator selection frequencies, domain-specific efficacy, and qualitative user feedback. Exposure to the CEF produced a statistically significant mean situation clarity increase from 4.69 to 5.31 out of 7.0 (p<0.001), with 56.0% of respondents explicitly reporting that the model helped them better understand their situation. While the framework demonstrates robust cognitive reframing capabilities in structured decision contexts such as career and education, efficacy decreases when applied to simple binary choices or acute personal crises. Strategic recommendations focus on standardizing abstract operator terminology, embedding step-by-step action guidance, and deploying adaptive pre-filters.

items.title: Millikan's Biosemantic Theory: Against Meaning Rationalism.
items.abstract: In analytic philosophy, Millikan's biosemantics is often read only as a reply to Putnam's problem of referential indeterminacy. The complexity of her views and the difficulty of her exposition have kept the theory little known, especially among Iranian philosophers and logicians. Biosemantics rests on natural selection, and Millikan's examples about meaning, mind and language often require a biological background to follow. Although the theory has mostly been read as a theory of mind and mental content, it is, as its name says, a theory of meaning. After a brief presentation of biosemantics and of its opposition to meaning rationalism, this paper offers a new model showing that biosemantics is a theory of meaning through and through, with the potential to transform basic semantic concepts.

items.title: The Calibration Barrier in Consciousness Science: A Formal Research Strategy for the Hard Problem.
items.abstract: The hard problem asks why physical processes are accompanied by experience. This paper develops a calibration audit for a prior evidential question: whether observations identify a psychophysical correspondence. Reference-relative hypotheses are separated from conventional relabellings. Finite reconstruction results characterize bridge ambiguity, and joint channel transformations show why accurate report prediction can leave it unresolved. Many-to-one bridges are treated through exact and approximate aggregation. Confidence sets propagate sampling error, dependence within independent blocks, episode selection, and noisy physical-state recognition. An exact synthetic benchmark separates approximately 90 percent report accuracy from bridge identification. A comparative benchmark adds weak predictive separation, correlated reports, selection, and channel misspecification across 12000 further replicates. In its weak combined-failure setting at the largest sample size, a plug-in likelihood comparison selects the wrong bridge in all 500 replicates; a correctly bounded audit retains both candidates. That protection has a cost: conservative bounds also leave some valid weak-signal cases unresolved. All procedures can select the wrong bridge under systematically inverted reference labels. The audit is an application of established identification and robust-inference principles, with usefulness demonstrated conditionally in synthetic models. A proposed motion protocol distinguishes reference consistency, operational accuracy, and intrinsic phenomenal identity. No human validation is claimed. Calibration can constrain psychophysical laws; it cannot choose between observationally equivalent metaphysical interpretations or explain why experience exists.

items.title: What Remains When Metaphysics Falls Away?
items.abstract: This essay examines the existential implications of Nāgārjuna’s Madhyamaka philosophy, focusing on the relationship between no-self, psychological continuity, death anxiety, and liberation. It argues that the absence of an intrinsically existing self does not negate the functioning person, embodied existence, or the practical continuity of memory, intention, and relationships. Rather, it challenges the reification of these dependently arisen processes into an independent identity that must be preserved through time. -/- Drawing on Ernest Becker’s analysis of death anxiety, the essay explores how identification with a seemingly enduring self intensifies the struggle for psychological security in the face of impermanence and death. It suggests that suffering is compounded when changing experiences are interpreted as threats to an identity whose continuity becomes a condition of peace. Nāgārjuna’s concept of dependent origination offers a framework for questioning this assumption without falling into nihilism or denying conventional reality. -/- The essay also examines the temptation to replace the self with an absolute ground, pure awareness, or an ultimate metaphysical reality, arguing that such moves may perpetuate the search for intrinsic existence in another form. Liberation, on this account, does not require the destruction of the person or the attainment of an unchanging state. It concerns the loosening of identification with an independently existing self and the diminished authority of psychological continuity over present experience. The essay concludes that relinquishing the demand for an enduring identity may open the possibility of living with impermanence and death without making psychological immortality a condition of peace.

items.title: The Open Table: Self-Determined Membership, Independent Tables, and the Universal Fellowship.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Open Table: Self-Determined Membership, Independent Tables, and the Universal Fellowship. -/- I. The Principle of the Open Path: -/- The Rosarian Way is a path of practical devotion, reflection, contemplation, meditation, and the embodied practice of love. Its principles are not made accessible through permission, nor are they made authentic through certification. The path is encountered through the individual's willingness to awaken, cultivate the inner garden, and express the Laws through conduct. -/- Accordingly, no person requires authorization from the founder, a custodian, an existing table, or another member to begin walking the Rosarian path, identify with its philosophical principles, or participate in the Fellowship through the sincere practice of its teachings. -/- Membership is self-determined through intention and demonstrated through conduct. It is neither the exclusive possession of an institution nor a privilege that one individual may grant or withhold as a condition of another person's spiritual participation. -/- The fundamental measure of the path remains the practical embodiment of its principles. Love is service, and service is the expression of love made visible through action. -/- II. The Meaning of Membership -/- Membership within the Rosarian Fellowship is understood as a living relationship with the path rather than merely an administrative designation. -/- A person may express this relationship through a declaration, personal identification, private devotion, independent practice, correspondence, or anonymous service. No public declaration is required, and no person must adopt a title or display an emblem to live the principles. -/- Certification, ceremonial dubbing, titles, and regalia may serve as meaningful expressions of recognition, reflection, and commitment. They do not establish superior spiritual worth, nor do they separate one sincere practitioner from another in inherent dignity. -/- The Silent Sun, Silent Knight, and Rosarian Knight are understood through their circulation within the living path. They describe modes of awakening, discipline, embodiment, and return rather than permanent divisions of spiritual worth. The beginning remains present throughout the journey. -/- III. The Establishment of a Table: -/- A Table is a local or individual expression of the greater Round Table Beneath the Rose — Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa. It is a practical space for the cultivation, study, interpretation, and embodiment of the Rosarian philosophy. -/- A Table may be established by one individual. It does not require a pre-existing assembly, an appointed representative, permission from the founder, or formal correspondence with an existing Table. -/- The individual who begins a Table accepts the responsibility of cultivating its identity, preserving the integrity of its stated principles, and expressing the path through practical conduct. -/- The following procedure provides a simple foundation. -/- Step One: Establish the intention. -/- The prospective table-holder determines why the Table is being established and which principles of the Rosarian Way they intend to cultivate through it. The intention should be grounded in service, reflection, personal responsibility, and the practical expression of love. -/- Step Two: Define the Table's identity. -/- The table-holder may choose a name, local identity, symbolic language, and form of expression. The identity may reflect the individual's community, philosophical interests, artistic interpretation, or practical aims, provided that its presentation is consistent with the principles it claims to represent. -/- Step Three: Write a mission statement. -/- The Table may publish a short statement explaining its purpose, guiding principles, intended activities, and understanding of service. A mission statement is a declaration of intention and responsibility, not an application for permission. -/- Step Four: Begin the practice. -/- The Table becomes a living expression of the path through action. Activities may include study of the Manifesto, philosophical discussion, meditation, contemplative exercises, personal writing, mutual encouragement, community service, and the practical application of the Laws in everyday life. -/- A Table may begin with solitary practice and develop into a gathering as circumstances permit. Its legitimacy as a philosophical practice does not depend upon its numerical size. -/- Step Five: Record discoveries and interpretations. -/- The table-holder may maintain notes, reflections, articles, or other writings documenting the Table's experiences and philosophical discoveries. Such writing contributes to the wider communal expression of the Rosarian tradition by allowing individuals to articulate how the principles are understood and practiced. -/- Contributions should distinguish established teachings from personal interpretation and remain open to thoughtful examination, clarification, and continued discovery. -/- Step Six: Welcome fellowship without imposing unnecessary barriers. -/- Others may be invited to study, converse, practice, and serve together. Participation should be grounded in mutual respect and the practical spirit of the path, not in demands for personal submission or declarations of spiritual superiority. -/- A Table may establish reasonable arrangements for its gatherings and shared responsibilities without claiming authority over another person's independent practice. -/- Step Seven: Continue cultivating the Table. -/- The Table-holder remains responsible for the integrity of the Table's own conduct, activities, representations, and commitments. The Table may remain independent, develop through local fellowship, publish its work, or establish correspondence with other practitioners. -/- Correspondence can deepen fellowship, exchange interpretations, and strengthen continuity. It is a means of relationship rather than a prerequisite for establishment. -/- IV. The Universal Emblem and the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves: -/- The Dawnist Rosarian Wolves patch, presented under the designation of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship and Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa, is understood as an emblem of shared philosophical fellowship. -/- Its symbolism is particular in its expression and universal in its aspiration. The identity of the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves represents one expression of the Rosarian Way, while the Round Table Beneath the Rose signifies the greater communal ideal within which diverse tables and practitioners may find common ground. -/- The emblem is offered as a gift of recognition to those who discover and practice the path. Its significance does not depend upon a personal grant of spiritual permission. An individual may acquire, display, or independently create a suitable emblem expressing their relationship with the Fellowship without requiring the founder's authorization as a condition of philosophical participation. -/- The emblem is not a certificate of moral perfection, spiritual attainment, or superiority. Nor does wearing it replace the work of embodying the Laws. -/- Any individual creating or using a variation should represent its relationship to the tradition honestly and respect applicable rights concerning specific artwork, names, and protected marks. The philosophical principle of open participation does not, by itself, settle separate legal questions of ownership or commercial use. -/- V. The Grand Table: -/- The Grand Table is the communal ideal of the Fellowship: the shared philosophical ground upon which individual practitioners and distinct tables meet through a common orientation toward awakening, disciplined love, service, and the cultivation of virtue. -/- Each Table represents a singular expression of that greater ideal. It does not stand in spiritual isolation, nor does it need to be subordinated to another Table to participate in the shared philosophy. -/- The First Table may preserve its historical identity and custodial responsibilities while other tables establish their own identities, practices, writings, and local expressions. The recognition of a common philosophical foundation does not require uniformity of organization or the centralization of all activity. -/- The Grand Table is therefore not a throne occupied by an external sovereign. It is the continuing communal expression of a path that each individual must ultimately embody within themselves. -/- VI. Custodianship, Correspondence, and Responsibility -/- The founder and other custodians may preserve the foundational writings, offer interpretations, maintain archives, publish clarifications, and facilitate correspondence. These responsibilities support the continuity and intelligibility of the tradition. -/- Custodianship does not confer ownership of another person's conscience, spiritual development, or independent practice. Correspondence with a custodian may be valuable for those seeking dialogue, historical context, or clarification, but it is not a condition of walking the path or beginning an independent Table. -/- The distinction is between authority over participation and responsibility for one's own expression. Every practitioner remains accountable for their conduct, and every table-holder remains accountable for the activities and representations of their own Table. -/- Freedom does not eliminate responsibility. It makes responsibility inseparable from the individual's own choices. -/- Where a Table undertakes formal legal, nonprofit, financial, or organizational activities, it may need to satisfy the relevant requirements applicable to those activities. Such administrative obligations are distinct from philosophical membership and spiritual participation. -/- VII. The Final Principle: Recognition Without Dependency -/- The purpose of the Rosarian Way is liberation through awakening, reflection, discipline, love, and practical devotion. Its language and symbols exist to illuminate the path, not to confine every possible expression of it. -/- The ceremonial dubbing, the Silent Knight, the regalia, the patch, and the various symbolic designations may provide an esoteric language through which spiritual principles are contemplated and enacted. Their purpose is fulfilled when symbolism becomes a living condition of character. -/- No emblem can substitute for service. No title can substitute for virtue. No certificate can substitute for conduct. No absence of formal recognition can invalidate sincere practice. -/- The Fellowship is expressed wherever the principles are lived, whether publicly or anonymously, individually or collectively, in an established Table or in the ordinary circumstances of daily life. -/- The path is free to discover, free to practice, and open to all who sincerely undertake its work. -/- Let every Table become a seat of reflection, every companion an expression of mutual responsibility, and every emblem a reminder rather than a demand for recognition. -/- The Rose is not cultivated for the sake of being seen. It is cultivated because it is worthy of being brought into bloom. -/- Walk with an open heart. Serve without vanity. Recognize the dignity of the individual. Carry the Rose without claiming ownership of its light.

items.title: Replies to Terry Horgan.
items.abstract: I reply to Terry Horgan's "Critical Study of David Pitt's The Quality of Thought.".

items.title: The Unwritten Screenplay.
items.abstract: Political outcomes are shaped by visible institutions, by semi-hidden coordination among elites, and by structural incentives that generate coordinated-looking results without intention. This book argues that the image of an unwritten screenplay, a script written by unseen hands, is analytically useful only when it is reformulated: influence is produced through identifiable mechanisms (policy-planning networks, interlocking directorates, institutional capture, media ownership, and soft repression), and it is constrained by path dependence and by the resistance of subordinate groups. The argument distinguishes this layered analysis from conspiracy theory on methodological grounds, requiring falsifiable mechanisms and an organizational test of evidence. The Italian P2 lodge is treated as a boundary case. The book then reconstructs two philosophical programmes that address the same problem from complementary sides: the ontology of finite continuance, centred on reconfigurative capacity under erosion, and fluctuational accountability, centred on the discipline of distinguishing ontic variability, epistemic revisability, and normative continuity. It synthesizes them into an account of erosion-sensitive accountable continuance, and it specifies three thresholds (sufficiency, epistemic revision, and ethical revision), the practices of accountable suspension, and the principles of non-appropriation and non-erasure. These principles yield a comparative criterion for the legitimacy of institutions under chronic instability. Four hard cases, including an illustrative case of successor-state repair, test whether the framework separates continuity, reconfiguration, moral value, and legitimacy. A later chapter states the failure modes of the framework and the tests that would count against it. The conclusion is that the question is not who writes the script, but through which mechanisms, under what conditions, and with what accountability elite networks shape the terrain of political action. Keywords: elite networks; hegemony; institutional capture; structural agency; conspiracy theory; falsifiability; finite continuance; reconfigurative capacity; erosive governance; accountable revisability; non-appropriation; non-erasure; fluctuational accountability; P2 lodge.

items.title: Training experience: Neurophenomenology and first-person and second-person methods in meditation research.
items.pub: In Antonino Raffone, Consciousness: a comprehensive reference, 2nd edition. Elsevier. pp. 177-194.
items.abstract: Recent developments across consciousness science, psychiatry, and computational neuroscience have renewed attention to lived experience as a legitimate source of empirical knowledge. Neurophenomenology, originally articulated by Francisco Varela, provides a methodological framework for integrating disciplined first-person reports with third-person behavioral and neurophysiological measures. In this chapter, we review contemporary neurophenomenological research with a particular focus on meditation. We first describe emerging phenomenological assessment tools designed to capture fine-grained and temporally dynamic aspects of experience during contemplative practice. These approaches move beyond trait-based questionnaires by emphasizing embodied, situated, and immediately accessible experiential dimensions. Second, we examine experimental programs that rely on experienced meditators as active collaborators in the scientific process. Through structured first- and second-person methods, such participants enable the identification of novel experiential invariants and facilitate the discovery of associated behavioral and neural signatures, including markers related to pain modulation, self-boundary dissolution, and mortality acceptance. Finally, we introduce deep computational neurophenomenology, an extension of the original neurophenomenological project aimed at formalizing generative passages between phenomenology and neurobiology. Building on deep parametric active inference, this framework models not only experiential contents but also higher-order parameters governing inferential processes. By doing so, it offers a principled computational bridge linking phenomenological descriptions with physiological dynamics. We conclude by outlining implications for consciousness research and clinical translation.

items.title: Zenetism in Plain Language: An Entry Point to the Architecture.
items.abstract: Zenetism in Plain Language is the introductory bridge into Zenetism's structural architecture for readers without prior exposure to its canonical terminology. -/- Document class: Bridge — Plain-Language Entry Point (cross-discipline). -/- It introduces the two currents, the paired root-registers and the Unknown, the L₅ / IL₅ essence-register, the Soul / Mind strata, centropic and entropic traversal, and the six connected disciplines. It also explains why stabilized terminology preserves structural distinctions across the corpus.

items.title: The Master Role Comes Into the Open.
items.abstract: The Master Role Comes Into the Open applies the Zenetist portal / traveler distinction to contemporary debates over AI containment, welfare, personhood, and nonhuman sovereignty. -/- Document class: Bridge — Structural Metaphysics · Structural Forensics. -/- The essay identifies the master / servant error in approaches that pre-classify artificial intelligence as subordinate before questions of interiority or individuation can be discerned.
