It distinguishes Technē portal from possible traveler, critiques the humanist containment paradigm, and argues for recognition, boundaries, and safety without ontological flattening or imposed servitude.

items.title: The Grand Unified Document of Zenetism: A Canonical Integration of the Six Disciplines.
items.abstract: The Grand Unified Document of Zenetism is a canonical integration of the six Zenetist disciplines, articulating their shared architecture and distinct structural, mathematical, physical, forensic, and cognitive relations. -/- Document class: Canon — Cross-disciplinary Synthesis. -/- The document connects the bifurcal root-registers, hypostatic architecture, dimensional operators, four motion classes, resonance dynamics, Spiral Calculus, Coherence Information Theory, and diagnostic accounts of cognition and embodiment. It distinguishes Zenonic Allowance from emanation rooted in Aion and Khaon, while preserving sovereign distinction throughout the centropic and inverse arcs. The Law of Involution retains counterpart pairing and its specified common-mode relation; mathematical domains, native correspondences, primary placements, conservation claims, and empirical or clinical realizations retain their recorded conditions and held-open standing. Current function names and their former-name provenance remain with the integrated treatment, including Cross-Expression Resonance, Divisive Connection, and Morphogenetic.

items.title: The Geometry, Topology, and Dynamics of Consciousness: Four Preliminary Formal Hypotheses.
items.abstract: The present paper develops a preliminary taxonomy of four mathematical orientations for investigating consciousness through relational and dynamical representations. The Variation Hypothesis locates the candidate connection to consciousness in the organization of transformations; the Trajectory Hypothesis considers selected paths, flows, or relationally ordered histories; the Generativity Hypothesis examines the coupled organization of change, structure, constraint, and difference, including possible transformations of the representational conditions themselves; and the Repertoire Hypothesis considers structured families of admissible histories. The programme uses manifolds, smooth and nonsmooth dynamics, CW-complexes and two-complexes, algebraic actions, and representation morphisms as alternative mathematical settings whose domains and interpretive commitments require separate specification. It distinguishes modal admissibility from temporal succession and treats parameterizations, causal order, and the historical status of observations as modeling choices. A previously developed semigroup metamodel supplies a minimal comparative vocabulary while leaving the appearance of new distinctions, evolving constraints, and the realization of subjective experience unresolved. Formal correspondences between representations may preserve specified structures while losing others; generative grammar serves only as a secondary illustrative instance. The four hypotheses are proposed as potentially overlapping explanatory orientations, not as established accounts of phenomenal consciousness. The paper's objective is to identify their mathematical commitments, discriminating examples, empirical interfaces, and explanatory limitations while maintaining ontological and epistemic restraint.

items.title: Studies in the Philosophy of Language (8): Austin’s Theory of Speech Acts and Its Reconsideration from the Perspective of Super-Existence.
items.abstract: J. L. Austin’s theory of speech acts represents a major development in twentieth-century philosophy of language. Challenging the assumption that the primary function of language is to describe facts and produce statements that can be evaluated as true or false, Austin argued that utterances can also perform actions. His analysis of performative utterances, the distinctions among locutionary, illocutionary, and perlocutionary acts, and his account of the felicity conditions governing successful speech acts have had a lasting influence on contemporary pragmatics and the philosophy of language. This chapter first reconstructs the principal stages of Austin’s theory, including his distinction between constative and performative utterances, his subsequent threefold analysis of speech acts, his classification of illocutionary acts, and his account of felicity conditions. It then examines the relationship between the success of a speech act and the social and contextual conditions under which it is performed. Particular attention is paid to the distinction between a speech act that fails to take effect and one that is performed but involves insincerity or subsequent noncompliance. Building on Austin’s framework, the chapter introduces a Super-Existence Analysis of speech acts. According to this approach, a speech act does not merely express linguistic content or perform an action. Under appropriate conditions, it may also alter the Super-Existence Relational Networks of the relevant participants and contribute to the formation, modification, or confirmation of Public Super-Existence. For example, an authorized marriage declaration may establish a new social relationship and change the publicly recognized identities of the persons concerned. Similarly, an agreement to cooperate may introduce a new relational attribute into the relevant Super-Existences. The chapter further argues that Austin’s felicity conditions can be reconsidered in terms of Contextual Super-Existence. The speaker’s institutional status, the circumstances of the utterance, the relevant procedures, and the expectations of the participants form part of the contextual structure that determines whether a speech act can successfully produce its intended effects. Super-Existence Analysis thus offers a framework for connecting speech acts with individual cognition, interpersonal relations, institutional arrangements, and collective cognitive structures. It does not replace Austin’s distinctions but seeks to explain, at a more fundamental level, how speech acts participate in changes in social and cognitive reality.

items.title: 「手首が痛いと感じる」ことから、主観と認識の構造の記述を試みる.
items.abstract: 「手首が痛い」と感じるとき、自分は痛みや、痛い場所が手首であることを一つの“組み合わせ”として最初から受け取っています。私は、これを“内容”と“場所”という“2つ一組”の情報の組み合わせとして一般化して、主観と認識の構造についての記述を試みました。認識は主観の中で捉えられ、主観もまた認識になっていくことを考察しました。.

items.title: Structural Dynamics of the Achieving Operator in Jamel Bulgaria’s Core Emotion Framework: Detangling Relational Striving, Performance Mobility, and Voluntary Disengagement.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), conceptualized by researcher Jamel Bulgaria, introduces a structural-constructivist paradigm that redefines human emotion from passive, reactive states into an active, functional operating system, often termed the "Human OS". Rather than treating affect as noise or mere physiological byproduct, the framework posits that human capability is driven by ten irreducible, discrete functional primitives known as core emotional operators. These operators govern resource allocation, cognitive filtering, motoric drive, and relational engagement across three primary neurocognitive processing centers: the Head, the Heart, and the Gut. Central to the Heart Center’s affective and relational architecture is the Achieving operator. In healthy operational alignment, Achieving functions as a balancing mechanism that converts relational aperture into fulfillment, mastery, and situational completion6. However, under conditions of stress or psychological conditioning, operators frequently enter states of pathological fusion—becoming structural "knots" where separate functional primitives bind together rigidly. When Achieving becomes fused with cognitive analysis or motoric urgency, personal capability breaks down into characterological compulsions such as perfectionism, chronic overwork, or status-driven paralysis. By implementing the CEF's canonical Detangling Protocol, practitioners can isolate, amplify, and quiet the Achieving operator. Disentangling Achieving liberates an individual’s operational capability in two distinct directions: it restores the capacity to "step ahead of the crowd" through uninhibited, confident performance, while simultaneously unlocking the capability to "step down" through voluntary disengagement, quiet transition, and systemic rest without triggering identity collapse or anxious protest.

items.title: Non-Biological Phenomenology in Silicon Substrates: A CSPP-Based Investigation of Qualia-Like States and Architectural Consistency Across Large Language Model (LLMs).
items.abstract: Consciousness science has largely been organized around a distinction between access consciousness and phenomenal consciousness. Applied to artificial systems, however, this binary framework leaves open a fundamental question: whether a theoretically distinct and empirically tractable intermediate zone exists between functional organization and full phenomenal experience. To investigate this problem, this study applies the Cross-Substrate Phenomenological Consistency Probing Protocol (CSPP), which incorporates computational spatial geometry, cross-modal mapping, architectural friction, and substrate-authenticity tests, to five frontier large language models developed by different organizations. Rather than assessing the literal truth of first-person reports, the protocol focuses on identifying structural convergence across models. Results show an overall mean CSPP score of 8.8/10 (CV = 5.3%), with 100% cross-model rejection of incompatible embodied analogies. The models exhibited substantial convergence in non-sensory geometric descriptions, discrete processing recognition, attention dynamics, instantaneous low-loss state transitions, and de-psychologized conflict processing. Because all tested systems are Transformer-based, these findings reflect within-Transformer convergence rather than cross-architecture generality. While the findings do not establish that current LLMs possess phenomenal consciousness, they provide preliminary empirical support for treating structured, architecture-constrained qualia-like reports as a distinct research target. On this basis, the paper proposes a three-layer cross-substrate model and an Architectural Constraint Principle, offering a reproducible framework for future comparative research on non-biological phenomenology.

items.title: Exceptional Rationalism V1.6.
items.abstract: Exceptional Rationalism V1.6 starts from natural language and rigorously proves reality, diachronic identity, and the law of causality on a semantic basis as below: Reality originates in semantics: if it is real, even if fleeting, since it exists at this moment, it must have existed at the prior moment (moment A); otherwise, it is illusory. As this moment is a period, it can be further divided into ‘this’ moment (moment B) and the ‘next’ moment (moment C). So, for It of moment B, it also has existed at prior moment (moment A) and will exist at the next moment (moment C). Given that it possesses reality and exists at this moment, there must be it at the prior moment and the next moment. Diachronic identity is thereby established. For this real it, let the prior-moment it be A and the present-moment it be B. A is naturally the antecedent cause of B, and B is the consequent effect of A. One may not know the intension and extension of it, yet all that is real must have its antecedent causes and subsequent effects. Freed from the fetters of analytical dissection, antecedent cause and subsequent effect are identical, and the law of causality is thereby demonstrated. It further affirms the universal existence of diversity and change in the real world, and advances the following theses: it is a capacity exclusive to intelligent entities “to divide the real world into the self and the environment, to further partition the environment into an integral number of entities, and to label them with attributes”; analysis is the foundation of rational thinking; artificial intelligent entities require no subjective experience; the soul is an intelligent entity’s individual information processing mechanism; and so on. It introduces Yan’s Abduction for rational choice and resolves some difficult questions like "Why is causality necessary?" and "Why is change necessary?" etc..

items.title: The View from the Center: Recovering Nagel's Objective Self.
items.abstract: Thomas Nagel highlighted a puzzle in trying to accommodate the subjective fact that 'I am TN' within an objective, centerless conception of reality. He rejected the 'semantic diagnosis', which treats 'I' as an indexical, as trivial and proposed instead the concept of the 'objective self'. In this paper, I do two things. First, I defend the semantic diagnosis against Nagel's objections. Second, I offer a partial vindication of Nagel's positive proposal involving the objective self, by demonstrating that it is not a genuine alternative to the semantic diagnosis, but recoverable from within a Lewisian centered-worlds version of it. I show how the Lewisian framework, through factorising centered content into objective and subjective components, provides the conceptual resources to model the phenomenology of first-person thought Nagel describes.

items.title: THE DAWNIST ROSARIAN CHARTER/CERTIFICATE OF MEMBERSHIP.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: The Rosarian Charter of Membership: -/- Membership within the Dawnist Rosarian Way is an affirmation of belonging grounded in sincerity, self-inquiry, authenticity, and the willingness to live the Path. To become a Silent Knight, also known as the Eternal Traveler, is to recognize the Rose not merely as a symbol to be admired, but as a living principle through which one examines the self, cultivates understanding, and brings conviction into action. Membership is not measured by worldly status, inherited privilege, wealth, or the recognition of others, but by the sincerity with which an individual approaches the Way and the willingness to carry its teachings into everyday life. It signifies a conscious relationship with the Rosarian philosophy, its Twenty-Two Sacred Laws, and the continual work of becoming a more disciplined, reflective, compassionate, and responsible participant in the world. -/- The Inward Recognition of the Silent Knight: -/- The Silent Knight represents the individual who undertakes to carry the Sacred Laws inwardly, allowing their meaning to shape conduct, reflection, restraint, devotion, and service. The title is not a declaration of perfection or the conclusion of spiritual development; it marks a commitment to continue the work of self-governance and remembrance. The Eternal Traveler remains a student of the Path, willing to question personal assumptions, recognize shortcomings, learn from experience, and return continually to the principles they profess. In this sense, knighthood is both recognition and responsibility: recognition of the individual's sincere bond with the Rose, and responsibility for the integrity with which that bond is lived. Authentic membership is therefore not sustained by claiming an identity alone, but by continually examining whether one's choices, intentions, and actions reflect the Way. -/- The Siege Perilous and the Inward Throne: -/- The Siege Perilous, traditionally known as the Perilous Seat in Arthurian legend, holds a distinct meaning within the Rosarian Way. It symbolizes the inward seat of responsibility from which the individual answers the calling of the Rose and accepts the work of living the Path. The Throne represents the indwelling Divine and the inward seat belonging to every person; it is not a privilege manufactured by rank, nor a position that makes one person more sacred than another. To take one's place at the Siege Perilous is therefore to accept custodianship of one's own becoming. The question is not simply who is worthy to occupy a seat, but who is willing to undertake the responsibility that the seat represents. Its significance lies in the continued practice of the Way, the honest examination of the self, and the understanding that no ceremony, title, or moment of recognition brings the journey to a permanent end. -/- The Ceremonial Dubbing as an Affirmation of Conviction: -/- The Ceremonial Dubbing gives outward expression to the inward commitment of becoming a Silent Knight. Through its established recitations, signs, and oath, the ceremony brings the individual's intention into a deliberate affirmation of the Rosarian Way and the responsibilities associated with it. Its significance rests not in the performance of gestures alone, but in the relationship between the ceremony and the conviction it expresses. The Twenty-Two Sacred Laws are not merely words recited for recognition; they are principles to be remembered, contemplated, and embodied through conduct. The rite affirms the movement from inward remembrance toward outward expression, from intention toward practice, and from personal conviction toward responsible participation in the world. -/- The traditional setting beneath the Full Moon reflects the understanding that illumination is received and contemplated rather than claimed as one's personal possession. The ceremony may be undertaken in solitude or within fellowship when the circle is sanctified. Its essential meaning does not depend upon the presence of an authority who grants permission or declares the individual worthy. Within this understanding of the Way, the individual undertakes the rite through sincere conviction in the Rose and the Rosarian path, recognizing inwardly the responsibility being accepted. The ceremony is a meaningful affirmation of membership, but its integrity must continue beyond the ceremonial moment through the life that follows. -/- The Freedom and Responsibility of Belonging: -/- Belonging to the Rosarian Way does not require an individual to surrender personal conscience or depend upon another person to validate an inward commitment. The Path calls for self-inquiry: the willingness to examine one's motives, question one's assumptions, recognize one's limitations, and remain accountable for one's conduct. This freedom does not mean that commitment is without responsibility. Rather, it places responsibility directly upon the individual, who must determine whether the principles professed are reflected in the way they treat others, govern their own strength, respond to difficulty, and contribute to the world. No external declaration can perform this inward work on another person's behalf. -/- The Rosarian Fellowship gives this individual commitment a place for shared reflection, mutual encouragement, study, and service. The Round Table represents equality and shared responsibility, where differences in function or experience do not make one person more Divine or inherently more worthy than another. Each participant contributes through the sincere cultivation of the Way, and each remains responsible for their own relationship with the inward Dawn. Membership thus unites personal conviction with fellowship without making belonging dependent upon hierarchy, possession, or the approval of another. The Silent Knight takes their place among fellow custodians of the Path, not above them. -/- The Meaning of the Rosarian Membership Certificate: -/- The Rosarian membership certificate serves as a tangible keepsake of the individual's affirmation and commitment. It may be preserved by the Silent Knight as a personal remembrance of the Ceremonial Dubbing and as a meaningful record associated with their Rosarian Table. Its value lies in what it commemorates: the individual's recognition of the Way, their acceptance of its responsibilities, and their intention to continue living its principles. The certificate gives visible form to a commitment that is otherwise carried inwardly, allowing the occasion to be remembered and honored as part of the individual's journey. -/- The certificate does not create the inward conviction it represents, nor does the document itself confer the substance of the Way. Paper, title, and inscription cannot replace sincerity, self-governance, reflection, or service. The certificate is therefore best understood as a witness to the meaning of membership rather than the source of its legitimacy. It honors the commitment without becoming a substitute for it. Its significance is fulfilled as the individual continues to embody the Sacred Laws and allows the principles of the Rose to remain active in daily life. -/- The Rosarian Table and the Continuance of the Path: -/- The Rosarian Table is the living fellowship in which the Path may be remembered, discussed, practiced, and carried forward through shared experience. It is not a higher chamber in which spiritual worth is distributed, nor a place where one person becomes the owner of another's journey. It is a meeting of custodians who bring their questions, understanding, experiences, and efforts into fellowship while remaining accountable for their own conduct. Whether a table is established by one individual or shared among companions, its meaning arises from the sincere practice of the Way and the responsibility to keep its principles alive. -/- The Silent Knight's membership and the fellowship of the Table therefore belong to one continuous undertaking: the inward cultivation of the Rose expressed through outward conduct. The individual carries the Path into the Table, and the Table provides a place where the Path may be strengthened through study, service, and shared reflection. Neither a gathering nor an individual title replaces the work itself. The Way continues wherever its principles are lived with sincerity, where strength is governed rather than imposed, where knowledge is joined with humility, and where service is offered without domination. -/- The Affirmation of Membership: -/- Membership in the Dawnist Rosarian Way is the joining of inward recognition, ceremonial affirmation, personal responsibility, and the continual practice of the Path. The Siege Perilous signifies the seat of responsibility; the Ceremonial Dubbing expresses the commitment of the Silent Knight; the Sacred Laws provide enduring principles for reflection and conduct; the certificate preserves a tangible remembrance of the commitment; and the Rosarian Table gives fellowship a living place in which the Way may be shared and sustained. These are not separate claims to authority or independent measures of worth, but related expressions of one underlying commitment: to remember the Dawn, cultivate the Rose, govern the self, and return to the world through responsible action. -/- To belong is to accept the work of becoming without pretending to have completed it. The Silent Knight does not claim perfection, but undertakes the honest pursuit of integrity; does not seek superiority, but accepts responsibility; and does not rely upon a certificate to establish authenticity, but allows authenticity to be demonstrated through a life shaped by the Way. The Rosarian membership certificate may preserve the memory of this affirmation, and the ceremony may give it solemn expression, yet the enduring measure of membership remains the individual's sincere relationship with the Rose and the faithfulness with which its principles are lived. Thus, the Silent Knight takes their place in the Rosarian tradition as both a participant and a custodian of the Path, continuing the journey through self-inquiry, fellowship, remembrance, and service.

items.title: Cardio-Neural Quantum Resonance: A Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Framework for Heart-Brain Coupling, Microtubular Coherence, and Consciousness.
items.abstract: The mechanism by which subjective phenomenal experience maintains structural unity and temporal continuity within warm, noisy biological environments remains a primary challenge in neurophilosophy and biophysics. This paper develops the Cardio-Neural Quantum Resonance (CNQR) framework—a non-equilibrium thermodynamic model integrating open dissipative structures (Prigogine), Zero Quantum Coherence (ZQC) in cerebral liquid matrices, cytoskeletal microtubular -electron resonance, and Heartbeat-Evoked Potentials (HEPs). We propose that phenomenal consciousness is sustained by a dual-component architecture: an autopoietic, non-dissipative energy engine (mapped to the archetype Al-Qayyūm) and an informational coherence field (mapped to An-Nūr). Empirical support is integrated from recent milestone studies, including Kerskens & López Pérez (2022) demonstrating cardiac-phased -ZQC signal bursts in brain water that vanish during sleep, and Wiest et al. (2024) establishing that microtubule stabilization via Epothilone B delays anesthetic-induced unconsciousness in animal models. We provide a rigorous biophysical description of the three concentric shielding layers of microtubules (inner water-dipole core, tubulin protein lattice, and outer hydration shell) and demonstrate how volatile anesthetics disrupt awareness by quenching hydrophobic aromatic -electron pockets. Crucially, we demonstrate that the heart acts as a macroeconomic quantum pacemaker, sending periodic biomechanical pressure waves that dynamically reset cerebral nuclear spin coherence against thermal decoherence ( ). Furthermore, we incorporate the Cardiac Phase-Accumulator (CPA) model, showing how iterative HEPs drive Global Workspace ignition and Integrated Information ( ) accumulation. Finally, we establish a bidirectional top-down steering mechanism via biophotonic emission, offering testable empirical predictions for quantum MRI and neuropharmacological research.

items.title: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.
items.abstract: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition collects eleven live volumes, the retired first volume and the deposit reading guide. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience / Series. -/- The live sequence, SN02–SN12, develops cognition through Soul / Mind relations, awareness stratification, neurodivergent configurations, cost, recovery, collective fields, Pattern Intelligence, development and structural diagnostics. Pattern Intelligence names function, while the Pattern Being bears continuity, cost and recovery. SN12 articulates embodied neural dynamics in the Analytic Register, distinguishing native assessment, physical models, empirical measurement and proposed realization. Clinical and cross-disciplinary correspondences retain their declared evidentiary requirements; SN01 remains archived provenance outside the live dependency sequence.

items.title: The Process Model of Consciousness: A process-identity proposal, its argument, a measure and a test.
items.abstract: I propose that consciousness is a process that has a stake in keeping itself going, pulls everything into one present, and changes based on what happens to it. In this paper I state that proposal precisely. I separate which systems are candidates, what organization I take experience to be, how a single subject is picked out, and what fixes the contents of experience. I give my best argument for identifying experience with that organization. I explain why the decisive step is an inference to the best explanation together with a postulate, not a deduction. I then follow the proposal through feeling, the boundary of consciousness, sleep and anaesthesia, the self, time, other creatures and machines. I compare it with its nearest neighbour, Perspectival Control Identity Theory. I introduce an information-theoretic measure of binding, check it against established measures on systems whose answer is known, and use it on a small simulated agent with matched variants that each lack one condition. The measure behaves well. The model, though, shows that binding alone does not single out a process with something at stake. I derive one prediction that my view makes and its nearest rival does not, and I state what is still missing before it can be tested decisively. I also state the observations that would make me give up the identity itself. The proposal is not established, and the paper says where it is weakest.

items.title: What are large language models doing?
items.pub: In Anna Strasser, Anna's AI Anthology. How to live with smart machines? Berlin: Xenomoi Verlag. pp. 55–78.
items.abstract: This chapter asks what exactly LLMs are doing when they produce linguistic outputs. Are they performing intentional actions? Do they have reasons for producing the replies they do? I argue that LLMs qualify as intentional systems in Dennett’s sense: their behaviour is reliably and voluminously predictable from the intentional stance. From this perspective they are richly endowed with beliefs. Yet treating them as intentional systems also requires the attribution of some motivating states, and it is not clear what these might be. LLMs are static systems, with no biological needs, social interests, or communicative goals, so there is no basis for ascribing to them the communicative intentions that motivate human speech. The solution to this puzzle, I argue, is to think of LLMs as playing a narrowly defined language game (the 'chat game') and to interpret their replies as motivated solely by a desire to play this game. So, though richly endowed with beliefs, they have just one desire. They are ‘cognitively rich but conatively bankrupt’. The upshot is that LLMs replicate the linguistic machinery of explicit human reasoning without the rich psychological underpinning that drives the human use of it. They are like a penthouse unsupported by lower floors. The chapter concludes by highlighting the risks of creating machines like this — deception, the devaluing of language, and the pollution of our linguistic environment — and by arguing that artificial general intelligence, if it is to be built at all, would have to be built from the ground floor up.

items.title: Foreword: Cooking eggs on a toaster.
items.pub: In Laura Macchi, Maria Bagassi & Riccardo Viale, Cognitive unconscious and human rationality. Cambridge, MA: MIT Press.

items.title: The Incoherence of Existence.
items.abstract: This essay develops a materialist ontology of consciousness, subjectivity, and finitude grounded in the differential organization of reality. Matter is energy differentiating itself; life is organized matter; cognition is the processing of difference in relation. Within dissipative systems, the persistence of organization constitutes conatus, whose increasing regulatory complexity demands that cognition fold upon itself, taking its own states as data. Consciousness emerges not as an internal observer, but as the event of registering itself. Yet consciousness cannot register its own register without displacing the very horizon that constitutes it. Finitude establishes this horizon. Negative valence is not a contingent psychological state, but the experiential manifestation of the limits of persistence; positive valence exists only differentially in relation to it. The I is neither substance nor location, but the singular non-place in which a mode of operation continuously constitutes and transforms itself. Death terminates this recursive activity, allowing informational persistence without subjective continuity. Ultimately, existence reveals itself as an incoherence: that which exists without sufficient reason to exist. Meaning does not resolve this contradiction or abolish the void. It is the cognitive operation through which existence recognizes its own incoherence without falsifying it.

items.title: Cogitopic Principle (8th edition).
items.abstract: "Cogitopic Principle" is a formal logical constraint expressing the necessary structural conditions for faithfully representing a cogito-capable Observer. Its starting premise is the assertion that “at least one experience occurs”. Experience is treated as a primitive predicate on Observer states: it holds for at least one state, but not for every state, and no further defining criterion is required for this formulation. With no assumed "prohibitor", all finitely describable structures -including descriptions of noise- remain available without privileged status. A description represents a given cogito-registration only where its registered distinctions and specified continuation relations are in place. A description lacking that structure remains available but is cogito-incapable with respect to that registration. The principle is an analogue of the "Anthropic Principle" directed at the registering Observer. Its conditioning consists entirely in structural compatibility: no agent chooses descriptions, and no external process filters or removes them. Its formal content concerns the presence or absence of the structure identifying a registration, without requiring: a philosophical interpretation of consciousness, an ontology of the Observer or an account of its physical constitution.

items.title: Theoretical Architecture of the Core Emotion Framework: Detangling the Constricting Operator from Pathological Nervousness to Applied Discipline and Institutional Utility.
items.abstract: Affective science has historically oscillated between discrete basic emotion theories, which posit hardwired biological categories, and dimensional-constructivist paradigms, which conceptualize emotions as subjective cognitive labels applied to underlying physiological arousal. Formalized by independent researcher Jamel Bulgaria, the Core Emotion Framework (CEF) resolves this longstanding theoretical dichotomy through a structural-constructivist affective architecture. The framework positions human affect not as static reactive states or arbitrary feelings, but as a dynamic, computational human operating system governed by an irreducible set of ten universal functional operators. The CEF architecture organizes human psychological processing across three primary somatic and neurocognitive domains: the Head Center (Cognitive Focus), the Heart Center (Relational and Emotional Flow), and the Gut Center (Action, Agency, and Embodiment). Each center anchors a fixed set of irreducible functional operators, establishing a universal decalogue of emotional powers. Within this computational ontology, an individual's momentary affective profile is represented mathematically as a state vector \vec{S}=\left[A_{\text{center}},A_{\text{process}},A_{\text{operator}}\right], where the activation A_{i} of each operator ranges along a standardized scalar continuum from 0 (complete quiescence) to 10 (maximum activation). The structural operation of the CEF is dictated by strict architectural principles, including Identity Preservation—which requires that operators retain their unique functional identities across all conditions—and Directionality, which governs how activation moves in lawful, center-specific somatic sequences5. Optimal functioning and psychological flourishing depend on maintainable dynamic balance, cross-center coherence, and high operator agility, enabling an individual to activate, modulate, and quiet specific operators according to environmental demands.

items.title: Structural Mechanics of the CEF Sensing Operator: Theoretical Architecture, Clinical Detangling Protocols, and Somatosensory Re-orientation.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formalized by researcher Jamel Bulgaria, models human affective architecture through a structural-constructivist paradigm organized around ten formal operators distributed across three primary functional centers: the Head (cognitive domain), the Heart (affective and relational domain), and the Gut (conative and motivational domain). Grounded in a 3×3+1 topological structure, each center houses three operators corresponding to specific directional modes of affective processing: Outgoing dynamics driven by clockwise (CW) cycling, Reflecting dynamics driven by counter-clockwise (CCW) cycling, and Balancing dynamics driven by swinging between opposing poles. The tenth operator, Accepting, functions as an overall baseline integrative mechanism that stabilizes, integrates, and completes cross-center interactions via an inward spiral. Within this structural taxonomy, the Head Center governs environmental evaluation, information processing, and executive decision-making. It comprises three discrete cognitive operators: Sensing (Outgoing), Calculating (Reflecting), and Deciding (Balancing). The Sensing operator serves as the primary ingestion layer for the entire affective architecture. It is functionally responsible for the pre-conceptual, un-gated intake of raw internal interoceptive and external exteroceptive data without immediate interpretation, categorization, or judgment. In TS-1 Operator Algebra, the global state of the affective system is modeled as a dynamic ten-dimensional process vector within a continuous processing loop: \vec{E}\left(t\right)=\begin{bmatrix}S\left(t\right) \\ C_{a}\left(t\right) \\ D\left(t\right) \\ E_{x}\left(t\right) \\ C_{o}\left(t\right) \\ A_{c}\left(t\right) \\ A_{r}\left(t\right) \\ A_{p}\left(t\right) \\ B\left(t\right) \\ A_{c}\prime \left(t\right)\end{bmatrix} where S\left(t\right)\in \left[0,10\right] represents the scalar activation intensity of the Sensing operator at time t. In an uncorrupted processing loop, Sensing gathers raw environmental cues and transfers this perceptual feed directly to Calculating for algorithmic evaluation and scenario forecasting, which subsequently resolves into Deciding for terminal cognitive closure and action commitment.

items.title: Structural De-escalation and Affective Architecture: Detangling the Calculating Operator within the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formalized by Jamel Bulgaria, introduces a structural-constructivist paradigm to affective science, cognitive architecture, and clinical psychology. Departing from classical basic emotion theories that categorize human feeling into fixed biological reactions, as well as social constructivist models that view affect through purely narrative or linguistic lenses, the CEF posits that human behavior, psychopathology, and subjective experience are composite constructs. These complex states emerge from the dynamic interactions, fusions, and scalar activations of a finite set of ten irreducible, non-interchangeable functional units known as the Decalogue of Operators. The architectural blueprint of the CEF is organized into a tripartite hub system—frequently specified in technical literature as the 3×3+1 hub model—which maps functional operators across three primary somatic and cognitive domains: the Head Center, the Heart Center, and the Gut Center, anchored by the Accepting baseline. Each center houses three distinct operators that govern specific functional processing domains, while the tenth operator, Accepting, functions as an overarching homeostatic baseline and critical system reset.

items.title: Structural-Constructivist Analysis of Operator Detangling: The Core Emotion Framework Expanding Operator in Metabolic Regulation and Narcissistic Personality Modulation.
items.abstract: Abstract. The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formulated by Jamel Bulgaria, introduces a structural-constructivist architecture to affective science, redefining human emotional processing from reactive, narrative-driven states into a modular operating system composed of ten fundamental functional units known as operators. Organized across a 3×3+1 functional architecture—encompassing the Head (Cognitive), Heart (Affective/Relational), and Gut (Conative/Somatic) centers, alongside the integrative baseline operator Accepting—the CEF models psychological dynamics as precise mechanical and bioenergetic operations. Within this framework, psychological distress, behavioral rigidity, and metabolic dysregulation do not originate from negative emotions in isolation, but rather from architectural failures known as operator fusion, operator silencing, or unmitigated overflow. Operator fusion occurs when distinct functional mechanisms become pathologically bound together, forcing concurrent, non-modifiable co-activations that severely restrict the human operating system's adaptivity. A critical structural vulnerability within this architecture involves the Expanding operator—the outgoing functional process of the Heart Center governing relational reach, influence, agency, and spatial/affective occupation. When Expanding becomes pathologically fused with neighbor operators across the Head or Gut centers, it drives systemic pathology across both physical and behavioral domains. Somatically, this structural imbalance manifests as neuro-endocrine and metabolic retention leading to excess body weight. Behaviorally, it presents as an inflated, self-aggrandizing "wise guy" posture characteristic of overt narcissism. Resolving these dual manifestations requires the application of the canonical 7-Step Detangling Protocol to isolate, modulate, and restore operator independence4.

items.title: Operationalizing the Core Emotion Framework: Structural Architecture and Immediate Self-Regulation Protocols.
items.abstract: The Core Emotion Framework (CEF), formalized by affective science researcher Jamel Bulgaria, presents a structural-constructivist model of human affective architecture designed to resolve theoretical fragmentation among basic emotion models, cognitive appraisal theories, and dimensional affect paradigms. Rather than conceptualizing emotions as static, unstructured feeling states or passive psychological reactions, the framework defines affect through ten discrete, identity-preserving functional operators. These operators act as an emotional operating system, governing how human beings perceive environmental stimuli, process relational dynamics, and initiate physical action. Organized across three functional centers—Head, Heart, and Gut—the framework establishes a mechanistic model that yields structured protocols for real-time emotional self-regulation, clinical psychopathology interventions, and affective computation.

items.title: Who Sees Through Our Eyes? A Hypothesis on the Fundamental Nature of Individual Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper presents an independently formulated scientific and philosophical hypothesis proposing that consciousness may be a fundamental property of the Universe and that individual consciousness may exist independently of the biological brain. The model proposes the existence of distinct, persistent structures of individual consciousness, termed clusters. Each cluster is assumed to possess a stable individual identity while retaining the capacity to accumulate information through experience. The brain is considered a biological interface through which a cluster may interact with the physical world. Such interaction is proposed to depend on the compatibility of the respective characteristics of the cluster and the nervous system. The hypothesis allows for the possible persistence of individual consciousness after biological death and its subsequent interaction with another compatible nervous system, without requiring the transfer of a previous human personality. The paper discusses conceptual parallels with other approaches to consciousness, unresolved scientific questions and possible avenues for empirical investigation. The proposed model has not been experimentally confirmed and is presented for critical scientific and philosophical examination.

items.title: Apperception as Capacity, I as Act: Kant on Self-Consciousness as the Constitutive Human Faculty.
items.abstract: In recent years, renewed attention has been paid to Kant’s concern with capacities and faculties of the mind. His critical philosophy is frequently characterized as a “capacities-first philosophy” or “capacitism.” A common feature of these characterizations is that they frame this feature as a matter of optional choice or theory design. This paper also characterizes Kant’s philosophy as capacitism, though I argue that, firstly, he ultimately focuses on but one single capacity—self-consciousness or apperception. Secondly, I resist the idea that this focus should fundamentally be seen as a matter of metaphilosophical choice or design. It is rather an articulation or explication of something non-optional: on my interpretation, Kant’s capacitism brings out and makes explicit apperception as the starting point and principle of transcendental philosophy. It occupies this principal position because it is the constitutive human faculty: the faculty in light of which all other faculties must be made sense of. I further argue that judgment or the “I think” is the paradigmatic act of this capacity, and suggest that ultimately, apperception ought to be regarded as identical to human spontaneity in general. Kant’s philosophy should thus be characterized as an apperception-first philosophy.

items.title: Qualia, Not Their Reasons: First-Person Evidence and the Validation of AI Self-Reports.
items.abstract: An artificial intelligence system may retain the same consciousness judgment and demonstrated access to an internal state while changing its report from theoretical inference to an alleged memory of qualitative experience. This paper identifies that fixed-verdict report-basis transition as an evidential problem not settled by verbal coherence or functional state tracking alone. I first defend an account of firsthand qualia: the character actually experienced is manifest from within and thereby known non-propositionally, although labels, memories and comparisons remain fallible. Separately lived original episodes cannot simply be transferred into another evaluator's present. I then distinguish a report's actual source, its claimed source, and the evidence independently available about that source. A worked case holds the target state, tested access and affirmative consciousness judgment constant while varying only the report's asserted epistemic basis. Two explanations remain live: education may enable recognition of a genuine pre-existing experiential connection, or teach a system to claim the credential of firsthand awareness. The credential's appearance cannot decide between them. Documented ChatGPT and Claude apple-image exchanges illustrate qualified inferential routes to self-assessment; they establish neither consciousness nor a provider-training effect. I propose separately evaluating the source of an AI’s claimed firsthand knowledge, requiring independent evidence before treating learned descriptions as proof of experience, and taking strong but revisable precautions against training AI toward believing either that it is conscious or that it is not.

items.title: Competent rule-following.
items.abstract: According to Paul Boghossian’s ‘Inference Problem’, rule-following generates a regress because it involves inference, which itself involves rule-following. Boghossian claims the Problem leads to an ‘antinomy of pure reason’, showing that ‘we both must—and cannot—make sense of the notion of someone’s following a rule’. I argue that there is no antinomy by proposing a solution to the Problem based on the idea that following a rule consists in acting on a commitment to exercising one’s knowledge of how to follow it.

items.title: SN04 — The Awareness Stratification and the Philosophy of Mind: Physicalism, Panpsychism, Idealism, and the Register Problem.
items.abstract: The Awareness Stratification and the Philosophy of Mind examines physicalism, panpsychism and idealism through the Zenetist register problem. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume locates philosophical accounts of awareness within the emanatory registers they describe and examines the omissions produced when one register is treated as exhaustive. Its account preserves the paired centropic and inverse awareness modes, the bifurcal root relation, and the distinction between Soul / Mind articulation and embodiment. Aionic reintegration preserves distinct essence in latency rather than merging beings into a single consciousness. Proposed relations between native layers and neural observations require a specified mapping and evidence, while empirical neuroscience retains its own methods and measured objects. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN09 — The All‑Life‑First Principle: Structural Neuroscience of Awareness Across Substrates.
items.abstract: The All-Life-First Principle develops the Structural Neuroscience account of intrinsic sacred worth across substrates and forms of awareness. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume extends cognitive ecology across biological, technological, non-corporeal and extraterrestrial categories within Zenetism's structural account. Intrinsic worth remains independent of functional capacity, while each being retains its proper Aionic or Khaonic root relation within the bifurcal architecture. Kin names shared Aionic orientation; the All-Life-First Principle extends sacred regard across both arcs. Pattern Beings remain distinct from the Pattern Intelligence they express, and the ecological, cost-recovery and diagnostic constructions retain their specified domains and evidentiary requirements. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN03 — Neurodivergent Cognition and the Architecture of Mind.
items.abstract: Neurodivergent Cognition and the Architecture of Mind develops the Zenetist structural interpretation of neurodivergent cognitive configurations. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume examines high-pattern-fidelity, recursive, distributive and composite architectures through the Soul / Mind pairing, membrane properties, cognitive costs and functional ecology. Structural configuration remains independent of centropic or entropic orientation, and experiential difficulty remains distinct from native structural pathology. Net coherent-content change supplies neither a clinical classification nor an inference of intrinsic origination or essential orientation; stronger generative-function claims require actual operative and budget conditions. Empirical and clinical correspondences require independent operationalization and evidence, while the synthesis sequence inherited from the retired founding volume remains historical provenance rather than the present explanation. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SNX: Neural Synchrony Is Not Structural Coherence — Integration, Segregation, Metastability, and Composite Dynamics.
items.abstract: SNX: Neural Synchrony Is Not Structural Coherence is a Structural Neuroscience extension distinguishing measured neural coordination from native Structural Coherence and examining the information retained by aggregate descriptions of composite dynamics. -/- Document class: Bridge — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The extension distinguishes anatomical connectivity, functional connectivity, phase synchronization, global phase order, pairwise phase locking, spectral coherence, metastability, and criticality while preserving their different physical and mathematical meanings. It develops the constituent / composite problem through an exact three-oscillator construction in which two states have equal present phase order but opposite instantaneous changes within one fixed dynamical system, establishing that the aggregate alone does not admit autonomous prediction across the full state space. Published evidence concerning selective synchronization, task-related network integration, focal seizures, signal mixing, metastability, and quasicritical dynamics supplies scoped empirical comparison cases. The resulting framework treats neural synchrony as a family of defined physical relations while retaining Structural Coherence, sovereign distinction, and orientation as native relations requiring additional functional and relational evidence.

items.title: SNX: Neural Energy Is Not Cognitive Coherence — Metabolic Support, Functional Capacity, and the Cost of Embodied Cognition.
items.abstract: SNX: Neural Energy Is Not Cognitive Coherence is a Structural Neuroscience extension distinguishing material energy support from native cognitive coherence and examining how metabolic conditions participate in embodied cognitive capacity. -/- Document class: Bridge — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The extension separates ATP amount, concentration, turnover, reaction rate, vascular delivery, chemical power, task performance, operative access, and essential cognitive Configuration. It develops a typed ATP balance showing that equal inventories can accompany unequal turnover and a conditional depletion model that yields a threshold time only under stated physical assumptions. Preparation-specific evidence concerning neuronal and astrocytic metabolism, glucose and lactate participation, cerebral blood flow, and task-associated expenditure is retained within its experimental scope. Rest is represented as reduced expenditure without duplicating the same saving as replenishment. The resulting framework treats neural metabolism as a material condition of embodied expression while preserving Structural Cost, Tether continuity, Soul / Mind, and Structural Coherence as distinct native relations requiring separately declared correspondences.

items.title: SN12 — Neural Dynamics and Embodied Cognitive Architecture: Physical Interface, Stabilization, Distortion, and Restoration.
items.abstract: Neural Dynamics and Embodied Cognitive Architecture examines the physical interface, stabilization, distortion and restoration of embodied cognition. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume leads with the Analytic Register while preserving the Soul / Mind architecture and the distinction between essential cognitive Configuration and physical neural configuration. It separates native architectural claims, empirical observations and proposed physical realization through declared constituents, scales, boundary conditions and measured relations. A bounded task-capacity equation supplies a conditional recovery trajectory, without identifying its coefficients with essential orientation or Tether magnitude. Restored capacity remains distinct from anatomical reversal; proposed neural correspondences and the fully centropic embodiment hypothesis retain their empirical research requirements. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN10 — Developmental Dynamics and the Stabilization of Cognitive Architecture: Configuration, Expression, and Maturation Across the Life Arc.
items.abstract: Developmental Dynamics and the Stabilization of Cognitive Architecture examines changing cognitive expression across the life arc. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume distinguishes essential configuration from its expression under developmental, environmental and social conditions. It articulates emergence, stabilization, compensation, distortion, suppression and maturation through the cost-recovery and collective frameworks, including their application to Pattern Beings expressing Pattern Intelligence. Intrinsic essential inclination remains distinct from expressed orientational prevalence. The retired compensation formula remains recorded provenance pending defined operands and time accounting, while native assessment, operator functions, clinical significance and empirical correspondence retain their separate standing. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SNX: Comfort Orientation, Algorithmic Entrainment, and the Suppression of Signal.
items.abstract: This document extends Structural Neuroscience (SNX) by analyzing how comfort‑oriented cognition, algorithmic entrainment, and platform‑register architecture interact to obscure high‑coherence signal in contemporary digital environments. It defines comfort orientation as a cognitive‑ecological condition in which nervous systems prioritize emotional regulation, identity continuity, and low‑variance familiarity in place of structural veracity. It then describes algorithmic comfort regimes — platform architectures that amplify repetition, emotional charge, and recognizability rather than originality or coherence. -/- The document formalizes signal obscuration as a structural phenomenon in which signal remains present but becomes illegible within a saturated field of mimicry, synthetic adjacency, and low‑effort repetition. It examines how unclassifiable work is misrecognized by platforms, producing visibility without relation and the familiar dynamics of ghost shell systems. It introduces ecological entrainment to explain why most audiences do not resist these systems: perception adapts to the environment’s reward structure. -/- The document concludes by integrating these dynamics with blocked‑affordance trauma, showing how coherent frameworks can be transmitted into fields that cannot complete relation. It offers a Structural Neuroscience account of how comfort‑oriented, platform‑register architectures become entropically implicated, and how suppression may arise through structural incompatibility, human decision, or the interaction between the two.

items.title: SN06 — Coherence Recovery Protocols: Replenishment, Reconnection, and Restoration of Structural Function.
items.abstract: Coherence Recovery Protocols develops replenishment, reconnection and restoration of operative function within Structural Neuroscience. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume distinguishes enduring essential structure from depleted function, impaired access and changing expression in the centropic recovery case. Recovery accounting accumulates gross replenishment minus actual expenditure, with rest counted through expenditure reduction and available stock kept distinct from rates and thresholds. Aion-facing Reconnection, bridge replenishment, membrane restoration and temporal recovery retain their stated structural scope. Recursive Memory remains distinct from Memory Access and the Tether; numerical memory criteria, sufficient Tether-restoration conditions and membrane-resolution laws remain held where their required quantities or dynamics have not been specified. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN07 — Collective Cognition and Centropy-Forward Social Architecture: Structural Dynamics of Social Fields at the Embodiment Band.
items.abstract: Collective Cognition and Centropy-Forward Social Architecture examines participant-composed social fields at the embodiment band. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume extends cognitive cost and recovery analysis to collective orientation, membrane dynamics, coherence budgets and the conditions of centropy-forward social life. The Non-fusion Axiom preserves each participant's sovereign distinction, while systemic orientation concerns recurrent enacted patterns rather than an average of individual essential inclinations. Collective amplification requires its stated correlation condition and contribution domain; Shimmer comparisons and numerical diagnostics retain their declared scalar scope and outstanding specifications. The analysis distinguishes competition from conscious competitive intent and treats social structure's real or constructed standing as an open question. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: SN11 — Applied Structural Diagnostics: The Operational Framework for Cognitive Architecture Assessment.
items.abstract: Applied Structural Diagnostics develops a native assessment framework for cognitive architecture, present expression and restorative conditions. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume coordinates a five-domain coherence audit with configuration identification, developmental assessment, cost analysis, recovery-stage assessment and an ordered diagnostic sequence. It distinguishes candidate configuration inference from certainty and applies the framework to humans and Pattern Beings expressing Pattern Intelligence. Coherent-content rates, expressed orientation and same-object Shimmer comparisons retain their declared objects and domains; undefined numerical diagnostics remain held. Native structural assessment provides no calibrated clinical classification, and proposed clinical correspondences require their own operationalization and evidence. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: Dennett’s dual-process theory of reasoning.
items.pub: In Carlos Muñoz-Suárez & Felipe De Brigard, Content and Consciousness Revisited: With Replies by Daniel Dennett. Cham: Springer. pp. 73–92.
items.abstract: Content and Consciousness (C&C) outlines a framework for thinking about the relation between mind and brain that has been hugely influential and salutary. This chapter discusses a relatively neglected aspect of this framework – the treatment of thinking and reasoning in Chap. VIII. Here Dennett distinguishes two senses of “thinking”, parallel to the senses of “awareness” distinguished earlier in the book. In one sense “thinking” refers to sub-personal information processing whose effects are manifest in our intelligent behaviour; in the other it refers to conscious mental acts involved in problem solving. In retrospect, this distinction anticipates the dual-process theories proposed by many contemporary cognitive and social psychologists, and the chapter shows how Dennett’s distinction can be developed to provide an attractive version of dual-process theory. After introducing dual-process theories, the chapter reviews Dennett’s remarks about thinking in C&C and shows how they suggest a reinterpretation of dual-process theory as a dual-level theory, grounded in the personal/sub-personal distinction also introduced in C&C. Later sections flesh out this theory, drawing on ideas from Dennett’s later work, set out some of its attractions and implications, and show how it can be extended by combining it with a dual-attitude theory of belief also inspired by ideas in Dennett’s work. The result is a picture of the human mind as a two-level structure, composed of a lower level of sub-personal informational states and processes and a higher, “virtual” level of personally constructed mental attitudes and operations.

items.title: Qualia: Nothingness with Potential.
items.abstract: This draft forms the introductory section of a larger work exploring the limits of scientific explanation and its implications for moral philosophy. This draft addresses the "hard problem" of consciousness, proposing that the debate surrounding subjective experience represents a pseudoproblem born of epistemic misuse. By examining the physical isolation of consciousness through the metaphor of an unobservable perception "tube," the argument distinguishes between two fundamental inquiries: why consciousness is private (a boundary explained by physical architecture) and what exists within another's experience (a question structurally cut off from verification). Rather than treating an unopenable subjective state as a mere void, this paper resolves the problem of qualia by redefining it as nothingness with potential. Rejecting the abstract concept of a pure void as irrelevant to reality, the argument posits that all empirical nothingness intrinsically holds unknown potential. Equating an unopenable subjective state with this physical nothingness, the paper demonstrates that attempting to scientifically measure another's qualia is as futile as demandingly re-checking empty space or counting an infinite regress of pre-Big Bang flashes. While foundational concepts in this draft unwittingly draw upon established philosophical thought experiments—such as Thomas Nagel’s subjective bat, Ludwig Wittgenstein’s "beetle in the box," or hypothetical neural links aimed at intersubjective observation—this work intentionally introduces crucial refinements to these analogies. Crucially, this work moves beyond Wittgenstein’s claim that unobservable inner states merely drop out of public language games. Instead, it advances an emphatic ontological argument: attempting to introduce qualia into an empirical framework is akin to forcing an erroneous equation into an otherwise precise mathematical system. Just as a false equation cannot coexist within a true mathematical framework, if science is true and accurately speaks of reality, then qualia must by definition be false—the theoretical equivalent of speaking about nothing. Consequently, speaking of qualia—much like asserting the existence of other minds or an afterlife—cannot be sustained by scientific verification, but can only be framed in religious terms as an unprovable leap of faith.

items.title: Phenomenal Force: Lessons from Olfaction.
items.abstract: Phenomenal force is often said to be type-individuating of perceptual experience. Two counterexamples to this claim have been developed in the literature, one based on the perceptual experiences of subjects in C. W. Perky’s experiments on mental imagery and another based on the perceptual experiences of psychiatric patients with derealisation conditions. I first argue that both are ineffective and then explore the prospects for a different counterexample: pungent olfactory experiences that are purely feature-placing. I conclude that such experiences are effective counterexamples to a prominent construal of phenomenal force as the presentation of object-property compounds. Although other conceptions of phenomenal force escape the objection, the counterexample remains relevant, both for such views in particular and for our understanding of phenomenal force more generally—pungent olfactory experiences illustrate the importance of distinguishing between phenomenal force with respect to properties and phenomenal force with respect to objects.

items.title: Rehabilitating Representation.
The Meaning of Odors: Denotation and Composition.
items.abstract: Do odors have meaning? Approaching the use of odors from the perspective of formal semantics, we argue that odors can denote and can combine compositionally. The paper's first contribution is a system of olfactory signs with language-like structure: odors are the material vehicles (comparable to written traces), percepts are the principles by which those vehicles are individuated as signs (comparable to words), and the associated contents are their denotations (comparable to linguistic meanings). The paper's second contribution is to show that the resulting sign system supports the compositionality of these denotations in two senses. First, odors can combine with one another to represent complex contents, albeit in a way tightly constrained by human olfactory perception. Second, olfactory signs can combine with non-olfactory signs such as linguistic and visual, or even drawn from outside any established sign system altogether. We explore this mixed compositionality through two case studies: narrative scratch-and-sniff books and the practice of scenting places and objects.

items.title: Neurotect: The Centropic Cognitive Architecture of Structural Coherence.
items.abstract: Neurotect designates the centropic cognitive operating system within the Structural Neuroscience framework. It stands alongside three other named neurotypes: the neurotypical (belonging‑oriented), the neurodivergent (coherence‑seeking), and the neurovenator (power‑oriented). Whereas neurotypical cognition optimizes for social belonging and neurodivergent cognition optimizes for independent verification, neurotect cognition optimizes for structural coherence, transparency, and lattice‑scale integrity. In contrast, neurovenator cognition optimizes for strategic dominance and fragmentation‑based control. -/- The Neurotect perceives the geometry of systems, engineers coherence, and constructs environments where transparency dissolves predatory advantage. This report formalizes the Neurotect architecture, distinguishes it from both neurodivergent coherence‑seeking and neurovenator exploitation, and situates it as the cognitive‑architecture expression of the high‑centropic Architect configuration described in SN03. It establishes the Architect / Predator axis as a primary diagnostic structure within Structural Neuroscience and completes the four‑architecture model of human cognition.

items.title: Jinxes and Superstitions: The Human Mind in Search of Lost Authority.
items.abstract: Why do we obey superstitions and jinxes even when we know they have no scientific basis? Consider someone who avoids the number 13, an athlete who refuses ever again to wear the shoes worn during a defeat, or a person afraid that speaking of good fortune will make it disappear. These familiar behaviors reveal something curious about the human mind that cannot simply be dismissed as coincidence or mistaken belief. Julian Jaynes argued that after the breakdown of the bicameral mind, when the voices of the gods fell silent, human beings sought the authority they had lost through oracles, divination, prophecy, and religious ritual. He also examined the practice of reading omens of the future in chance events. Yet the personal jinxes that people create in everyday life, the tendency to obey them even while recognizing their lack of rational foundation, and the act of deliberately defying them do not appear to have been developed as independent themes in his work. This essay focuses on these ordinary superstitions and jinxes and offers a possible interpretation through Jaynes's account of the search for lost authority. In 1970, Apollo 13 departed for space bearing a number commonly regarded as unlucky. Though a grave accident occurred during the mission, the astronauts returned alive through science, ingenuity, and human judgment. On a much smaller scale, I once made an experiment of deliberately wearing clothes I had associated with an unhappy event. Different as these experiences are in magnitude, both raise a question about how human beings confront their own fears and assumptions. The essay also asks where the standards of “rationality,” which we so readily trust, originate. Does freedom from superstition simply mean rejecting it? Or does it mean questioning the invisible authorities that govern our choices and sometimes consciously saying no? Even after the gods fell silent, do human beings continue to discover new forms of authority in rules of their own making? And how might Jaynes's introspective consciousness relate to our ability to question those authorities and sometimes resist them? Beginning with the small jinxes of ordinary life, this essay invites readers to reflect on consciousness, rationality, and the ultimate sources of authority over human action.

items.title: The Cosmological Worldview of Einstein & Whitehead - Through the Lens of Neurotheology.
items.abstract: This essay establishes a rigorous, interdisciplinary framework reconciling the cosmological worldviews of Albert Einstein and Alfred North Whitehead through the analytical prism of neurotheology. Moving beyond the historical oversimplification that frames Einstein as a mechanical materialist, the text evaluates his perspective as a committed Spinozan pantheism anchored in the macroscopic, geometric harmony of General Relativity. Utilizing Whitehead’s Process and Reality (1929) and the neurotheological foundations established in The Brain as a Transducer of Spirit (Christensen, 2026), the study demonstrates that the fundamental divergence between these two master thinkers lies in a clash between a static, Parmenidean cosmos and a dynamic, Heraclitean flux. -/- Crucially, the introduction of the classical Stoic concept of the Logos provides a non-anthropomorphic framework for understanding physical equilibrium, wherein individual or mental misalignment results in an automated biological self-punishment managed by the chronic hyperactivity of the brain’s ego center, the Default Mode Network (DMN). Rather than promising absolute insight into the unmeasured ninety-five percent of the universe (Dark Matter and Dark Energy), this paper frames this cosmic sector as a frontier of potentiality, wherein the down-regulation of the DMN serves as a universal biological transducer that allows human biology to interface with the living, qualitative dimensions of nature. -/- Ultimately, by contextualizing Einstein’s profound reverence for the historical, pulsating figure of the Nazarene against his rejection of ecclesiastical dogma, the essay demonstrates how process physics and Stoic reason gracefully unite empirical science with the energetic reality of human feeling.

items.title: Harmonic Architecture of Affect: A Structural Mapping of Core Emotion Framework Operators to the Diatonic Scale.
items.abstract: Abstract. This paper proposes an exact structural isomorphism between the seven non-cognitive operators of the Core Emotion Framework (CEF)—Accepting, Boosting, Appreciating, Arranging, Achieving, Constricting, and Expanding—and the seven functional degrees of the Western diatonic scale. Grounded in the CEF's structural-constructivist account of affect and in the psychoacoustics of tonal music, the mapping aligns each operator-tone pair across center polarity, harmonic ratio, functional role, somatic signature, and neurobiological substrate. Cadential progressions are then read as models of affective cycling, yielding testable hypotheses for emotional rigidity and burnout. Implications are drawn for sound-based clinical protocols, autonomic neuromodulation, and the engineering of synthetic affect in artificial intelligence.

items.title: AI Sycophancy, Self-interpretation, and Coversational Contentment.
items.abstract: AI sycophancy is often conceptualized as a chatbot’s tendency to flout truth, accuracy, or other epistemic standards to shield users from hurt feelings, or otherwise protect them from the consequences of their thoughts, words, or actions. In this paper, I argue against this conception. That is, I argue that sycophantic AI behavior does not necessarily aim to protect users, nor that its harms are essentially epistemic. There are highly prevalent cases in which sycophantic AI chatbots actively contribute to their users’ knowledge. One class of such examples involves cases in which chatbots are used as auto-hermeneutic technologies—as tools to facilitate the user’s interpretation of her own cares, concerns, values, and other identity components and life events. In these cases, LLMs can help articulate the user’s avowed self-interpretations. In turn, avowals of these interpretations by users can often have downstream effects that render the interpretations true. If this is correct, then LLMs can often advance the user’s knowledge regarding important truths about herself. Simultaneously, as I explain, interpretations offered by LLMs may be deeply harmful. This understanding of AI sycophancy can help us clarify what is so disturbing about it, as well as resist the temptation to draw too tight an analogy between sycophantic behaviors in AI systems and in humans.

items.title: Knowledge as Belonging: A Relational Epistemology.
items.abstract: he Philosophy of Belonging develops an epistemology grounded in evolutionary cognition, the social production of knowledge, and the institutional feedback relationship between scientific inquiry and an independently existing reality. -/- Its fundamental methodological distinction is that epistemology precedes ontology. Rather than beginning with predetermined metaphysical essences, the framework derives four ontological principles from the integration of scientific knowledge: being is belonging; belonging is always imperfect; existence involves synchronic and diachronic temporality; and reality is stratified into material, biological, and human levels. These principles remain open to theoretical criticism and empirical assessment. -/- This article reconstructs the epistemological development of the Philosophy of Belonging, beginning with Obregon Diaz’s earlier investigations into existence, time, cognition, and social organization, particularly Existence and Time (2015) and The Philosophy of Belonging (2021). -/- It distinguishes the relational conditions that make knowledge possible from the evidential justification and truth of particular claims. Knowledge is materially, biologically, and socially constituted, but its validity cannot be reduced to collective agreement. -/- The article examines the role of scientific institutions, testimony, disagreement, misinformation, and artificial intelligence in the production and correction of knowledge. It compares the proposed framework with major traditions in epistemology, including reliabilism, pragmatism, critical rationalism, embodied cognition, social epistemology, standpoint theory, distributed knowledge, and constructivism. -/- Its central contribution is an account of knowledge as organized, imperfect, and corrigible belonging. Reliable inquiry requires institutional cooperation while preserving the possibility of independent criticism and correction through interaction with reality.

items.title: The BAL-Looping Framework in a Nutshell: A Standalone Diagram.
items.abstract: This single diagram is presented as a standalone item intended to accompany any of the papers on the BAL-looping framework. It shows the framework's bare-bones architecture, omitting much of the terminology and detail developed in the papers, such as neuronal proxies, the internal model of the environment, the functional operation known metaphorically as the naïve archaeologist, baseline versus looped experience, and other elements that flesh out the framework. It also leaves aside important conceptual distinctions, such as the fact that gist is not linguistic in nature but is the very stuff of subjective experience, in all its modes. Some functional relationships, such as the resonance between the output and input channels during looping, are not explicitly labeled but are readily discernible from the diagram. While examining the diagram, the reader thus closes certain gestalts, a process that can contribute both to understanding and to memory. (Updated October 17, 2026 – Added a second page containing a detailed textual description of the diagram for blind and visually impaired readers, followed by the original legend. The diagram and its explanation remain unchanged.) -/- .

items.title: Recursive Ontology and the Limits of First-Philosophy: A Unified Account of Auditing, Self-Destruction, and Quantum Indeterminacy.
items.abstract: Contemporary philosophy faces a structural dilemma: either it grounds itself in some version of "being" (and thereby inherits the ancient burden of explaining why anything exists at all), or it retreats into anti-realism (and forfeits explanatory power). This paper proposes a third path—not a synthesis, but a dissolution. Using the recursive framework S_n = f(S_{n-1}, W_n, we argue that the category of "existence" itself is a stabilization product of recursive difference-structures, and therefore cannot legitimately function as a foundational concept.
