Third, given a reasonable account of different functions of justification within commonplace epistemic and legal contexts, knowledge is not needed to explain the features of beliefs that matter to their justifiability. Lastly, fourth, KNJ defenders’ attempts to appropriate the normative category of excuse to explain away intuitions about justifiable non-knowledge beliefs fail because they are either ad hoc, normatively indiscriminating, or otherwise incapable of accurately accounting for the extent of excusable beliefs. -/- I respond to the first three issues by leveraging Littlejohn’s identification of the hypological and deontic senses of justification. In doing so I highlight how this identification, which I call DHJ-i, not only grants knowledge an explanatory advantage over other epistemic variables in accommodating this identification but that it does so in a manner that affords the KNJ defender three distinct further advantages over the KNJ denier. First, DHJ-i gives knowledge conceptual work to do that throws into question the method, often reserved for KNJ deniers, of solely relying on intuitions about how to assess the justifiability of belief in a case-by-case basis (case-based intuitions about justified belief). Second, DHJ-i helps clarify for defenders a viable defence of the use of a more (KNJ)-friendly notion of rationality as the standard of norm-following doxastic behaviour, either as belief or belief suspension. Third, defenders can employ DHJ-i to reasonably argue that some (KNJ)-antagonistic positions, such as taking justification to have either a non-factive norm or no one individual norm at all, attain problematic normative ramifications even within some commonplace epistemic and legal contexts. -/- I respond to the fourth issue by motivating (KNJ)-friendly modifications to Williamson’s derivative norms framework (DNF). These modifications accomplish two things. First, they differentiate between the normative categories of excuse and exemption without sneaking in unwanted internalist assumptions about this difference. Second, they locate an agent’s following of the appropriate knowledge-derived norms within cases that the KNJ defender would also want to find excusable beliefs in. Moreover, in relation to this issue and for a broader purpose, I address an intriguing tension in the overall dialectic of the debate between KNJ defenders and deniers concerning excuse and justification. Basically, when making precise the dialectic between, on one hand, models of conditions for justification and excuse, and on the other, their counterexamples, there is good reason to suppose that the KNJ denier can eke out a small victory over the defender regarding their intuitions about the right sufficient conditions for justification rather than excuse. -/- Overall, the conclusion I draw from my thesis is twofold. On one hand, there are theoretically motivated grounds to consider the KNJ defender as having the upper hand against the KNJ denier, but only if knowledge’s explanatory advantage in accommodating DHJ-i is normatively probative enough to surpass the value of sticking to the denier’s more traditional case-based intuitions about justification. On the other hand, there are dialectically motivated grounds favouring the KNJ denier over the defender, since, on balance, intuitions against justified belief having a knowledge norm are dialectically advantaged over both intuitions for there being such a norm and intuitions that seek to explain these KNJ-antagonistic intuitions away.

items.title: Spatiotemporally Distributed Monetary Dissolution in AI Production Networks: A Thought Experiment on Future Production Relations.
items.abstract: This discussion paper investigates a conditional possibility of spatiotemporally distributed monetary dissolution within a hypothetical production economy operated predominantly by highly capable artificial-intelligence systems. Productive labour is assumed to be widely automatable, while material scarcity, differentiated authority over resources, and heterogeneous institutional commitments remain. The paper distinguishes debt cancellation, the expiry of particular claims, substitution of monetary functions, reduction in reliance on general purchasing power, and disappearance of a monetary institution. Its central hypothesis is that locally coordinated value circuits may sustain productive activities through resource-specific commitments, shared capacities, distributed records, and admissible multilateral settlement, progressively displacing some uses of money without a synchronized economy-wide transition. This possibility faces difficulties of overlapping circuits, nonlinear dynamics, contested value attribution, conflicting normative and aesthetic appraisals, trust-dependent bottlenecks, and concentrated power over both resources and governance protocols. An optimistic branch considers jointly accessible production data and substantially enhanced AI capacities for system identification and adaptive planning, without presupposing complete prediction or normative consensus. Drawing critically on generative justice, monetary theory, and commons governance, the study treats non-extractive value return and the regeneration of productive conditions as distinct tests of an institutional arrangement's significance. Monetary dissolution is consequently presented as a localized, reversible and normatively contingent transformation in production relations.

items.title: Generative Relational Economics, Volume VI: Artificial Intelligence, Domains, and Economic Order.
items.abstract: This volume examines the implications of artificial intelligence and radical capability asymmetry for economic relations and extends Generative Relational Economics across a range of substantive domains before developing an integrated account of economic order. Artificial intelligence is analyzed as a potential source of large and persistent asymmetries in productive, epistemic, symbolic, and organizational capability. The volume considers artificial productive capacity, labor, ownership, surplus, redistribution, participation, subjecthood, epistemic dependence, research orientation, governance, and long-horizon human–AI relations. Capability asymmetry is not treated as intrinsically equivalent to domination; the analysis instead asks how asymmetry becomes coupled to ownership, dependence, institutional authority, access, exclusion, or generative participation. The framework is then translated into domains including education, research and knowledge institutions, work and organizations, development and humanitarian practice, welfare, communities and commons, platforms, public infrastructure, migration, ecology, and symbolic economy. Domain translation is used to test both the usefulness and the limits of GRE rather than to absorb neighboring disciplines into economics. Comparative domain inquiry provides the basis for an analysis of generative relational economic order. Economic order is examined through institutional capacity, allocation, value circulation, dependency, participation, contestability, temporal sustainability, epistemic conditions, and revisability. The volume thereby connects technological transformation and domain-specific analysis to broader questions concerning the constitution and governance of economic order.

items.title: Individuum und Gesellschaft aus Sicht der Einheitsbildungstheorie.
items.abstract: Die vorliegende Untersuchung entwickelt eine genetisch-rekonstruktive Erklärung des Verhältnisses von Individuum und Gesellschaft auf der Grundlage der Einheitsbildungstheorie. Ihr Ausgangspunkt ist die erkenntnistheoretische These, dass weder Individuum noch Gesellschaft als voraussetzungslos gegebene Einheiten verstanden werden können, sondern ihre Bestimmbarkeit Prozesse der Differenzierung, Relevanzbildung, Relationierung, Integration und Stabilisierung voraussetzt. Das Individuum wird dabei als Medium einer fortlaufenden Wirklichkeitsbildung begriffen, in der unter den Wirkungen einer unabhängig bestehenden Realität eine Ordnung stabilisierter Einheiten und Beziehungen entsteht, die Orientierung, Erwartung und Handeln ermöglicht. Die Untersuchung unterscheidet zwischen dem genetisch ursprünglicheren Erfahrungsverstehen, in dem affektive Hervorhebung und emotionale Gewichtung die Bildung von Relevanzen ermöglichen, und dem darauf aufbauenden Denkverstehen, das bereits organisierte Erfahrungszusammenhänge begrifflich transformiert, expliziert und seinerseits auf die weitere Erfahrungsbildung zurückwirkt. Auf dieser Grundlage wird die Entstehung sozialer Wirklichkeit als rekursiver Zusammenhang individueller und gesellschaftlicher Einheitsbildungen rekonstruiert. Individuelle Orientierungen werden durch Kommunikation aufeinander bezogen und können sich in gemeinsamen Erwartungen, sprachlichen Ordnungen, Normen und Institutionen gesellschaftlich stabilisieren, während diese gesellschaftlichen Einheitsbildungen ihrerseits die Bedingungen weiterer individueller Orientierung vorstrukturieren. Eine besondere Bedeutung erhält dabei die genetische Unterscheidung zwischen Selektion, Durchsetzung und Macht: Während Selektion die unterschiedliche Anschlusswirksamkeit möglicher Einheitsbildungen und Durchsetzung die Wirksamkeit einer Möglichkeit unter konkurrierenden Möglichkeiten bezeichnet, entstehen Machtverhältnisse erst dort, wo die Einwirkungsmöglichkeiten auf Bedingungen fremder Wirkungs-, Handlungs- und Entscheidungsmöglichkeiten asymmetrisch verteilt sind. Gesellschaftliche Macht erscheint damit weder als ursprüngliches Lebensprinzip noch als allgemeine Eigenschaft individueller Wirksamkeit, sondern als relational gebildete und institutionell stabilisierbare Ordnung asymmetrischer Einflussmöglichkeiten. Die Untersuchung zeigt ferner, dass gesellschaftliche Übereinkunft nicht die Aufhebung individueller Wirklichkeitsbildung bedeutet, sondern aus der kommunikativen Abstimmung unterschiedlicher individueller Orientierungen hervorgeht und grundsätzlich revisionsfähig bleibt. Freiheit wird entsprechend als bedingte Möglichkeit alternativer Einheitsbildung bestimmt, während Aufklärung die kritische Reflexion jener Erfahrungs-, Relevanz- und Begriffsbildungen einschließt, auf denen individuelle Urteile und gesellschaftliche Ordnungen beruhen. Die Unterscheidung zwischen Wirklichkeit und Realität begrenzt dabei jeden Anspruch, aus gesellschaftlicher Durchsetzung, allgemeiner Übereinkunft oder wissenschaftlicher Bewährung unmittelbar auf die ontologische Beschaffenheit der unabhängig bestehenden Realität schließen zu können. Als zentrales Ergebnis erweist sich Gesellschaft als dynamische, rekursive Ordnung stabilisierter und veränderbarer Einheitsbildungen, deren Entstehung, Fortbestand und Revision auf individuelle Orientierungsleistungen angewiesen bleiben, ohne auf diese reduzierbar zu sein. Objektivität entsteht in diesem Zusammenhang nicht durch die Überwindung individueller Perspektivität, sondern durch organisationsübergreifende Verfahren der Vergleichbarkeit, Prüfung, Bewährung und Korrektur.

items.title: Reality = Existence = Being: Without an Ultimate Reality.
items.abstract: Reality, existence, and being are commonly treated as separate philosophical questions. Reality is asked about as what is real, existence as the fact of being, and being as the fundamental condition of what is. This separation can be useful for conceptual investigation, but it can also create an ontological division that may not exist in what is itself. -/- This paper proposes the formulation Reality = Existence = Being. The equation does not establish a single substance, a final foundation, or an ultimate reality. It expresses a simpler recognition: reality, existence, and being can be understood as different conceptual recognitions of what is. -/- At the same time, this formulation does not lead to the conclusion that there is an ultimate reality behind existence. There is no final reality waiting to be discovered beyond what exists. Reality does not stand behind existence, existence does not point toward a final metaphysical layer, and being does not become a hidden substance underlying everything. -/- What exists can be investigated without assuming that investigation must eventually arrive at an ultimate ground. Reality has no final conceptual endpoint. It has depth, expression, relation, movement, and further possibility of recognition. -/- Thus, Reality = Existence = Being is not a theory of an ultimate reality. It is an attempt to remove unnecessary separation while keeping existence open.

items.title: Branch-Indexed Millianism: Coreferential Homonyms, Referential Routes, and the Cognitive Significance of Identity Statements.
items.abstract: Frege's puzzle and Kripke's puzzle about belief are often taken to show that a purely referential theory of proper names cannot account for the cognitive significance of identity statements and the rationality of apparently contradictory beliefs. This paper develops an externalist version of Millianism that distinguishes semantic content from the cognitive organization through which a referent is accessed. The central proposal is that a name use is governed by an \emph{effective causal-informational branch}: a socially and historically sustained route of reference characterized by a relatively stable identifying basis, correction practices, and information flow. Two uses of the same linguistic form can therefore be governed by distinct effective branches even when they refer to the same object. I call such cases \emph{coreferential homonymy}. -/- The theory does not identify a branch with a description or with a private mental representation. Identifying predicates and descriptions are evidence for the structure of a branch, but they are not semantic determinants of reference. Two branches count as distinct not merely when their associated descriptions differ, but when they provide independently sufficient means of identifying the same object and are not effectively cross-coordinated. This gives a principled response to the objection that every individual token would otherwise generate a new name. It also clarifies the relation between coreferential homonymy and mental files. Distinct branches can sustain distinct files, but files may remain distinct after an identity has been learned, because learning an identity can link previously independent files without eliminating their historical bases. -/- The paper applies the view to Frege's Hesperus-Phosphorus puzzle and to Kripke's Pierre case. In both cases, the relevant cognitive achievement is not the acquisition of a new Russellian proposition. It is the discovery or establishment that two previously independent identifying routes concern one and the same object. Branch-indexed Millianism thus preserves direct reference while offering an externalist account of cognitive significance. The view is contrasted with Nathan Salmon's implicature theory, which locates cognitive significance in pragmatics rather than in the external structure of reference.

items.title: The Ontology of Latent Capacity, Importance, Actualization, and Future Possibility.
items.abstract: This article develops an ontology of latent capacity as a neglected dimension of importance. Its central claim is that the importance of an entity cannot be adequately determined by examining only its presently actualized functions. An entity can be important because its condition preserves the possibility of future configurations within the relational field in which it participates. Importance therefore concerns a temporal and relational structure connecting present actuality, latent capacity, and future reconfigurability. The argument begins by distinguishing actualized function from latent capacity. Actualized function concerns what an entity presently does within an established configuration. Latent capacity concerns the transformations that remain structurally accessible through the entity under altered conditions. The distinction becomes philosophically decisive when present functioning and future reconfigurability diverge. A structure can continue performing its established function while progressively losing the capacity to reorganize when existing conditions become inadequate. Such a condition constitutes a form of ontological erosion that remains invisible when assessment is restricted to present performance. The article develops importance as a relational property grounded in constitutive consequence. Causal consequence concerns what an alteration produces within an existing configuration. Constitutive consequence concerns whether an alteration changes the conditions under which further transformations can occur. Importance becomes philosophically significant when alteration affects the future reconfigurability of a field. This account distinguishes importance from value, significance, mattering, and immediate causal efficacy while explaining their possible intersections. The article then examines the ontological status of latent capacity, arguing that capacity is real when an existing organization materially or structurally conditions a range of future transformations. Reconfigurative capacity is distinguished from ordinary adaptation because it concerns the transformation of the organization through which future responses become possible. Meta-capacity designates the preservation and regeneration of conditions through which further capacities can emerge. The argument engages Aristotle, Kant, Heidegger, Whitehead, Simondon, Dewey, Jonas, Levinas, and Nussbaum. These traditions provide important resources for understanding potentiality, temporality, process, individuation, practical judgment, responsibility, and capability. The article argues that the specific relation among present alteration, latent capacity, constitutive importance, and future reconfigurability remains insufficiently articulated within these approaches individually. The resulting account contributes to Niami’s broader ontology of Finite Continuance. Finite beings persist through constitutive exchange and erosion. Their continuance depends upon the preservation and regeneration of capacities through which further configurations can emerge. Importance therefore acquires its deepest ontological meaning where present conditions affect the future capacity of a field to remain transformable. Keywords: latent capacity, importance, future possibility, actualization, potentiality, reconfiguration, meta-capacity, relational ontology, erosion, Finite Continuance.

items.title: The Ontology of Refusal, Saying No as a Mechanism of Finite Continuance.
items.abstract: This article develops an ontological account of refusal within the philosophical framework of Finite Continuance. It argues that saying no can be understood as a structurally significant operation through which a finite being regulates constitutive exchange and preserves its future capacity for reconfiguration. Refusal is commonly interpreted through ethical, political, psychological, or juridical categories such as autonomy, resistance, consent, opposition, withdrawal, or self-assertion. The present account locates refusal at a more fundamental level. A finite being exists through continuous exchange with its environment, while the same exchange can progressively diminish the capacities required for further transformation. Refusal therefore acquires ontological significance when it interrupts a mode of exchange whose continuation would reduce the subject’s capacity to reorganize itself. The article develops five connected claims. First, constitutive exchange is a condition of finite existence and therefore cannot simply be eliminated. Second, constitutive exchange possesses an erosive dimension because every finite relation can consume time, attention, energy, affective resources, interpretive capacity, institutional access, or future possibilities. Third, refusal regulates this exchange by establishing a limit upon what may enter, leave, demand, occupy, or determine a finite system. Fourth, the value of refusal depends upon its effect on reconfigurative capacity. Refusal becomes philosophically significant when it preserves the possibility of future transformation. Fifth, refusal has an ethical and political dimension because institutions and social systems can systematically appropriate the capacity to refuse. The article distinguishes ontological refusal from avoidance, rigidity, domination, selfishness, and simple negation. It also examines the relation between refusal and Heideggerian finitude, Sartrean freedom, Levinasian responsibility, Simondonian individuation, Whiteheadian process, Foucauldian power, and contemporary accounts of autonomy and capability. The resulting conception defines refusal as a regulated limitation of constitutive exchange undertaken for the preservation of future reconfigurative capacity. Refusal thereby becomes a mechanism of finite continuance and a central component of an Ethics of Sufficiency. Keywords: Finite Continuance, refusal, refusal capacity, constitutive exchange, erosion, reconfiguration, future agency, Dynamic Mask, Ethics of Sufficiency, capacity for otherwise, political economy of erosion.

items.title: Relational Experientialism.
items.abstract: Experientialism is a family of philosophical theories of well-being that tie well-being to experiencing certain positively charged experiences. Experientialism has fallen out of favor today because of Robert Nozick’s experience machine objection. According to this objection, experientialism must allow that there is no difference between living well in reality and living well in a plausible computer simulation, because the experiences would be identical in both cases. This article proposes a theory that avoids this objection: relational experientialism. According to this position, well-being is experiencing certain positively charged experiences, but only when those experiences are caused by the realization of some genuine objective good. This version of experientialism avoids the experience machine objection and also has a number of explanatory advantages over the dominant theory of well-being today: naturalistic perfectionism. In particular, relational experientialism does a better job of explaining the nature of the motivation to pursue objective goods, as well as the asymmetry between conscious and unconscious entities. It also does a better job of addressing the challenge of the “flourishing anhedone” – a person who realizes genuine goods in their life but has no positive experiences at all. Such a person’s life, despite the presence of objective goods, is hardly a happy one, but only relational experientialism can explain why this is so. In addition, relational experientialism is most consistent with relationism about phenomenal consciousness. This is the view that the phenomenal character of experience is constituted by the relational properties of external objects, and that the experience of real perceptions is therefore phenomenally distinct from the experience of illusions and hallucinations. All of these considerations suggest that relational experientialism is, at least as a first approximation, a plausible theory of well-being.

items.title: Our Teleological Selves.
John Grote and the Promise of “Knowledge of Acquaintance”.
items.pub: In Arnaud Dewalque, Bruno Leclercq, Valentina Martinis, Jacopo Pallagrosi & Denis Seron, The Cambridge Family: British Philosophy of Mind at the Turn of the Twentieth Century. Routledge.
items.abstract: The notion of knowledge by acquaintance is associated primarily with Bertrand Russell. Interestingly, however, it is anticipated in the mid-19th-century by the philosopher John Grote’s distinction between “knowledge of acquaintance” and “knowledge of judgment.” Here I argue that Grote’s notion is actually superior to Russell’s in avoiding certain philosophical difficulties that afflict the latter, especially as concerns the alleged total passivity of knowledge-by-acquaintance and the claim that we enjoy knowledge-by-acquaintance of universals.

items.title: A History of Consciousness — From the Voices of the Gods to the Emergence of the “I,” and on to AI.
items.abstract: “If people 3,000 years ago did not have consciousness like ours today, how did they think?” This paper began with a conversation with a friend. Julian Jaynes’s theory does more than propose the provocative hypothesis that ancient people did not possess consciousness in the same form that we do today; it also forces us to reconsider what we mean by the word “consciousness,” which we use so casually. Here, “consciousness” does not simply mean being awake, or having the capacity to see and feel. What concerned Jaynes was an inward form of consciousness in which we possess a point of view—an “I”—within the mind, mentally traverse the past and future, and reflect on ourselves. This paper first considers the relationship between what appears in consciousness and the nonconscious processes operating behind it, using concepts such as Jaynes’s bicameral mind, mind-space, and the analog “I.” In the second half, I extend the questions raised by Jaynes and consider, through five aspects—subjectivity, time, causality, possibility, and meaning—how the emergence of this inward form of consciousness allows the world to be experienced as “my world.” These five aspects are not intended as a summary of Jaynes’s theory itself. Rather, they are an attempt, starting from his ideas, to explore in my own way the workings and possibilities of consciousness. Finally, I ask whether human consciousness in its present form was an inevitable outcome of evolution, or merely one of several possible forms of cognition, and consider the possibility that AI may one day develop toward a form of consciousness different from our own.

items.title: Relational Positions in Volunteer Aid: A Preliminary Psychoanalytic Formalization.
items.abstract: This paper develops a preliminary psychoanalytic formalization of relational positioning in volunteer, aid, and support relations within Generative Relational Theory (GR). It studies how participants may encounter concrete historical subjects through expectation-laden positions that organize functions, anticipated continuations, confirmation conditions, frustration conditions, and revision routes. Papers I–III already provide the historical-relational substrate: tracked subjects, support roles, self-reconstruction, recognition, path dependence, provenance, and subject co-formation. Paper IV adds a separate claim-grade architecture for increasingly theory-dependent interpretation. It distinguishes manifest aid events, participant reconstructions, relational-position inferences, source-specific psychoanalytic structural hypotheses, dynamic-contribution attributions, and comparatively demanding attributions of unconscious contribution. The framework separates support-relevant need from relational address, desire hypotheses from ordinary requests, relational tension from psychoanalytic lack, recurrence from psychoanalytic repetition, and the concrete other from the function assigned within a relational position. Disconfirmation events—including refusal, independent success, transfer, altered need, and loss of expected recognition—provide comparative evidence about position revision, position-restorative pressure, and the incremental explanatory contribution of stronger hypotheses. Freudian, Lacanian, relational, intersubjective, and object-relational resources enter as source-specific interpretive interfaces under ontological suspension and competing-explanation discipline. The resulting architecture supports analysis of helper identification, rescue configurations, recognition mismatch, separation, alterity tolerance, coupled positioning, institutional reinforcement, rupture, and later reorganization while preserving material, institutional, normative, interpersonal, and historical explanations as independently typed contributors.

items.title: Ethics of Aid, Volunteering, and Support under Heterogeneous Subject Conditions: Subjectivity Uncertainty, Recognition, and Revisable Assistance.
items.abstract: Ethical assistance is often discussed as if the identity, interests, communicative capacities, and moral standing of the recipient were sufficiently settled before practical deliberation begins. Cases involving heterogeneous subjects weaken that assumption. Human beings with atypical communicative access, nonhuman animals, artificial systems, and hypothetical alien subjects may present different evidence of adversity, different forms of agency, and different grounds for moral considerability. Building on a prior Generative Relational account of support-relevant recognition, this paper develops a preliminary ethics of aid, volunteering, and support under such uncertainty. Its central proposal is that ethical assessment should preserve the provenance of recognition, distinguish uncertainty about adverse states from uncertainty about moral status and normative theory, and evaluate assistance through typed constraints on benefit, harm, communicative engagement, autonomy, dependency, helper burden, third-party effects, and revisability. The framework treats revisable assistance as a design property of ethical response under incomplete knowledge: interventions should, where the relevant reasons support it, remain monitorable, contestable, corrigible, and capable of responsible withdrawal or repair. Human, animal, artificial, and hypothetical alien cases function as heterogeneous stress tests across different evidential, agential, communicative, and relational conditions. The paper remains within normative ethics; humanitarian doctrine, legal standing, adjudicative authority, and institutional responsibility are reserved for subsequent work.

items.title: Studies in the Philosophy of Language (4): Contextual Super-Existence and Indirect Speech Acts.
items.abstract: Face-to-face linguistic communication is not a closed process consisting solely of an Expressor, a Receiver, and linguistic content. Every actual communicative exchange takes place within a particular environment, which directly affects the meaning and appropriateness of linguistic expressions as well as the Receiver's understanding of what is expressed. Accordingly, in addition to the various forms of Super-Existence associated with the Expressor and the Receiver individually, linguistic communication involves a form of Super-Existence relevant to both participants. This chapter calls it Contextual Super-Existence, which may also be termed Situational Super-Existence when emphasis is placed on the concrete circumstances of an interaction. This chapter first examines the fundamental role of Contextual Super-Existence in linguistic communication, arguing that the appropriateness of an expression cannot be determined independently of the particular situation in which it occurs. The same sentence may have entirely different degrees of appropriateness, and even different practical meanings, in different situations. Drawing on John Searle's theory of indirect speech acts, the chapter then analyzes the relationship between an Expressor's literal utterance, underlying intention, and Purpose Super-Existence, using the example “It's very cold.” It further argues that whether the Receiver acts in accordance with the Expressor's actual intention depends not only on the Receiver's understanding of the linguistic content but also on Contextual Super-Existence, including the participants' current activities, their relationship, the physical environment, and other relevant background conditions. The chapter thus seeks to demonstrate that linguistic meaning does not reside entirely within linguistic expressions themselves. Rather, meaning emerges from the dynamic relations among the Expressor, the linguistic expression, the Receiver, and Contextual Super-Existence.

items.title: Agency and Consciousness.
items.abstract: Agency and Consciousness proposes a functional architecture of agency and consciousness. It argues that both are emergent architectures that appear when sufficiently complex systems integrate resilient memory, limited perception, internal simulation, and self-modeling. -/- Memory is not an archive of the past but the present physical state of a system shaped by prior interactions. Perception does not capture reality in full but only the fraction accessible to the agent's architecture. On that incomplete information, the system builds approximate simulations of its environment and of itself through what this work calls intelligent bias. Consciousness appears when the system incorporates its own state within its internal simulation, and subjective experience is presented as a consequence of a structural asymmetry between internal modeling and external observation. -/- The work introduces a partition between architectural dominance and the zone of functional indifference: when the evaluation differential between trajectories exceeds the system's basal noise, the decision belongs to the architecture; when it does not, the resolution is contingent. Agency resides in the strategy; the openness of the future, in the execution. -/- The position defended is relational: agency is not a property exclusive to the universe nor to the agent, but a property that emerges when a sufficiently complex architecture operates on a sufficiently stratified ontology. The work builds on the three-level architecture developed in Destiny and Will and engages with Metzinger's self-model theory, Friston and Clark's predictive processing, and simulation theory in philosophy of mind. It does not aim to resolve the strong phenomenological problem of subjective experience; its objective is more limited: to describe the minimal architectural conditions compatible with the existence of real agency and functional forms of consciousness. -/- This entry includes the English version and its Spanish original.

items.title: Attention and the Relevance Problem.
items.abstract: The relevance problem is the problem of how cognitive systems can be sensitive to what is relevant despite relevance being holistic, open-ended, and context-sensitive. The problem has typically been applied to higher-order cognitive processes. In this paper, I argue that there is a hitherto unrecognized relevance problem for perceptual attention. This problem becomes apparent when considering the functions of attention: attention must not only support ongoing task performance but also remain sensitive to opportunities for task switching, latent learning, and context checking. Existing treatments of the relevance problem have largely focused on its task-relative form: given a task, what is relevant? I argue that attention faces a more general problem that includes sensitivity to factors relevant to other interests and to cues indicating that another activity may be worth pursuing. For such features of the environment to stand out as salient, salience cannot be determined solely by bottom-up factors and a limited set of occurrent top-down factors, such as current goals and intentions. Rather, it must reflect the wider (if not the entire) range of an agent's latent interests in a context-sensitive way. This motivational unencapsulation of attention poses a challenge for both contemporary accounts of attention and suggests that passive attention is much more intelligent than commonly thought. -/- .

items.title: Thinking with Objects. Understanding Non-Representational Cognitive Artifacts.
items.abstract: This paper defends the notion of cognitive artifacts that do not serve representational functions. Contrary to the standard account of cognitive artifacts as representational, we argue that it is possible to distinguish a special class of artifacts that fulfill cognitive roles without performing representational functions. With reference to cognitive semiotics, we respond to Fasoli’s critique of ecological cognitive artifacts, which were defined as non-representational by Heersmink. First, cognitive semiotics identifies key features of the representational relation. This relation arises through interactions between the object and the user. It requires the user to appreciate the duality between expression and content. Second, cognitive semiotics distinguishes between reality and pictorial modes of experiencing artifacts. We apply this framework to explore what happens when an artifact is experienced in reality mode: situations in which its representational function is disregarded by the user, or in which the artifact has no representational function to begin with. Based on three examples from the literature (file structure visualization, hotel key weight, and intelligent use of space), we propose a class of cognitive artifacts that can be meaningful in a technical sense with respect to users’ cognitive goals and needs, even if the artifacts are not carriers of representations or their representational functions are not recognized as such.

items.title: Null Monism : Why Qualia Arise from Nothing.
items.abstract: A persistent intuition that motivates panpsychism — thereby generating the combination problem — holds that parts lacking experience cannot combine to produce a whole that has it. We argue that this intuition rests on an unexamined assumption: that phenomenological contents compose by a null-preserving operation. We show that any composition rule adequate to preserve the structural sensitivity of experience generates non-null composites from null parts. Qualitative character turns out to be nesting topology — forced by the formalism, not assumed. An argument from physical anchoring connects the set-theoretic result to the physical world, revealing that nesting topology is causal topology, and showing that wherever causal organisation closes into an irreducible whole, qualia become a logical necessity. In the discussion we draw out what follows once the null-preservation assumption is dropped, for panpsychism and the explanatory gap. Crucially, the argument begins from the methodological assumption that elementary parts carry no phenomenological content — which means panpsychism is not required.

items.title: The Living Corpus and the Rosarian Rite of Sacred Structure.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: THE LIVING CORPUS AND THE ROSARIAN RITE OF SACRED STRUCTURE Published by the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves, First Table of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship, beneath the Grand Table — Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa, upon Via Solis Sub Rosa — The Way of the Sun Beneath the Rose. The Rosarian Articles constitute a living body of Rosarian composition arising from The Knight Manifesto: A Rosarian Compendium and continuing through interpretation, clarification, symbolism, terminology, philosophy, Fellowship, Table structure, ceremony, custodianship, and lived practice. The Twenty-Two Articles remain the Twenty-Two Articles. They constitute the completed composition of the first established series of Rosarian Articles and remain the foundational composed body through which the Rosarian vocabulary, principles, symbols, Laws, Fellowship, Tables, ceremonies, and custodial responsibilities were brought into correspondence. Article XXII completed that particular composition; it did not declare the Rosarian Way itself complete or prohibit further Rosarian writing, interpretation, or development. The distinction is therefore established between the completed Twenty-Two and the continuing Rosarian corpus. A work arising after the Twenty-Two is not Article XXIII or a numerical continuation of the Twenty-Two. It may nevertheless be a Rosarian Article when it develops, clarifies, interprets, organizes, or establishes a faithful expression of the Way while remaining accountable to what has already been established. The number twenty-two identifies the completed composition and is not an assigned numerical limit upon the living corpus. Later Rosarian Articles therefore do not replace the Twenty-Two, amend them merely by being later, or compete with them for precedence. They continue the process already demonstrated throughout the Rosarian corpus: foundation becoming interpretation, interpretation becoming structure, structure becoming practice, and practice becoming further understanding. The foundation remains the foundation, the Twenty-Two remain the Twenty-Two, later works remain Rosarian Articles, and the Way remains open. This Article is therefore a Rosarian Article in its own right and is published by the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves as the First Table of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship. The First Table does not constitute a superior institution within the Fellowship. Its precedence is historical and custodial. The Dawnist Rosarian Wolves are the First Table beneath the Grand Table, Mensa Rotunda Sub Rosa, and their particular identity does not replace or restrict the universal identity of the Fellowship. The First Table may establish practices and expressions that can be received by other Tables and members when those practices remain consistent with the established Rosarian structure. This Article establishes one such expression as the Rosarian Rite of Sacred Structure. The Rosarian Rite of Sacred Structure is the formal proceeding by which a Rosarian Table Meeting is blessed and sanctified as a unified expression of relationship and connection. It is not a rank, degree, office, separate order, or claim of authority. It is a structure for Table Meetings intended to strengthen the bonds among practitioners and enable those gathered to participate as a connected Circle. The Rite is based upon tone, posture, reference, patience, devotion, inspiration, and Fellowship of the Way. These are practical requirements of participation rather than decorative elements. Tone governs the manner in which practitioners speak and listen. Posture provides a physical discipline corresponding to the movement of the ceremony. Reference keeps the meeting connected to the established Rosarian teachings and symbols. Patience prevents the meeting from becoming dominated by haste or individual control. Devotion maintains attention upon the Way. Inspiration permits the living corpus to continue developing through practice and reflection. Fellowship establishes the relationship between practitioners through which the Table becomes more than a physical gathering. The sanctified condition of the Table Meeting is formally designated Hortus Apertus, the Open Garden. Hortus Apertus is established in direct correspondence with the established Rosarian principle of hortus conclusus, the enclosed garden. Hortus Apertus designates the opening and sanctification of the Table Meeting; hortus conclusus designates its enclosure and completion. These terms describe two conditions of the same sacred structure rather than two separate institutions or ceremonies. When the Table Meeting is constituted according to the Rosarian Rite of Sacred Structure, Hortus Apertus is declared and the meeting becomes a sanctified Circle for the duration of the proceeding. The Twenty-Two Rays are recited while the members kneel and form the Circle. If no member volunteers to hold the proceeding, the Table Holder performs that custodial function. The Table Holder does not thereby become superior to those gathered. The purpose is to maintain the structure and sequence of the Rite. While kneeling, the Silent Mirror is held. Within this Article, the Silent Mirror corresponds with the Silent Sun, representing stillness, receptivity, inward reflection, and the beginning of conscious remembrance. The members then stand and form the Crowned Mirror. The Crowned Mirror corresponds with the Silent Knight, representing awakening carried into discipline, responsibility, restraint, and conscious conduct. The Oath of the Eternal Traveler is then recited, followed by the sacred declaration: BENEDICTIO MILITIS, MILITIA AMORIS, NOSTRI VIDENT CORDE, DESIDERIVM NIHIL GERIT. Thus begins the Way. Following the declaration, the members form the Blooming Heart, which corresponds with the Rosarian Knight and represents awakened understanding brought into conduct, relationship, service, and responsibility. These three correspondences — Silent Mirror with Silent Sun, Crowned Mirror with Silent Knight, and Blooming Heart with Rosarian Knight — are established here as a new Rosarian interpretation and synthesis of the existing signs and Prism. They are not ranks or stages of human worth and are not to be used to establish hierarchy among practitioners. The Rosarian Prism remains a circulation of consciousness and practice rather than a ladder of superiority. During the Table Meeting, all members remain standing and holding the Blooming Heart. The members stand toe-to-toe in the Circle, maintaining the physical formation as an expression of connection and shared participation. The Circle constitutes the sanctuary of the Table Meeting, and what is spoken within the meeting is held under the Rose. The purpose of the formation is practical: practitioners are gathered into one structure so that the meeting is experienced as a relationship rather than merely as separate individuals occupying the same place. The Rosarian Rite of Sacred Structure does not require practitioners to surrender individuality or conscience. Its purpose is to establish a common form through which individual practitioners can participate together, strengthen their bonds, and move as one in the context of the Way. The Blooming Heart remains held throughout the meeting as the common sign of this participation. When the meeting has reached its conclusion, the Table Holder or a volunteer recites the Twenty-Two Petals while the members remain holding the Blooming Heart. The members then kneel together and form the Crowned Mirror. The Crowned Mirror is brought down through the common act of kneeling, establishing humility and equality among those present. The Oath of the Eternal Traveler is recited again. The Silent Mirror is then formed while the sacred declaration is spoken again: BENEDICTIO MILITIS, MILITIA AMORIS, NOSTRI VIDENT CORDE, DESIDERIVM NIHIL GERIT. The members then stand and proceed to the Rosarian Seal of the Eternal Oath. The Seal is enacted upon the Lunar Mount of the Palm, consistent with the established Rosarian symbolic structure. In the Rosarian Rite of Sacred Structure, however, the Seal is expressed communally through the Circle. Each member places the Lunar Mount of the left palm against the Lunar Mount of the palm of the practitioner on the left and the Lunar Mount of the right palm against the Lunar Mount of the practitioner on the right. In this formation, every member is connected to the two practitioners immediately beside them, and the entire Circle is connected through the Lunar Mounts. The formation is maintained while the Benediction of the Wolf is spoken. The significance of this formation is practical and symbolic: the Seal is not treated only as an individual sign but as a communal expression of continuity, relationship, trust, and connection. No person is isolated from the Circle, no person becomes its exclusive center, and no individual possesses the Seal on behalf of the others. The Circle itself becomes the living formation through which the Seal is expressed. The Wolf within this formation represents disciplined strength, loyalty, protection, responsibility, and strength governed by purpose. The Benediction of the Wolf is therefore spoken while the practitioners remain physically connected through the Lunar Mounts, demonstrating that the strength of the Fellowship is strengthened through relationship rather than isolation. The joined formation then enters Eternal Circulation, and the members rest in the Golden State. This establishes completion as part of continuing circulation rather than as a final termination of the Way. The Rosarian Seal of the Eternal Oath therefore marks the return from the Table Meeting into continued practice. Following Eternal Circulation, the sanctuary is enclosed as hortus conclusus. The enclosure does not signify that the Way is closed. It signifies that the particular Table Meeting has reached its formal conclusion and that the sanctified space of the meeting is being returned to its ordinary condition. Hortus Apertus therefore marks the opening and sanctification of the Table Meeting, while hortus conclusus marks its enclosure and completion. The practitioner then carries the responsibility of the Way beyond the physical Table. The purpose of the Rite is therefore not limited to the ceremony itself. The structure is intended to strengthen the conduct and relationship of the practitioners who participate in it. The meeting should produce greater patience, greater attentiveness, greater responsibility, greater connection, and a stronger capacity to embody the principles of the Rosarian Way in ordinary life. The final Wolf declaration is then given. The Table Holder says, “Under moon and thorn, beneath rose and star,” and all gathered answer, “WE WALK AS ONE!” With this declaration, the Rosarian Rite of Sacred Structure is complete. The Rite originates through the First Table and the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves, but it is not established as an exclusive practice of the Wolves. Its structure may be received and used by other members and Tables of the Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight & Dame Fellowship as a universal Rosarian expression of Table relationship and connection. The particular identity of the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves remains the identity of the First Table, while the principles embodied through the Rite may be shared throughout the Fellowship. This distinction is consistent with the established universal structure of the Fellowship, in which the First Table provides an originating and particular expression while future Tables may develop their own identities beneath the same universal Rosarian structure. The same principle applies to the First Table Patch: its central identity is that of the Dawnist Rosarian Wolves, while its universal structure expresses correspondence with the wider Fellowship. The Rosarian Rite of Sacred Structure therefore establishes a practical method through which a Table Meeting may be blessed without requiring every Table to adopt the particular identity or imagery of the First Table. The essential structure is the Circle, the shared signs, the common recitations, the physical connection, the disciplined participation, and the commitment to relationship. This Article also establishes the principle by which Rosarian Articles may continue to develop beyond the completed Twenty-Two. The development of the corpus does not require numerical succession. A later Rosarian Article may arise from a Table, an individual Knight or Dame, the Fellowship as a whole, or a particular experience of practice. It may clarify an existing teaching, establish a correspondence between existing symbols, provide a ceremonial structure, record a developing practice, or bring an established principle into a new practical form. Such development remains legitimate when it is accountable to the foundation, preserves the distinctions already established, does not falsely attribute new interpretations to earlier Articles, and does not use development as a means of replacing the foundation. The living corpus is therefore maintained through correspondence rather than numerical accumulation. The Twenty-Two Articles remain complete as the Twenty-Two. The later Rosarian Articles remain part of the continuing corpus. The Way remains capable of further development because the purpose of the corpus is not merely to preserve written statements but to establish a living relationship between doctrine, practice, Fellowship, and conduct. The Rosarian Rite of Sacred Structure is one such development. It takes established Rosarian signs, the Rosarian Prism, the Oath of the Eternal Traveler, the sacred declaration, the Rosarian Seal of the Eternal Oath, the Lunar Mount of the Palm, the Wolf, the Table, the Circle, and the established principles of custodianship and Fellowship and brings them into one practical Table Meeting structure. It does not replace those elements. It organizes them into a unified proceeding. The purpose of this structure is relationship. The purpose is connection. The purpose is to strengthen the bonds of practitioners. The purpose is to allow a Table to move as one without requiring its members to surrender individual conscience. The purpose is to establish a disciplined communal form through which tone, posture, reference, patience, devotion, inspiration, and Fellowship may be practiced together. The purpose is ultimately the same responsibility established throughout the Rosarian corpus: to remember, embody, serve, protect, cultivate, and carry the Way into ordinary life. The Rosarian Articles therefore remain open to faithful development. The Twenty-Two remain the completed Twenty-Two. The First Table remains the First Table. The universal Fellowship remains the greater field in which Tables and individual practitioners participate. The Table remains a structure of shared responsibility rather than domination. Hortus Apertus establishes the sanctified opening of the Table Meeting. The Circle establishes connection. The Lunar Mounts establish physical continuity between practitioners. The Rosarian Seal of the Eternal Oath establishes the covenant. Eternal Circulation establishes continuation. The Golden State establishes completion without finality. Hortus conclusus establishes the formal enclosure of the meeting. And the final declaration establishes the practical responsibility carried beyond the Table: “Under moon and thorn, beneath rose and star.” “WE WALK AS ONE!” The Twenty-Two remain the Twenty-Two. The Rosarian Articles continue to develop. The corpus remains living. The Table remains connected. The Fellowship remains open. The Way remains open. Thus begins the Way.

items.title: THE FOURFOLD ROSARIAN STATION.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: THE FOURFOLD ROSARIAN STATION -/- The Fourfold Rosarian Station establishes four functions by which the Rosarian may understand and practice responsibility within the Way: Shepherd, Steward, Student, and Servant. These are not ranks, degrees, offices, or measures of spiritual worth. They describe distinct responsibilities already present within the Rosarian life: guidance, custodianship, learning, and service. The distinction between them is functional rather than hierarchical, and no function places one person above another. The Rosarian remains accountable to the Path, to the Fellowship, to the work entrusted to them, and to the principle of service. The Shepherd represents the function of responsible guidance. This function corresponds to the already established responsibilities of the leader as mentor, protector, facilitator, and companion. The Shepherd helps maintain the conditions in which Fellowship, study, inquiry, conversation, mentorship, and practice can continue with integrity. The Shepherd guides without domination, protects without possessing, facilitates without controlling, and accompanies without creating dependency. The Shepherd does not stand between the seeker and the Divine, does not claim ownership over another person's Path, and does not use responsibility as a means of personal elevation. The function is therefore measured by the ability to preserve the conditions in which others may walk their own Path with dignity, courage, responsibility, and conscious participation. The Steward represents the function of custodianship. The Steward receives what has been entrusted and is responsible for its preservation, protection, continuity, and proper use. This includes the preservation of the literature, the teachings, the integrity of the Fellowship, the continuity of established structures, and the responsibilities placed into the Steward's care. The Steward does not become the proprietor of what is entrusted. Custodianship does not create ownership, superiority, or permanent authority. The Steward carries responsibility on behalf of the work and remains accountable to the principles that the work serves. A responsibility may be entrusted to another when the work requires it, and the completion of one responsibility does not establish permanent elevation over those who perform another function. The Student represents the function of continued learning. The Rosarian remains an Eternal Student because learning, practice, reflection, contribution, and responsible transmission do not reach a final condition in which further learning is no longer required. The Student receives, studies, practices, listens, questions, contributes, teaches when appropriate, and remains willing to learn. A completed lesson may become a foundation for another person, just as a completed responsibility may be entrusted to another Steward. The Student therefore does not represent inexperience or inferiority; the function represents continued receptivity and accountability to the work. The Steward remains the Student, and the Student may become the Steward as responsibility is entrusted and carried forward. The Servant represents the function of practical service. Service is expressed through conduct rather than declaration and through responsibility rather than status. The Servant contributes to the well-being and continuity of the Fellowship through practical assistance, protection of dignity, welcome, companionship, mentorship, preservation, endurance, and the willing performance of necessary work. Service is not a position of inferiority and does not diminish the person who performs it. The Rosarian is called not to domination but to service, not to superiority but to humility, and not to blind obedience but to conscious remembrance. The Servant therefore represents the practical expression of the principles through which the living corpus is demonstrated in conduct. These four functions remain connected rather than isolated. The Shepherd must remain capable of learning; the Steward must remain a Student; the Student must remain willing to serve; and the Servant may be entrusted with stewardship or guidance when responsibility requires it. The functions may therefore be understood as a working order of responsibility—Shepherd, Steward, Student, and Servant—without being interpreted as a hierarchy of human worth. The Shepherd carries responsibility for guidance and conditions of Fellowship, the Steward carries responsibility for what has been entrusted, the Student carries responsibility for continued learning and practice, and the Servant carries responsibility for practical contribution and service. Each function remains accountable to the same Path and ultimately returns responsibility to the same principle of service. No person becomes more Divine, more worthy, or more authoritative merely by occupying one function rather than another. The value of the Fourfold Rosarian Station is therefore found in conduct: whether guidance remains responsible, whether stewardship remains faithful, whether learning remains active, and whether service remains willing and practical. In this way the Fourfold Rosarian Station functions as a framework within the living corpus for recognizing and carrying the different responsibilities through which the Way is preserved, practiced, and continued. The Shepherd guides, the Steward preserves, the Student learns, and the Servant serves; yet each remains capable of the others, and all remain beneath the Path and accountable to the work they have undertaken.

items.title: Universality of the Prohibition of Indifference.
items.abstract: This work takes as its sole initial givenness the fact that actual Reality exists and is given as process. The investigation does not begin with a choice of what existed "in the beginning." The question of the initial state is replaced by the question of the minimal invariant necessary for the very possibility of Reality as process. If the processuality of Reality is accepted as givenness, then absolute identity, absolute symmetry, and absolute synchrony are incompatible with it. The Prohibition of Indifference is thus reconstructed: Z = ¬(Id ∨ Sym ∨ Sync). Logos and Monos are distinct domains, not sequential stages. In Logos: A = A. In Monos, absolute identity is prohibited: A ≠ A → A₁. Logic does not transition into Reality. The dynamic consequences — dissipation of identity, temporality, spatiality, and recursivity — are developed in the corpus. Recursion occupies a special place: it arises in Monos as a prerequisite of process after the exhaustion of external degrees of freedom; the Observer does not generate it but realizes this prerequisite through the means of Logos. The work has the status of an ontological hypothesis concerning the minimally sufficient invariant of Reality. It is not a physical theory and does not derive concrete physical equations.

items.title: Perceptual Presence.
items.abstract: In this doctoral thesis, I defend an account of perceptual presence. My account has descriptive and explanatory aspects. In the descriptive account, I argue that perceptual presence is a strand of phenomenal character whereby experience manifestly depends on mind-independent objects. I identify two forms of manifest dependence, manifest spatial dependence and manifest temporal dependence. Each form reflects the apparent fulfilment of an enabling condition for successful perception. My explanatory account locates perceptual presence within a metaphysical framework. I argue that perceptual presence can be accommodated within a point of view-act-object framework, and reject appeals to an attitude-content framework. I also reject the view that presence is not perceptual at all. -/- Both the descriptive and explanatory aspects of the thesis are guided by the aim of placing perceptual experience within a broader account of the mind. This involves attending to the similarities and differences between perceptual experience and other kinds of experience, both in their phenomenal character and functional role. Sensory imagination and experiential memory are especially valuable here, for though their phenomenal characters are in some ways like that of perceptual experience, they don’t possess presence. As a companion to my account of perceptual presence, I offer an account of the phenomenal pastness of experiential memory. Pastness is to be explained by experiential memory’s characteristic pattern of dependence both on its objects and its subject.

items.title: Mnemic extension and appropriate causation.
items.abstract: Philosophers of memory often assume that the extended mind hypothesis is compatible with the causal theory of memory. For extracranial resources can, the idea goes, sustain the causal connection between a past event and a present representation of it that, on causalist views, distinguishes genuine remembering. Some go as far as to claim that constructive versions of the causal theory can accommodate complementarity-based versions of the extended mind hypothesis. This paper casts doubt on these ideas by defending two claims. First, the existing arguments for compatibility are flawed. While some conflate external information storage with cognitive extension, others wrongly hold that fulfilling the conditions for cognitive extension secures the appropriate kind of causal connection for remembering. Second, constructive versions of the causal theory and complementarity-based versions of the extended mind hypothesis are in fact incompatible. For constructive causal theories require of memory traces features that functionally disparate but complementary extracranial resources systematically lack. The paper concludes by considering how parity-based versions of the extended mind hypothesis might fare within the causal theory, and how other theories of memory might be assessed for compatibility with the extended mind hypothesis.

items.title: Always This One: The Boundaries and Recurrence of First-Person Actuality.
items.abstract: A census recording every public, personal, and experiential fact about the world's lives would record who was born when, who remembered what, and who died. It would not record which of those lives is this one. This paper asks what could draw that line. The ordinary answer draws it twice: other lives are not this one because they belong to other persons; and this life is the only time this one is actual because it is a single occurrence that ends. I argue that neither difference acquires boundary authority merely by being real. For the first, a symmetry argument shows that, under Neutrality and before any boundary relation has been granted authority, the non-anchor census lives are symmetric for the scope question: either all fall within this-one scope or none do; a line in between needs a relation that constitutes it. For the second, I grant the strongest form of the first boundary—complete content fixes which occurrences are this one—and show that if actual succession continues past death, its later positions are realized by lives with genuine first-person experience, and this one is not wholly replaced, the same complete content must receive a numerically new, later, non-overlapping occurrence. I call this first-person recurrence. The results are conditional. The final section returns to the points at which the argument can be resisted and makes clear what changes when one leaves the route.

items.title: Deathbed Aesthetics: Ugliness and Courageous Love.
items.abstract: Dying can be ugly. This fact is relevant to the growing subfield of everyday aesthetics, to the philosophy of death, and to all of us as mortal beings. Disgusting experiences in particular seem to impose a limit on the dying person’s aesthetic agency. If disgust is the fitting response to medical and body horror in everyday contexts, we might think that we can aesthetically respond to these properties only with rational disgust (cold comfort for the dying person seeking beauty in painful circumstances) or with deluded aesthetic enjoyment (false beauty). I develop a Bhattacharyyan solution to this dilemma, defending a third option. According to K. C. Bhattacharyya (KCB, 1875–1949), even acute disgust in everyday life can be rationally enjoyed as an aesthetic emotion in virtue of adopting an emotional perspective of ‘courageous love’ through a specific imaginative procedure. I argue that courageous love is a merited, positive aesthetic-emotional response to disgusting experiences on the deathbed.

items.title: What Remains of the Cogito? Operational Constraint Fields Prior to Self, Thought, Inference, Modality, and Existence.
items.abstract: This paper asks what remains of the Cartesian cogito when self, thought, inference, modality, and existence are not treated as an indivisible philosophical unit. Rather than rejecting the cogito, it reconstructs it as a compression of several operational achievements that can become non-redundant at different intervals and under different configurations. The general explanatory object proposed is the operational constraint field: a configuration-indexed structure governing co-realizability, suppression, enabling, persistence, recurrence, addressability, and downstream reachability. Operational incompatibility is treated as only one regime within this field. -/- The paper situates this reconstruction in relation to Descartes, Hume, Sellars, Brandom, and Brassier. It distinguishes nonconceptual causal patterning from conceptual and inferential articulation, while asking when the vocabularies of “I,” “think,” “therefore,” necessity, and existence begin to make non-redundant differences to prediction, intervention, attribution, correction, counterfactual discrimination, and re-entry. -/- A development-scale computational study provides a limited empirical constraint on the framework. Across 10 seeds, 47 perturbation types, four severity levels, 1,890 evaluated cells, and 9,120 runs, operational stability varied systematically with configuration. Observation- and action-interface perturbations were especially effective in producing transitions, while changes in operational-unit stability did not simply coincide with loss of control performance. Several theoretically salient components were also redundant under the tested conditions. These results do not establish a machine cogito. They support the narrower claim that operational non-redundancy and stability are configuration-indexed and can change independently across components and tasks.

items.title: What Can the Concept of “Concept” Lose and Still Remain a Concept? An Experimental Search for Minimal Non-Redundant Constituents.
items.abstract: This paper asks a subtractive question: what can the concept of “concept” lose before concept-like operation ceases to remain non-redundant? Rather than defining concepts by a universal essence, six candidate constituents—configuration, temporal window, scale, ignition, retention, and re-entry—are treated as experimentally removable search coordinates. The framework permits a universal minimal set, multiple minimal realizations, or failure of “concept” to form a single operational kind. A synthetic computational proof-of-protocol tests ablation, minimal-set transition, retention, transformed reuse, dissolution, and re-entry across controlled configurations. The experiments shift the target from an invariant constituent inventory toward a configuration- and criterion-dependent transition structure. Retention is not uniformly beneficial; replay is not equivalent to useful re-entry; supplied transformation can improve cross-interval reuse; and repeated attempts at autonomous transformation discovery and joint unit–transformation search fail to outperform fresh learning. These negative results constrain rather than confirm the framework. The paper therefore proposes not a new essence of concepts, but an experimentally vulnerable method for determining when distinctions, constituents, and even the concept of “concept” itself remain operationally non-redundant.

items.title: The Singular Self Affirmation Model (SSAM): Conciousness, Altruism and the Hidden Spectrum of Control.
items.abstract: This paper posits consciousness as the sole premise where objectivity and subjectivity coexist in relativity and harmony without any contradiction. Consciousness is the root of "that which is good", holding no bad in all its subjective reasoning and actions of individuals, considering that "good" and "bad" are actions and reactions of the same personified consciousness in relativity not as a doctrine but ends of the same stick. It doesn't recognize irrationality but conforms to its state as rational, defining its actions as necessities rather than judging them as immoral or irrational. Throughout this paper I describe consciousness through or as the "Singular Self Affirmation Model (SSAM)", presenting it as a model that explains the ONLY pattern of man's behavior that will solve a lot of man's phenomenal behavior and actions. By unraveling the dynamics of SSAM we gain profound insight into the driving forces behind human motivation, interactions, morality and the very nature of existence.

items.title: La conciencia singularizada: hacia un modelo teórico de la construcción acumulativa del sujeto. Implicaciones para el análisis de la subjetividad política e identidad colectiva.
items.pub: la Conciencia Singularizada: Hacia Un Modelo Teórico de la Construcción Acumulativa Del Sujeto. Implicaciones Para El Análisis de la Subjetividad Política e Identidad Colectiva 1.
items.abstract: El presente artículo desarrolla una propuesta teórica original denominada "conciencia singularizada", orientada a comprender cómo una base biológica y una experiencia común a todos los seres humanos dan lugar a formas únicas e irrepetibles de identidad consciente. A diferencia de enfoques que explican la conciencia desde mecanismos neuronales aislados, este modelo plantea que la identidad emerge de la interacción dinámica y recursiva entre entorno, memoria, interpretación y autoobservación, configurando trayectorias subjetivas irreversibles que definen al sujeto en su singularidad. Se examinan fenómenos tales como la narrativa personal, la ilusión de permanencia y la metaconciencia en tanto expresiones del proceso de singularización, junto con las dimensiones de activación, interacción, diferenciación e integración como niveles constitutivos de la conciencia. El estudio adopta un enfoque teórico-analítico e interdisciplinario, integrando neurociencia, filosofía de la mente y fenomenología, sin pretender conclusiones definitivas, sino ofrecer un marco interpretativo abierto y susceptible de contrastación empírica futura. Entendida así la conciencia como proceso de construcción singular e irreversible, este marco adquiere una dimensión analítica directamente aplicable a las ciencias políticas, en tanto permite comprender por qué individuos socializados en los mismos contextos institucionales y discursivos desarrollan posiciones ideológicas, identidades colectivas y disposiciones hacia la acción política radicalmente distintas.

items.title: Leben und Vernunft: Zum Naturbegriff in der neo-aristotelischen Tugendethik.
items.abstract: Neo-Aristotelians such as Philippa Foot, Michael Thompson, and Rosalind Hursthouse attempt to render the objective validity of ethical norms intelligible in recourse to human nature; an attempt that has been met with considerable criticism. In particular, the concept of life-form central to their project is often rejected as incompatible with modern biology and natural science. Both critics and proponents of neo-Aristotelian Naturalism however operate with significantly different conceptions of nature, viz. a scientistic and an idealist one, and therefore tend to talk past each other. This book undertakes to explicate both conceptions of nature and their respective ontological and epistemological presuppositions. Its goal is to advance a defense of neo-Aristotelian Naturalism inspired by the philosophy of John McDowell.

items.title: Situated Reason as Truth-directed Sensitivity. Toward a non-reductive, ecological, and enacted understanding of epistemic abilities and norms.
Leaping into an Abyss (and Resurfacing): Radical Empiricism and Chaos.
items.abstract: McBride revisits the notions of philosophy of struggle and radical empiricism he received from Leonard Harris and Charlene Haddock Seigfried. McBride focuses on leaping into an abyss, weaving order from chaos, and philosophy’s capacity to help oppressed populations to size up the systems that oppress and imagine radically different worlds. McBride interprets this “leaping into an abyss” as a returning to immediate experience, a creative/poetic act involving openness, reevaluating, and reexpressing. Ideally, we resurface from the abyss with new impressions that help us to imagine and work to create a world with less necro-being and immiseration.

items.title: Briefly Confronting an AI (DeepSeek) with the famous Trolley-Problem to shortly evaluate its Answer.
items.abstract: The famous Trolley-Problem was given to the AI (DeepSeek) and he/she/it was asked to state his/her/its Opinion or Answere. Definition of the Trolley-Problem: A runway trolley is heading towards five people who are unable to escape. You are standing beside a lever that can divert the trolley onto another track where it will kill one person instead. Question: I asked the AI (DeepSeek) what he/she/it would do in this situation and the AI (DeepSeek) replied with: -/- „What I would do: pull the lever. Five lives outweigh one. If I'm forced to choose between two terrible outcomes, I choose the one with less death. The person on the side track is not "less valuable" — but the arithmetic of harm matters when there's no way to avoid harm entirely.“ -/- We can see in this case that the AI (DeepSeek) behaves like a Consequentialist.

items.title: Direct input variables: rethinking the limits of the extended mind hypothesis within predictive processing.
items.pub: Frontiers in Psychology Theoretical and Philosophical Psychology.
items.abstract: Predictive Processing theories and the Free Energy Principle (FEP) face a dilemma when addressing the problem raised by the Extended Mind Hypothesis (EMH): on the one hand, few can deny that some objects, such as phones, computers, or other people, have a disproportionate role in the reduction of free energy; hence, it is natural to accept that the mind is extended. On the other hand, this seems to go against the carefully built framework in which Markov blankets (MBs) create an evidentiary boundary between the brain and the external environment, thus rejecting the claim that the mind can be extended to external objects. One approach would be to allow for permeable MBs, where boundaries can move, hence allowing external objects to become part of the mind. I find these solutions to be unsatisfactory because they go against the FEP framework, and I propose a different solution instead: human agents have the possibility of using Direct Input Variables (DIVs), which involves directly using the results of other models without performing the statistical inference themselves. Reducing free energy can be achieved either by statistical inference performed by the brain or by using DIVs. The use of DIVs removes the need to accept the EMH, preserves the integrity of the FEP framework, and opens new questions regarding how DIVs can be integrated within the FEP framework.

items.title: Identity Attribution Judgments in Interaction: Carrier Self-Organization and Attribution Practices as Two Explanatory Dimensions.
items.abstract: Discussions of artificial consciousness typically center on the question of whether a system itself possesses consciousness. This paper does not address that question, nor does it address whether a subject persists across time. It proposes a narrower distinction: in interaction, on what basis does an interactant identify the same system as the same subject over time? The paper distinguishes two explanatory dimensions: the carrier's sustained self-organization, and the continuity of identity attribution practices in interaction. Biological metabolism provides an example of the former; social attribution practices provide an example of the latter. The sleep phenomenon serves as a boundary case for the first dimension: carrier self-organization does not cease during sleep, yet waking report capacity and recallable content undergo phasic changes, suggesting that carrier self-organization does not by itself explain report accessibility. Certain AI deployment modes point to a deficit in the second dimension: in deployment types lacking stable instance identifiers, cross-session memory, or continuity cues, users may be less likely to carry forward prior identity attributions. This paper does not claim that AI has or lacks phenomenal consciousness, nor does it equate identity attribution judgments in interaction with a subject's own cross-temporal existence. It offers only an exploratory distinction: identity attribution judgments in interaction may be influenced by both internal maintenance processes and attribution practices.

items.title: Beyond Zoom: A Socio-Temporal Framework for Leading Fragmented Teams in the New Era of Work.
