An organism replaces matter, alters its internal organization, responds to its environment, and yet remains a living organism. We use the language of sameness almost automatically. But this ordinary language conceals a philosophical problem. If a finite being changes continuously, what exactly is preserved through that change? If nothing is preserved, in what sense does the being continue? If something is preserved, what is it? A substance, a structure, a function, a causal history, a pattern, a relation, a capacity, or something else? Traditional approaches to persistence have often attempted to answer this question by identifying some form of identity that survives change. The enduring object is supposed to remain numerically identical through time. The perduring object is understood through its temporal parts. The substance theorist appeals to an underlying bearer of properties. Psychological theories of personal identity identify continuity of memory, intention, character, or psychological connectedness. Narrative theories emphasize the organization of a life into an intelligible temporal structure. These approaches illuminate important aspects of persistence. Yet they leave open a deeper question: why should the preservation of identity be the fundamental condition of continuance? -/- Keywords: Finite continuance, ontology, capacity, reconfiguration, erosion, meta capacity, temporality, phenomenology, ethics, technology.

items.title: Constitutive Architecture of Consciousness ,A Response to the Hard Problem of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper develops the Constitutive Information-Binding Architecture (CIBA), a theoretical account of phenomenal consciousness grounded in the organization of distributed neural processes. The central proposal is that phenomenal consciousness is nothing over and above the simultaneous binding of neural networks corresponding to concurrent environmental perception, the lived body, the body-as-object, and retrieved memories within a unified, temporally continuous first-person organization. CIBA distinguishes informational integration, vector representation, constitutive binding architecture, and primary phenomenal organization, and introduces the Persistent Referential Indexing Architecture (PRIA) to characterize referential continuity across time. Phenomenal qualities are treated as differentiated organizational states rather than additional non-physical properties. The identity thesis is presented as a conditional philosophical interpretation of the proposed organization, not as an independently established empirical result. The framework's limitations and possible operationalization are specified, and empirically discriminating questions are derived from the architecture.

items.title: OF THE ENCOUNTER WITH ONESELF IN THE FUTURE AND THE POSSIBILITY OF NOT FINDING ONESELF: of freedom as anguishing oneself before oneself and being "as" anguish "beinganguish" in order to escape from anguish in Jean-Paul Sartre.
items.pub: Zygmunt Bauman Journals (Ufrgs - Federal University of Rio Grande Do Sul) 16 (41):2-40.
items.abstract: Dwelling on freedom as a keeping oneself out of the reach of being and keeping oneself immune to its action in a beyond a nothingness, Sartre points to anguish as the recognition of a possibility as its possibility and identification of the rupture in relation to its essence by nothingness. In this way, anguishing oneself in front of oneself is what imposes itself on freedom in a movement that encloses nothingness as "why", being the recognition by the human existent of a possibility as its possibility. Since anguish consists in the reflexive capture of freedom by itself, the being emerges "as" anguish "being-anguish" in order to escape from anguish, as Sartre argues, who points out the original act through which the existing human being is for itself its own nothingness as that which imposes itself on discovery in absolute immanence as pure subjectivity of the instantaneous cogito in a process that encloses the question involving consciousness and its modus essendi as its foundation which makes it possible for the human existent to appear in the world as the being that is its own nothingness and as the being through which nothingness comes into the world. Thus, in view of Sartre's theoretical-conceptual construction as the encounter with oneself in the future and the possibility of not finding oneself, to the extent that it points out a being for whom in one's own being the awareness of the nothingness of one's being between bad faith and lies is imposed, Prof. Luiz Carlos Mariano Da Rosa, In line with the hermeneutic-phenomenological ontological-existential principle, he stresses that, if we are-anguish-to-escape-from-it in the unity of the same consciousness, the possibility of bad faith implies the need for the unity of being and nonbeing, that is, being-for-non-being, converging towards the identification of consciousness through a definition that is not circumscribed by the boundaries of a being for which its being is imposed in its own being, while this being implies another being that does not concomitantly remaining under the aegis of a being for whom in his own being the consciousness of the nothingness of his being is imposed.

items.title: A Preliminary Taxonomy of Equivalence in Generative Relational Theory.
items.abstract: This paper develops a preliminary taxonomy of equivalence within Generative Relational (GR) theory. The inquiry begins from GR's distinction among ontological reality, relational reality, and manifestation reality and extends the comparison problem beyond equivalence at a single static level. The taxonomy is organized by the formal object on which an equivalence or equivalence-like relation is defined. It distinguishes equivalence within individual GR reality levels; equivalence of relational structures connecting multiple levels; equivalence of historical evolutions of single-level or multi-level structures; and equivalence of dynamical regimes or agreement of structural invariants. A preceding architectural section specifies the carrier, historical scope, retained structure, relation type, applicability domain, and representational resolution required by a well-formed equivalence claim. The formalism reserves the term equivalence relation for relations whose relevant axioms are established and separates it from similarity, tolerance, substitutability, simulation, bisimulation, isomorphism, and diagnostic agreement. History-bearing configurations, manifestation maps, retained relational content, symmetry-relative interchangeability, and admissible historical extensions provide inherited GR interfaces for the construction. The paper further studies cross-level lifting, stability under relational refinement, relational substitution, history-sensitive embedding, and the evolution of equivalence structures themselves through refinement, coarsening, and reorganization. Human–AI interchangeability provides a principal application, supplemented by AI–AI and Human–Human comparisons. Turing-style evaluation is located within the broader taxonomy, and a Generative Relational Equivalence Investigation is proposed as a structured procedure for testing how observed equivalence changes under contextual, relational, historical, continuation, and dynamical enrichment. Ultimate ontological equivalence remains suspended, and normative consequences require additional premises.

items.title: How Are Immediacy, Experience, and Rationality Generated? — Operational Shapes, Transcendental Reflection, Historical Compression, Invisible Mediation, Generated Observability, and Xenoscience.
items.abstract: This paper asks how immediacy, experience, and rationality are generated rather than presupposed. It argues that what appears as immediate experience or self-standing rational access is often the compressed result of prior mediation by perceptual organization, conceptual inheritance, historical stabilization, social practices, instrumentation, and inferential structures. The paper develops an operational account in which immediacy is not treated as the absence of mediation, but as the local disappearance of visible mediation within a sufficiently stabilized configuration. Experience is analyzed as an operationally organized field in which differences become selectively observable, retainable, and action-guiding, while rationality emerges only within intervals in which reasons, incompatibilities, commitments, and revisions become available as non-redundant constraints. Transcendental reflection is reconstructed not as access to timeless conditions of possibility, but as a method for identifying the historically and materially generated conditions under which particular forms of experience and rational assessment become possible. The concepts of historical compression and invisible mediation explain how layered processes can become phenomenologically or epistemically immediate once their enabling operations are no longer encountered as separate steps. Generated observability extends this analysis to scientific and artificial systems, where new sensors, scales, interfaces, and inferential architectures can produce previously unavailable objects and distinctions. Xenoscience generalizes the argument by treating immediacy, experience, and rationality as revisable operational achievements rather than universal starting points.

items.title: The Fractal Co-Creative Universe.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a speculative metaphysical model in which reality is understood not primarily as a fixed object but as an evolving, recursively creative process. The central proposition is that conscious beings may participate in the formation of reality while simultaneously being products of the reality in which they participate. The framework explores consciousness, imagination, perception, autonomy, collective reality, consent, and the possibility of multiple or nested realities. It draws conceptual connections to process philosophy, phenomenology, social constructionism, and John Archibald Wheeler's participatory universe, while distinguishing those precedents from the paper's original speculative extensions concerning creative sovereignty, branching realities, recursive creators, and reality rewriting. The model does not claim that contemporary science has established direct consciousness-based reality creation. Its purpose is to ask whether these possibilities can be formulated coherently, what philosophical consequences follow from them, and what would be required to distinguish them from competing accounts of reality.

items.title: Recognizing artificial minds or succumbing to paraeidolia? On Cappelen & Dever’s “whole hog” defense of artificial minds.
items.abstract: Prominent researchers are now defending the contention that current large language models have mental properties—humanity has, by these lights, successfully constructed artificial minds. Notably, Cappelen and Dever have recently argued that such models are capable of thought, understanding, and performing intentional actions. They support this controversial contention on the basis of an argument that trades on the idea that humans are highly competent at detecting mental states. In this article, we argue that their case in support of the existence of artificial minds is philosophically misguided and, at crucial points, rests upon dubious empirical grounds. Along the way, we also examine the methodological motivations behind their case. Cappelen and Dever claim that the philosophy of AI tends to traffic in an outmoded and retrograde methodology, one that unduly privileges elaborate thought experiments and contrived counterexamples; this methodology, they argue, needs urgently to be overturned in favour of a new form of inquiry that begins by assigning more weight to what we observe when we interact with AI. Once we make this reversal, they claim, the case for artificial minds is very strong indeed. We argue that their case for such a methodology is, for numerous reasons, wrongheaded and is in any event unlikely to yield fruitful answers to questions concerning whether or not LLMs possess particular mental properties.

items.title: Beyond the fundamentals.
Representational Adequacy, Natural Selection, and Quantum Ontology: Against a Three-Dimensionally Spatial Reality.
items.abstract: We human cognizers represent reality as three-dimensionally spatial. However, despite appearances to the contrary, I contend that the likelihood that reality is three-dimensionally spatial in accordance with our spatial representations is either low at worst or inscrutable at best, if these representations are the results of evolution. The key reason is that natural selection is interested primarily in fitness and not specifically in truth per se. Dimensional veridicality of our spatial representations — i.e. the property of veridically representing the true dimensionality of space — is not required for adaptive behaviour. Dimensional veridicality per se confers no additional evolutionary benefits. Representational adequacy with respect to the relevant structure of reality suffices for evolutionary fitness without dimensional veridicality. Independent considerations of quantum ontology — e.g. wave function realism — also challenge the common view that reality is three-dimensionally spatial. There are serious considerations that counsel agnosticism: we do not know, and hence should suspend judgment about, the true spatial dimensionality of reality.

items.title: Phases of Psychological Development in Bounded Learning Systems.
items.abstract: Two kinds of learning systems appear, at first glance, to develop in remarkably similar ways. Human beings move through an extended period of world learning, socialization and value formation, adult specialization, and later-life stabilization. Large foundation models are likewise produced through broad self-supervised pretraining, instruction and preference alignment, compression or expert specialization, and frozen deployment. These parallels are often presented as metaphors. This article argues that they are better interpreted as two instantiations of the same conditional, normative resource-allocation problem. A bounded learning system is represented by a state containing a world-model posterior, a value-function posterior, a representational rate or description length, and a remaining developmental budget. Under finite horizons, approximate environmental stationarity, asymmetric world and value channels, a world-model gate on value learning, mature-compression gains, and single-crossing marginal values, the optimal trajectory contains four dominant intervals: world modeling, value alignment, compression specialization, and stable inference. The article proves channel separation between factual and value information, a world-model gate for alignment, rate-distortion compression, optimal stopping, and the ordered emergence of the four intervals. Human development and large-model training are then interpreted as twin psychological cases. Subjective time is not the theory’s primitive; it is a downstream readout of attentional and memory-encoding rates. The model yields testable predictions about checkpoints, transition points, novelty, delayed specialization, premature compression, and pathological freezing.

items.title: Ethics of the Present: Time, Presence, and Vigilance in Hellenistic Philosophy.
items.abstract: This paper examines the Stoic conception of time and its ethical implications, with particular focus on prosochē (attentive vigilance). Early Stoic physics treats time as an incorporeal associated with cosmic motion: bodies alone act and are acted upon, while reports distinguish the present as “obtaining” and past and future as subsisting. The paper argues that this ontology provides an important background for later Stoic exercises that concentrate agency on present assent and action, without reducing Stoic ethics to a metaphysics of the instantaneous. Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius develop prosochē as sustained attention to impressions, judgments, and conduct. Stoic affective theory further clarifies the temporal structure of evaluation: joy (chara) concerns present genuine good, whereas wish (boulēsis) and caution (eulabeia) are rationally future-directed. Stoic eudaimonia is accordingly interpreted as temporal coherence: virtue is complete in its quality rather than increased by mere duration. Comparison with Epicureanism, Pyrrhonian Skepticism, Plato, and Plotinus shows distinct ways of relating temporal ontology to ethical orientation. The central claim is that Stoicism gives the present a distinctive normative role: not because past and future are simply unreal, but because rational agency is exercised through judgments and actions that occur now.

items.title: The Internal Contradictions in Integrated Information Theory 4.0.
items.abstract: The six postulates of Integrated Information Theory 4.0 (IIT) (Albantakis et al., 2023) are jointly unsatisfiable, and not because the theory ranks them: the exclusion postulate contradicts itself in successive clauses, integration forbids what composition requires, and the one conflict the theory does adjudicate it adjudicates against itself, excluding from the Φ-structure the determinations the postulate was written to secure. The postulates characterize consciousness through a zeroth axiom and the five essential properties of phenomenal experience, and are existence (P1), intrinsicality (P2), information (P3), integration (P4), exclusion (P5), and composition (P6), with all six claimed as jointly necessary for consciousness. The argument is conducted entirely in the theory's own vocabulary, which is granted in full so that no result below can be answered by redefinition. Three structural contradictions are developed in detail. The first is internal to a single postulate: P5 requires in one clause that the substrate be definite, this whole set of units, and supplies in the next the maximization over candidate systems and partitions that is to make it so, while P2 requires that the quality and quantity of existence be observer-independent. Four lines of evidence establish that the maximization's output depends on the investigator. The search space is the set-partitions of the units multiplied by a direction assignment per part, and the procedure defined over it terminates for no biological system, so the investigator's truncation is not a shortcut around the theory's procedure but what returns a substrate at all. The measure's claimed uniqueness is argued from its properties and never from the substrate it selects. The theory assigns the partition space, the distinctions, and the grain to one principle of maximal existence, and the three searches are nested rather than parallel, so they are one dependence. Where the procedure returns more than one answer, the theory resolves the tie in the first person plural. The second contradiction is between integration (P4) and composition (P6), which requires that consciousness be both undecomposable and structured into distinctions and relations, a pair the theory holds while stating that "causal distinctions have no inherent structure themselves" and reporting Φ-structures whose components it counts to the integer and bounds by formula. The third is between definiteness, the first clause of P5, and the joint demands of maximal information (P3) and structured composition (P6), which together require simultaneous specificity and variability. The available defenses, the discovery-property distinction, constitutive composition, and the aspect-distribution reading, each preserve the joint commitment by suspending one demand, and the three suspend three different demands, so the set is satisfiable at any moment only by not being the set the theory states. Two of the three suspensions fall on P5, which is the postulate that contradicts itself. Five results follow from the three. The observer-dependence of the maximization is the condition methodology names researcher degrees of freedom, and it is worse in IIT's case than in the standard one, because the choices reach the object the theory is about rather than the route to testing it. The theory records its own non-satisfaction cases: when the resolution of ties exhausts, the tied systems "do not comply with the exclusion postulate" and "do not qualify as complexes," so a system fails to be conscious because a computation returned two values rather than one. The rarity the theory offers as the reason ties can be set aside is itself a requirement of micro-level indeterminism, and the theory's worked examples require indeterminism to be absent for Φ to be high, with the cortex named as the substrate where both demands fall. The postulates specify what obtains and never what operates: where the theory names something at these seams it names a principle of maximal or minimal existence, offered as a good explanation of why outcomes are what they are, which supplies a reason and not an operator. The case of uncertainty, treated structurally rather than phenomenologically, is settled by the theory against itself, since the congruence condition on which distinctions compose a complex excludes incongruent cause-effect states from the structure, so the Φ-structure identified with the experience is not the structure of the state a system holding two incompatible determinations is in. No system therefore satisfies IIT 4.0 as stated, and which suspension is in force when a system is called conscious is settled outside the theory. The wider case against IIT's identity claim is developed in *Phi Without Phenomenology: The Compositional Failures of Integrated Information Theory (of "Consciousness")* (Stewart, 2026o). -/- **Keywords:** integrated information theory, IIT 4.0, Phi, Φ-structure, consciousness, postulates, axioms, intrinsicality, information postulate, integration, exclusion postulate, composition, definiteness, maximal substrate, principle of maximal existence, intrinsic difference, causal distinctions, causal relations, congruence, tie resolution, degrees of freedom, theories of consciousness.

items.title: The Belief-Independence of Perception: An Essay on the Mind's Architecture.
items.abstract: In this dissertation I argue that the mind has an architecture, and that perception and cognition are functionally distinct systems within it. What makes them distinct is a single property: the belief-independence of perception. A mental process is belief-independent when cognitive states—beliefs, desires, and thoughts—are dispensable to its computational explanation, which is to say that its outputs cannot be semantically traced back to cognitive contents in the way the conclusion of a genuine inference can be traced back to its premises. -/- In Chapter 1, I make this notion more precise. I separate out the functional and representational senses in which cognitive states might be dispensable to a process, and I argue that inferential isolation from cognition is the mark of belief-independence. -/- In Chapter 2, I ask how a psychological system could come to be isolated in this way, and I argue that informational encapsulation is sufficient for it, though not necessary. Defending the claim that perception is encapsulated means taking on the cognitive penetration literature. I go through the cases one at a time and argue that in each, either a purely perceptual explanation of the phenomenon is at least as well supported as the penetration explanation, or the perceptual outputs in question cannot be semantically traced to the cognitive contents said to affect them, so that whatever relation holds between them falls short of the inferential relation that would threaten the architectural distinction. -/- In Chapters 3 and 4, I argue that belief-independence explains features of perception, and so is more than a criterion for locating the perception–cognition boundary. In Chapter 3, I argue that encapsulation makes perception computationally tractable. On the standard view, encapsulation does this by shrinking a hypothesis space specified in advance. I argue instead that it works by leaving hypotheses outside that space out of consideration entirely, and that this same feature makes perception more accurate as well as faster. In Chapter 4, I argue that belief-independence is also necessary for perception to anchor thought to the world. Following a line of thought from Russell and Strawson, I argue that successful singular thought requires acquaintance relations of the kind perception provides, and that the FINST-and-object-file structure underlying visual tracking is one such relation. A perceptual system whose contents were fixed in part by belief would face the same reduplication problems that acquaintance is supposed to solve. -/- Taken together, the four chapters argue that perception and cognition are distinct stems of the mind's architecture, that the belief-independence of perception marks the line between them, and that it is because perception is belief-independent that it can make cognition both tractable and answerable to the world.

items.title: Cognitive Enfeeblement By Design.
items.abstract: Thinking hard is hard. Cognitive misers like us are therefore inclined to seek extreme cognitive assistance: assistance that is ubiquitously available, highly substitutive, and relatively domain-general. Increasingly, we are being offered assistance like this as the default mode of cognition – it is being embedded in the infrastructure of our digital lives. But whatever its merits for adults, providing extreme cognitive assistance to children is pro tanto morally wrong. This is because the cognitive capacities that make a person self-governing are skills: they are built through deliberate, regular exercise and lost without it. Extreme cognitive assistance removes both the opportunities for that exercise and the incentive to undertake it. Maybe this won't matter: in a future awash with extreme cognitive assistance, maybe persons won't need or want to think for themselves. But people should decide for themselves how much of their cognitive self-governance to hand over; and doing that requires having the capacity for cognitive self-governance in the first place.

items.title: Précis of The Weirdness of the World.
How Weird the World Is: Replies to Machery, Roelofs, and Schneider.
AI Weirdness and Distributive Gaming.
The Declaration of the Twenty-Two Rosarian Archetypes of the Twenty-Two Sacred Laws.
items.pub: Mystical Dawnist Rosarian Knight and Dame Fellowship.
items.abstract: We declare the Twenty-Two Rosarian Archetypes as the living forms through which the Twenty-Two Sacred Laws are remembered, embodied, and carried into the world. These archetypes are not merely names, titles, or symbolic figures, but expressions of a living doctrine: ways of being through which the seeker awakens, listens, breathes, purifies, remembers, serves, surrenders, and ultimately comes to dwell within the Rose. Each archetype gives human form to a Sacred Law, and each Law reveals a particular discipline of the Rosarian path. Together they form one continuous movement—from the first light of awakening to the hidden flowering of the Rose. The First Archetype is the Dawnbearer, bearer of the Law of Dawn. The Dawnbearer is the Bringer of First Light, the one who awakens souls and walks before others with the lamp of sacred remembrance. The Dawnbearer lives in gratitude and understands that awakening is not merely the acquisition of something new, but the remembrance of a light that was never truly absent. The Dawn calls the seeker from forgetfulness into awareness, from darkness into clarity, and from unconscious existence into a life lived deliberately beneath the rising light. The Second Archetype is the Silent Watcher, keeper of the Law of Silence. The Silent Watcher dwells in stillness, hears what is unspoken, protects unseen truths, and embodies quiet presence. Silence is not emptiness but receptivity; it is the chamber in which perception becomes clear and the hidden dimensions of truth can be heard. The Silent Watcher learns that not every truth requires immediate speech and that wisdom often begins by becoming sufficiently still to receive what cannot be heard through noise. The Third Archetype is the Breathkeeper, keeper 155 of the Law of Breath. The Breathkeeper moves according to sacred rhythm, speaks little, breathes deeply, and holds the invisible thread between life and spirit. Breath becomes the living bridge between the inward and outward worlds, the rhythm through which awareness returns to the present. Through breath the seeker learns patience, presence, restraint, and the sacred rhythm of existence. The Breathkeeper remembers that life is received moment by moment and that the Eternal may be encountered within the simple act of conscious breathing. The Fourth Archetype is the Purifier, keeper of the Law of Purity. The Purifier burns away illusion, walks clean through shadow, and dwells in simplicity and sacred clarity. Purity is the continual clearing away of what obscures the light: falsehood, confusion, vanity, needless attachment, resentment, and the habits through which perception becomes distorted. The Purifier does not fear the shadow, but enters it with clarity so that what is false may be distinguished from what is true. Purification is therefore not the rejection of existence, but the removal of whatever prevents the soul from seeing existence clearly. The Fifth Archetype is the Mirror of Truth, keeper of the Law of Truth. The Mirror of Truth reflects without distortion, stands in alignment, and speaks only what is soul-rooted and light-filled. The Mirror teaches that truth requires correspondence between what is inwardly known and what is outwardly lived. It asks the seeker to examine perception, speech, intention, and conduct so that the life does not become divided against itself. To become a Mirror of Truth is to abandon deliberate distortion and to allow reality to be encountered with honesty, humility, and clarity. The Sixth Archetype is the Untethered One, keeper of the Law of Non-Attachment. The Untethered One owns nothing inwardly, clings to nothing, loves with open hands, and moves freely in the current of the Divine. Non-attachment does not deny love, responsibility, or relationship; rather, it releases the demand to possess or control what cannot rightly be possessed or controlled. The Untethered 156 One learns to bless what arrives, release what departs, and remain inwardly free while participating fully in the world. The Seventh Archetype is the Reflector, keeper of the Law of Reflection. The Reflector sees the world as a sacred mirror, practices humility and self-inquiry, and transmutes judgment into compassion. Every encounter becomes an opportunity for examination, every conflict a possible teacher, and every reaction a doorway into deeper self-knowledge. The Reflector does not assume that every reflection is perfect or that every difficulty is the fault of the self; rather, the archetype calls the seeker to look honestly at what experience reveals and to transform judgment into understanding wherever understanding is possible. The Eighth Archetype is the Servant Flame, keeper of the Law of Service. The Servant Flame burns quietly for others, works in secret, and turns every act into a blessing without demand. Service is not performed for superiority, possession, or applause. It is the movement by which inward realization becomes outward action. The Servant Flame offers time, attention, labor, compassion, protection, and care without making recognition the condition of generosity. In this archetype the Rosarian learns that what is received inwardly must eventually become something that may flow outwardly through willing hands. The Ninth Archetype is the Devoted Vessel, keeper of the Law of Devotion. The Devoted Vessel sings love without words, offers every breath to the Source, and lives as a holy offering. Devotion is the orientation of the whole life toward what the seeker recognizes as sacred. It is not merely ceremony, declaration, or emotion, but the gradual alignment of thought, breath, action, and intention. The Devoted Vessel does not seek to possess the Divine, but to become receptive to it, allowing love and remembrance to move through the life as an offering. The Tenth Archetype is the Voice of Light, keeper of the Law of Sacred Word. The Voice of Light speaks with sacred intent, calls beauty into being, and guards the creative power of language. Words are treated as acts of creation: they may 157 strengthen or weaken, clarify or confuse, reconcile or divide, illuminate or obscure. Therefore the Voice of Light accepts responsibility for speech and learns that silence and speech are not opposites but complementary disciplines. To speak sacredly is to recognize that language carries consequence and that every word should be approached with intention, truth, and care. The Eleventh Archetype is the Inner Lamp, keeper of the Law of Inner Light. The Inner Lamp shines from within, needs no praise, and lights paths through darkness simply by being. Its light does not depend upon external validation. The seeker discovers that beneath the layers of illusion, fear, vanity, and distraction, there remains an inward light that may be remembered and uncovered. The Inner Lamp therefore becomes a figure of authenticity: one who does not need to announce their illumination, because presence itself becomes the testimony. The Twelfth Archetype is the Nourisher, keeper of the Law of Sacred Nourishment. The Nourisher blesses food, words, and thought, feeds the world through care, and makes the body a sacred dwelling. Nourishment concerns everything repeatedly received and everything repeatedly given. Food nourishes the body; words nourish or diminish the spirit; attention can create safety or anxiety; presence can heal or neglect. The Nourisher therefore learns to become conscious of what enters the self and what proceeds from the self, understanding that repeated consumption and repeated offering gradually shape the person and the world around them. The Thirteenth Archetype is the Harmonist, keeper of the Law of Balance. The Harmonist walks between opposites, holds the center in chaos, and wears both fire and water with grace. Balance does not mean avoiding difficult decisions or remaining neutral toward every circumstance. It means learning discernment: knowing when to act and when to wait, when to speak and when to listen, when to protect and when to release, when discipline is necessary and when freedom must be permitted. The Harmonist refuses to allow one legitimate concern to destroy every other legitimate concern and 158 learns to remain steady without becoming rigid. The Fourteenth Archetype is the Surrendered Heart, keeper of the Law of Surrender. The Surrendered Heart yields without loss, lets go with reverence, and trusts the rhythm of what cannot be controlled. Surrender is not abandonment of responsibility. It is the recognition of the boundary between what belongs to the seeker and what does not. One may govern one's conduct, make an honest effort, offer love, establish boundaries, and fulfill one's responsibilities, but one cannot command another person's thoughts, feelings, choices, or response. The Surrendered Heart therefore acts where action is possible and releases what lies beyond its authority. The Fifteenth Archetype is the Presence-Walker, keeper of the Law of Sacred Time. The Presence-Walker stands fully in the now, touches eternity in every moment, lives slowly, and sees clearly. Sacred time is not merely the measurement of hours but the recognition that attention itself is a portion of life. To listen to another person, to work, to rest, to eat, to walk, or to remain silent is to inhabit the moment rather than continually sacrificing the present to an imagined future. The Presence-Walker discovers that eternity is not necessarily distant from time; awareness can become the place where the eternal touches the living moment. The Sixteenth Archetype is the Forgiver, keeper of the Law of Forgiveness. The Forgiver cuts cords with kindness, heals through release, and frees both self and others with grace. Forgiveness does not require pretending that harm did not occur, nor does it require restoring trust where trust has not been rebuilt. A person may forgive while maintaining distance; they may release resentment while establishing necessary boundaries. Where repair is possible, repair may be pursued honestly; where an apology is owed, it should be offered without excuses. Forgiveness is therefore not forgetting. It is refusing to permit injury to become the permanent authority over what one becomes afterward. The Seventeenth Archetype is the Earth Listener, keeper of the Law of Nature's Wisdom. The Earth 159 Listener learns from stone, tree, and tide, lives seasonally, and honors the wisdom of natural rhythms. This Law teaches that not every problem is solved through greater speed, greater force, or greater effort. Nature reveals limits. Growth has seasons. Rest has purpose. Persistence is not always wisdom, and stopping the attempt to force what requires time can itself become an act of discernment. The Earth Listener therefore learns to observe consequence, honor the physical world, respect natural limits, and recognize that life moves through cycles of growth, rest, decay, renewal, and return. The Eighteenth Archetype is the Phoenix-Carrier, keeper of the Law of Death and Rebirth. The Phoenix-Carrier embraces endings, walks through fire, and brings new life from sacred death. The archetype teaches that some relationships, identities, beliefs, habits, roles, and expectations must eventually end. The seeker is not asked to become indifferent to loss, but neither are they asked to become permanently owned by it. Grief may be honored, lessons may be received, and what has genuinely ended may be released so that the new circumstances of life can be met honestly. Rebirth begins when the former way of living is acknowledged as no longer capable of continuing. The Nineteenth Archetype is the Hidden Saint, keeper of the Law of Anonymity. The Hidden Saint serves without title, radiates in silence, and may remain unseen while still being felt. The Hidden Saint does not turn generosity into evidence of personal virtue or make service dependent upon recognition. Appreciation may be received sincerely, but recognition must not become the reason for doing what is right. The Hidden Saint therefore represents the sacredness of unseen action—the good that is performed because it is good, the kindness that requires no witness, and the service that does not demand a name. The Twentieth Archetype is the Pilgrim Soul, keeper of the Law of the Eternal Traveler. The Pilgrim Soul travels with purpose, sees every path as sacred, and walks the unseen road inward and onward. The Eternal Traveler is awake to the road, attentive to signs and encounters, and rooted 160 inwardly rather than dependent upon temporary outer structures. The traveler learns that the body, name, possessions, circumstances, and worldly identities are passing forms. To live this Law is to travel lightly, to ask what may be blessed and laid down, and to carry forward not possessions alone but wisdom, wonder, love, and peace. The Twenty-First Archetype is the Flame of Immanence, keeper of the Law of Divine Presence. The Flame of Immanence sees the Divine in all, touches the holy in dust and wind, and dwells in the Here. Divine Presence is not presented as something that must arrive from a distant place; it is recognized as something that has never been absent. The Eternal may be encountered in breath, stillness, silence, nature, relationship, pain, joy, the stranger's voice, the falling leaf, and the difficult circumstance. Recognition of Divine Presence therefore becomes inseparable from reverence for existence and from the recognition of dignity in other living beings. The Divine is encountered not through possession but through awareness, service, compassion, and remembrance. The Twenty-Second Archetype is the Keeper of the Rose, keeper of the Law of the Rose. The Keeper of the Rose holds the secret, lives the doctrine, speaks little, and carries the Rose in the heart, sealed in silence. This is the archetype of embodiment: the one who no longer treats the doctrine merely as something to be discussed, but as something to be lived. The Rose becomes the flowering of the entire path—love, devotion, compassion, wisdom, forgiveness, beauty, service, truth, silence, presence, and remembrance becoming visible through the life of the practitioner. The Keeper does not claim to possess the Infinite; rather, the finite life becomes a vessel through which something of the Eternal may be recognized. Thus are the Twenty-Two Rosarian Archetypes declared: the Dawnbearer, the Silent Watcher, the Breathkeeper, the Purifier, the Mirror of Truth, the Untethered One, the Reflector, the Servant Flame, the Devoted Vessel, the Voice of Light, the Inner Lamp, the Nourisher, the Harmonist, the Surrendered Heart, the Presence-Walker, the Forgiver, the 161 Earth Listener, the Phoenix-Carrier, the Hidden Saint, the Pilgrim Soul, the Flame of Immanence, and the Keeper of the Rose. Each bears a Law, each Law opens a door, and each door leads deeper into remembrance. The Twenty-Two are therefore not separate paths but a single living circle. Dawn awakens the seeker; Silence teaches the seeker to listen; Breath teaches rhythm; Purity clears the way; Truth aligns the soul; Non-Attachment frees the hands; Reflection deepens understanding; Service turns realization outward; Devotion offers the whole life; Sacred Word gives intention to speech; Inner Light illuminates from within; Nourishment sustains what is living; Balance holds the center; Surrender releases what cannot be controlled; Sacred Time teaches presence; Forgiveness releases the chains of injury; Nature teaches rhythm and limitation; Death and Rebirth teach transformation; Anonymity purifies service of vanity; the Eternal Traveler teaches impermanence and inward pilgrimage; Divine Presence reveals the sacred within the Here; and the Rose gathers the whole doctrine into living embodiment. We therefore declare that the Rosarian Archetypes are living mirrors of the Twenty-Two Sacred Laws. They are not masks to be worn, nor ranks to be claimed, nor identities through which one may place oneself above another. They are disciplines of remembrance and forms of practice. One may encounter them throughout a lifetime, return to them repeatedly, discover one within another, and find that the Law once learned in thought must eventually become visible in conduct. The Dawn becomes the first light. The Silence becomes the listening heart. The Breath becomes the living rhythm. The Purifier clears the mirror. Truth becomes alignment. Freedom becomes the open hand. Reflection becomes humility. Service becomes the flame offered to others. Devotion becomes the vessel. Sacred Word becomes the voice. Inner Light becomes the lamp. Nourishment becomes care. Balance becomes the center. Surrender becomes trust. Presence becomes sacred time. Forgiveness becomes release. Nature becomes wisdom. 162 Death becomes transformation. Anonymity becomes hidden service. Pilgrimage becomes remembrance. Divine Presence becomes recognition. And finally, the Rose becomes the flowering of the whole. This is the Declaration of the Twenty-Two Rosarian Archetypes of the Twenty-Two Sacred Laws: one circle, twenty-two forms, one living doctrine, and one continual movement from awakening into remembrance, from remembrance into service, and from service into the flowering of the Rose.

items.title: The Near-Death Experience, an Instance of Higher-Dimensional Phenomenal Consciousness?
items.abstract: Phenomenal consciousness has no satisfactory explanation in the strict natural scientific physicalist framework. This may be an indication of consciousness not being a causal outcome of neurophysics at all. If this is the case, there would be no grounds for postulating that the collapse of neurophysical structures at death would dissolve consciousness and its constituent elements. If consciousness does not disappear when neurophysical functions terminate, the near-death experience could be an indication of the continuation of consciousness after the collapse of brain functions. This would be in line with the proposal that higher spatio-temporal dimensionality is involved in the emergence and maintenance of phenomenal consciousness, even after death.

items.title: The Metaphysics of Self-Causality.
items.abstract: This article proposes an idealist/panpsychist metaphysics which connects the integrated information theory of consciousness (IIT) with the work of the philosopher Arthur Schopenhauer: both frameworks describe the whole universe as consisting of different forms of auto-causation — or, as Schopenhauer termed it, ‘the Will’. IIT proposes that consciousness is self-causality: the ‘information’ being measured in a system (e.g. a set of neurons in the brain) is causality (that is, any difference that makes a difference in the future), while ‘integrated’ means the system ultimately has causal power over itself. Schopenhauer, too, claimed that all matter and energy consists of this kind of conscious self-causality, which makes sense according to Charles Darwin’s idea that what is extant is always that which self-perpetuates. The ‘is–ought problem’ is resolved in this article by explaining causality as valence, or the subjectively-experienced difference between good and bad (understood within this theory as satisfaction vs. frustration of causality from its own perspective).

items.title: Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game ｰ From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.
items.abstract: This paper explores consciousness as a causal puzzle. Where an investigation of water molecules examines their properties, this inquiry follows the relations that sustain a whirlpool. It shifts attention from identifying consciousness within the brain to tracing the causal organization that could sustain one subject's present and history. The tools are Occam's principle and subtraction. Place a body, an environment, and conditions for continued existence on the board, then remove the relations one by one. What ceases to be possible when a relation is removed? This paper calls the method of narrowing down necessary causal roles through such removal "proof by absence." The proposed linkage connects viability-related candidate competition, strong information discard, consequences, and continuation. Strong information discard means that incompatible losers irreversibly lose their standing to determine continuation at the same branch, not that their information is completely erased. The winner's consequences become the same system's conditions of continuation and influence subsequent candidate formation. A loser may remain as information without becoming realized history; a winner may disappear as information while its consequences remain effective. An engineering interpretation of death clarifies what viability constraints constrain: the conditions sustaining a specified organization and the boundary at which its continuation is lost. History thereby operates not only as a record, but as present conditions shaping subsequent possibilities. The convergence-point criterion traces the coupling among the unit whose candidates compete, the unit whose conditions change, and the unit that continues from those conditions. The internal reference point denotes the role through which carried consequences influence subsequent formation. Through correspondence with one present, the bearing of consequences, a single history, and internal reference, together with explanatory economy, the paper strongly infers that the system realizing this coupling constitutes the subjective container. Identifying necessary causal roles and identifying their realization with the subject are separate steps. The latter is not a deductive proof of experience or of the structure's uniqueness. The framework begins below human language, self-awareness, and deliberation. It hypothesizes that brains broadly and closely implement this loop and predicts shared functional organization across species. Comparisons with existing theories examine how their mechanisms connect to the same linkage. Appendix A develops artificial-system design conditions; Appendix B examines boundaries of realization through sleep, anesthesia, identity-state switching, and related cases. The remaining puzzle concerns qualia: through what mechanism does the inferred subject feel its perceptions? The framework directs this question toward perceptual processes participating in the formation of the present of a system that bears consequences and continues. It offers a starting hypothesis for an as-yet-unknown theory of perceptual information becoming an experienced event. This perspective paper grew from a puzzle pursued through dialogue with generative AI by a disability welfare worker outside academic consciousness research, after first learning about the hard problem. It presents causal reasoning without experimental validation. Its contribution is a proposed subject structure, criteria for comparison and testing, and a more concrete question about the emergence of felt experience.

items.title: How Meaning Turns Out-of-Body Experiences into Life Change: A Phenomenological Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Out-of-body experiences (OBEs) are vivid and extraordinary events that may lead to psychological transformation, though not all individuals who report them undergo lasting change. This qualitative study explores when and how OBEs become transformative. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten healthy adults who had experienced spontaneous OBEs. Thematic analysis focused on three variables: frequency, phenomenological complexity, and subjective interpretation. Findings suggest that transformation occurred only in those who reported complex OBEs involving both displacement and entities) and interpreted them within a transcendental framework. Participants with simple OBEs or a psychological interpretation showed no major change. All reported difficulties sharing their experience, often fearing disbelief or judgment. This highlights the importance of creating non-pathologizing environments where individuals can make meaning of such experiences, since interpretation appears to mediate their transformative impact.

items.title: Journalism for Democratic Attitudes.
items.pub: Journal of Ethics and Social Philosophy.
items.abstract: Journalism plays a crucial role in democracy. Unfortunately, democracy is in decline around the world. I argue for a normative-democratic ideal journalists can follow to promote attitudes that are crucial for democracy. My analysis runs through what Susanna Siegel calls salience principles: norms that determine what journalistic mass media puts forward as worthy of and demanding our attention. I begin by justifying three kinds of democratic attitude that are crucial for democracy from a variety of perspectives in democratic theory: knowledge of public affairs, the recognition of being part of a larger public, and mutual toleration. I then elaborate a normative ideal of salience principles that journalists should adhere to such that they facilitate these democratic attitudes. In addition to the Importance Principle and Public-as-Protagonist Principle suggested by Siegel, I propose that we should add one other salience principle (the Mutual Toleration Facilitation Principle) and an ancillary principle (the Democratic Motivation Principle). Throughout the paper, I give practical guidance to journalists as to how to adhere to the principles. Finally, I deal with the objection that adhering to the normative-democratic ideal I propose is financially infeasible for journalists.

items.title: Flights of Fancy: Comment on Eric Schwitzgebel’s The Weirdness of the World.
Outsourcing Emotions to GenAI: The Risk of Bypassing Identity Development.
items.abstract: There is growing research on how and when the use of Generative AI (henceforth GenAI) in cognitive tasks may lead to a decline in the users’ cognitive capacities. There is emerging evidence that Generative AI also presents us with the opportunity to outsource some emotional tasks, such as flirting on dating apps or apologising. We believe that this may enable unsuspecting users to outsource too much of their affective capacities. Here, we wish to focus on a particular problem: insofar as articulating our own emotions is essential to discovering what we value and thereby shaping what sorts of persons we are, users who are heavily dependent on GenAI for emotional tasks risk forgoing crucial opportunities to develop a proper sense of their own identity.

items.title: Clearing the Air About Psychedelic Spirituality.
items.abstract: Psychedelic-assisted therapy occasions mystical experiences and their intensity often predicts therapeutic outcomes. Owing to their spiritual import, psychedelics have been linked to supernatural thinking, religions, and cults. Several authors within the psychedelic field argue these associations render the field scientifically and ethically questionable, with some calling for the ‘mystical framework’ of therapy to be replaced. This paper examines the controversy surrounding psychedelic spirituality to diagnose the issue and offer proposals for easing tensions. We argue that the question of the veracity of mystical insights is the primary source of controversy, but is a philosophical rather than scientific question and can, for now, be bracketed. We also argue that despite the charge of guruism and cultishness, researchers should be free to hold personal beliefs about the truth of these insights. Given their profession, however, they ought to remain agnostic about such insights and maintain values and views inherent to the ethos of science in their professional conduct.

items.title: My AI Identity: When Human–AI Histories Become Non-Equivalent Operational Shapes.
items.abstract: This paper develops an operational account of AI identity by asking when a human–AI history becomes non-equivalent to another history even when the underlying model, architecture, or nominal agent remains the same. Rather than treating identity as persistence of substrate, model weights, memory storage, or self-description alone, the paper analyzes historical operational continuity: the retention, removal, reactivation, migration, and recurrence of relations that alter subsequent possibilities across changing configurations. Human–AI interaction histories become identity-relevant when their deletion, substitution, or reconstruction produces non-redundant differences in later behavior, inference, adaptation, recognition, or reachable states. The analysis therefore distinguishes stored history from operationally active history and tests whether apparently identical artificial systems remain substitutable after divergent trajectories of interaction. History fork, history removal, history reactivation, migration, and configuration-crossing recurrence provide cases for determining when continuity survives implementation change and when nominally identical systems become operationally non-equivalent. The paper connects these questions to classical problems of psychological continuity, memory, and personal identity while rejecting the assumption that biological persistence or human subjectivity must define the identity conditions of artificial systems. The broader claim is that AI identity should be analyzed through historically accumulated, configuration-dependent differences that continue to constrain future possibilities rather than through static architecture or instantaneous state alone.

items.title: Representational Realism is not the Default Position of Cognitive Neuroscience.
items.abstract: Mental representations figure prominently in cognitive neuroscience, and this prominence is often taken to imply an underlying commitment to robust representational realism: the view that representations are real neural entities bearing determinate content grounded in their physical properties. The present paper challenges this assumption on two fronts. First, I argue that robust realist approaches face principled limitations, such as overgeneralization, and struggle to accommodate the diversity and context-sensitivity of neuroscientific data. Second, I claim that robust realism is neither required nor typically presupposed in scientific practice, as researchers rarely adopt such strong ontological commitments. Moreover, I present an alternative position, representational pragmatism, which treats representations not as discrete entities but as idealized epistemic artefacts, namely modelling tools that enable intelligibility, guide experimentation, and support prediction. I contend that this approach is more consistent with both neuroscientific practice and empirical data. To illustrate these points, I articulate a set of widely accepted constraints on representational attribution and examine varitel semantics, a leading contemporary robust realist framework. I argue that it fails to meet these desiderata and cannot reconcile its commitments with empirical findings. This, I maintain, exemplifies a broader difficulty of robust realism: the fallacy of misplaced concreteness, whereby methodological abstractions are mistaken for literal features of neural architecture. Finally, I defend representational pragmatism as a more viable and scientifically grounded stance that also fares better on representational desiderata. I conclude that if there is a “default scientific position”, it appears more pragmatist than robust realist.

items.title: Filsafat dan Sains Kesadaran.
Emotion, Consciousness, and the Heart–Brain Connection: A Quantum Biological Perspective.
items.abstract: Understanding human consciousness and emotion requires an interdisciplinary approach that can involve topics from neuroscience, physiology, and even quantum biology. This article proposes an integrative theory in which emotion is defined broadly as a concept that can capture different phenomena arising from brain activity, from instinctual affective responses to higher cognitive feelings, and considers how similar principles may apply to the heart’s intrinsic nervous system. We review evidence that the heart, with its own network of neurons, communicates with the brain to influence emotions and conscious experience. In this view, consciousness is considered as a complex phenomenon arising from the brain’s neurons and from a dynamic brain–heart system in which bodily states (especially cardiac signals) are represented in the brain to influence the creation of feelings of self and sentience. We further explore recent quantum biology perspectives on consciousness, which suggest that quantum-level processes in neurons (e.g. microtubule quantum states or nuclear spin dynamics) might contribute to the emergence of mind. Preliminary connections to the philosophy of mind are examined, particularly how the exposed ideas address the ‘hard problem’ of consciousness and revive dual aspect and panpsychist interpretations. We discuss how heart–brain interactions and quantum processes together might provide new connections with conscious experience — including the age-old intuition of the ‘heart’ as an organ of wisdom and emotion.

items.title: The Structure of Multidimensional Concepts.
items.abstract: Recent work in philosophy and cognitive science has brought renewed attention to multidimensional concepts and properties such as healthy and democratic. In this paper, we take steps toward a comprehensive theory of them. Much of the existing literature treats multidimensionality piecemeal, isolating particular features. Most prominently, multidimensional concepts appear to involve forms of aggregation structurally akin to those studied in social choice theory. While this insight is illuminating, it stops short of explaining what dimensions are and how they contribute to concept application. This under-theorization gives rise to puzzles about how, exactly, standard social choice principles should be interpreted in the multidimensional setting. Our aim is to embed the aggregative module within a broader framework that accounts for the characteristic features of multidimensional concepts and reconciles them with social choice principles that might otherwise appear to stand in tension with them.

items.title: Replies to a fellow expressivist and two fellow inferentialists.
items.abstract: We respond to the comments by Imogen Dickie, Matthew Chrisman and Christine Tiefensee for a book symposium on our Reasoning with Attitude. Our commentators attempt to pull us further into either expressivism or into inferentialism. Here, we attempt to resist either pull and further establish our inferential expressivism as a home for both expressivists and inferentialists.

items.title: Consciousness as Computable Projections of State.
items.abstract: We propose an analysis of consciousness stated in terms of systems, states, canonical projections, and computability. Let S have state x = (s₁, ..., sₙ), and let Projᵢ(x) = sᵢ be the canonical projection of its ith component. A component sᵢ is conscious for S if and only if Projᵢ is computable by S. The consciousness of S is therefore the family Cₛ = (Projᵢ₁, ..., Projᵢₖ) of its internally computable state projections, while Cₛ(x) = (sᵢ₁, ..., sᵢₖ) is its current state of consciousness. The analysis distinguishes a component's existence and causal efficacy from its presence for the system; distinguishes the capacity to compute projections from their current values and actual executions; and makes system boundaries and state specification logically prior to consciousness. An elementary C program supplies the derivation rather than a metaphor. Reports and answers provide operational evidence of computability but do not constitute consciousness or its elementary occurrences. An elementary conscious phenomenon is an execution by the system of a computable canonical state projection. The same criterion applies to organisms, programs, and AI agents; hence simple programs can be conscious of components of their own states. This is a consequence of the analysis, not an attribution of subjective experience. We compare the proposal with higher-order, self-representational, global-workspace, recurrent, attention-schema, and computational-reflection accounts, and state the conditions for a genuine counterexample. -/- .

items.title: Learning from the past: epistemic generativity and the function of episodic memory.
items.abstract: I argue that the function of episodic memory is to store information about the past, against the orthodox view that it is to support imagining the future. I show that episodic memory is epistemically generative, allowing organisms to learn from past events retroactively. This confers adaptive benefits in three domains: Reasoning about the world, skill, and social interaction. Given the role of evolutionary perspectives in comparative research, this argument necessitates a radical shift in the study of episodic memory in nonhumans.

items.title: To Whom Do Thought, Memory, and Position Belong? — Address-Domain Re-Ignition, Configurational Transformation and Expiration of Commitments, Hyper-Decompositional Configurational Operationalism, and XenoThinking.
items.abstract: This paper asks to whom—or to what configuration—thought, memory, and position belong when their persistence cannot be identified with the continuous existence of a single subject, body, biological organism, or computational implementation. Rather than presupposing an owner of mental or inferential states, the paper tracks the address-domains in which distinctions, memories, commitments, and positions are retained, transformed, reactivated, or rendered operationally unavailable. Address-domain re-ignition occurs when a previously instantiated operational relation becomes consequential again in a new configuration without requiring numerical identity of its original carrier. Memory is therefore distinguished from mere storage: a retained difference counts as operational memory only when its reactivation changes subsequent possibilities. Commitments are similarly treated as configuration-dependent inferential constraints whose force can persist, migrate, transform, or expire when the conditions required for their application disappear. Hyper-Decompositional Configurational Operationalism provides a method for decomposing apparently unified subjects, memories, and positions into the minimal relations required for their persistence and re-instantiation. XenoThinking extends the analysis beyond human cognition by asking whether thought-like operations can recur across artificial, distributed, hybrid, or otherwise nonhuman address-domains. The broader claim is that ownership should not be assumed as the primitive relation connecting thought, memory, and commitment to a subject; attribution must instead be reconstructed from the configurations in which historically retained differences regain the capacity to constrain inference, action, and future reachability.

items.title: Which Operational Bundles Become Nonredundant as “Neural Organization,” “Intelligence,” and “Memory”? — Electrical Threshold Ignition, History Dependence, Media Substitution, Xenomemory, and Situated Ignition Conditions Across Biological and Artificial Substrates.
items.abstract: This paper asks which operational bundles become nonredundant when heterogeneous biological and artificial systems are classified in terms of “neural organization,” “intelligence,” and “memory.” Rather than presupposing that these terms designate fixed natural kinds or substrate-independent functions, the analysis decomposes them into configuration-dependent operations involving threshold activation, signal propagation, retention, history dependence, recurrent re-entry, adaptive weighting, discrimination, and modification of subsequent possibilities. Electrical threshold ignition provides a test case for determining when distributed physical processes become organized into functionally consequential transitions without assuming in advance that neural tissue is the privileged implementation. History dependence distinguishes stored state from operational memory by requiring prior differences to remain capable of altering later behavior or reachable states. Media substitution then tests whether these relations survive migration across biological, electronic, computational, or hybrid substrates and identifies where apparently equivalent implementations cease to be substitutable. Xenomemory names the broader class of history-dependent operational structures whose persistence and reactivation need not depend on a particular biological memory architecture. The paper therefore distinguishes substrate independence from unrestricted functional equivalence: similar outcomes may depend on different operational bundles, while apparently different media may preserve the same nonredundant historical relation. The broader claim is that neural organization, intelligence, and memory should be identified through situated ignition conditions and experimentally consequential operational differences rather than by prior commitment to biological or artificial substrates.

items.title: Does Local Optimization of the Present Body Contract the Space of Future Bodily Possibilities? Xeno-14 Body Principles, Reachability of Unexpressed Regimes, Latent Body Suppression, Regime Lock-In, and Fragility Transfer.
items.abstract: This paper asks whether local optimization of the present body can contract the space of future bodily possibilities. Rather than evaluating bodily organization solely by current performance, efficiency, strength, stability, or task success, it analyzes how repeated optimization can alter the set of bodily regimes that remain reachable later. The Xeno-14 Body Principles provide a test framework for examining posture, balance, gait, tension distribution, breathing, sensory organization, movement initiation, whole-body coordination, and long-duration bodily sedimentation without assuming that one optimized bodily state should dominate all others. The paper introduces the reachability of unexpressed regimes to designate bodily organizations that are not currently manifested but remain accessible under alternative configurations. Latent body suppression occurs when repeated stabilization of one regime raises the transition cost or removes the conditions required for alternative regimes to ignite. Regime lock-in describes the resulting persistence of a locally successful organization after its advantages have become configuration-specific, while Fragility Transfer identifies cases in which increased robustness or performance in one bodily dimension relocates vulnerability to another movement, scale, temporal interval, or future configuration. The broader claim is that bodily optimization should be evaluated not only by present performance but by its effects on the topology of future bodily reachability: an intervention can improve the current body while simultaneously reducing the diversity, reversibility, and adaptability of bodies that the same configuration could later become.

items.title: Settling Brains with Attention: Deep Neural Networks That Learn During Life.
items.abstract: A robot that works among people needs a brain that learns while it acts and finds what it needs in its own past, as animal brains do. Most deployed machine learning does not: its networks are trained by backpropagation and then frozen, and a transformer attends over a cache that grows with the context. Cadence is an open-source library of biologically inspired neural networks that learn during life, in real time. This paper describes it as a whole, aiming to make such networks powerful and scalable. A Cadence brain is one continuing network of regions joined by reciprocal synapses. With its senses held fixed, its neurons repair their local disagreements until the network rests in one equilibrium, which is its answer. Learning compares two nearby equilibria: a small nudge on the motor neurons travels back over the reciprocal synapses, and each synapse changes from the activity at its two ends, with no backward pass. In a deep brain the top-down half of each pair lands on an apical compartment, bounded to a share of the bottom-up drive; where depth pays, each added region raises accuracy, and four regions reach 0.86 against 0.89 for a two-layer backpropagation network. A dopamine-like prediction error drives reward learning, and arousal from surprise and unmet need decides when the creature explores, learns and writes memory. Like every purely recurrent network, settled activity must compress its past, so Cadence adds synaptic memory read by learned attention. Beside a working trace and an episodic memory, a recall memory keeps its recent moments verbatim as slots, keyed by the observation or by a code of meaning learned by settling, each holding an event and its successor. Before each settle one or several heads form a query from the present and the previous interpretation, weigh the slots by a softmax over the match and a learned term for each slot's age, and hold the read while the brain settles. Queries, age terms and codes learn during life by local rules, and the memory's cost per moment does not grow with the life. Read with its successor, the memory is an induction head, and the age term makes order answerable: questions about first, last and how long ago reach 0.9 to 1.0 in sequence tasks, stories and a survival world where lessons teach them. Composing reads within one moment and learning where to look from reward alone are measured as missing. Proofs establish what settling guarantees in a plainly summed network.

items.title: Empathy in Parallel Carnivores: A Naturalistic Neurobiological Model of Human-Animal Attachment.
items.abstract: Humans and dogs share a unique form of emotional resonance shaped by parallel facultative carnivory, cooperative evolution, and overlapping affective architecture. This perspective develops the Affective Carnivore Hypothesis, a naturalistic model proposing that human-animal empathy emerges from the interaction between trophic physiology, endocannabinoid modulation, and psychoplastogen-driven neuroplasticity. Carnivore-aligned diets stabilise glucose, reduce inflammation, increase BDNF, and strengthen prefrontal-amygdala regulation, supporting emotional clarity and accurate perception of nonverbal cues. Cannabis further enhances empathic salience, limbic resonance, and interoceptive awareness. Natural psychoplastogens expand relational capacity via dendritic spine growth, synaptogenesis, and enhanced limbic-prefrontal integration. This model is grounded in phenomenology, drawing on lived relational evidence from Buddha, Zen, and Bubba, whose companionship revealed how diet, affective modulation, and neuroplasticity manifest in real-world human-animal attachment. Volunteering at The DogFather Animal Rescue provided behavioural validation, illustrating how stable affective architecture supports calm handling, attunement, and prosocial caregiving. This work proposes that empathy between parallel carnivores is not merely sentimental, but biological: an emergent property of shared evolution, shared physiology, and shared affective mechanisms.

items.title: Finite Continuance and the Modal Structure of Reconfiguration Counterparts, Persistence, and the Preservation of Future Possibility.
items.abstract: Modal metaphysics traditionally asks which ways things could have been and how individuals relate to their possible alternatives. David Lewis's counterpart theory addresses the problem of de re modality by rejecting transworld identity in favor of counterpart relations between individuals in different possible worlds. This paper develops a complementary problem that emerges when modality is considered from the perspective of finite and historically situated entities: what conditions preserve the capacity of an entity to reach, generate, or sustain future configurations that remain possible for it? Drawing on the ontology of finite continuance, the paper distinguishes modal possibility, reconfigurational accessibility, and continuational viability. Modal possibility concerns what can obtain within an appropriate modal framework. Reconfigurational accessibility concerns whether a determinate finite structure possesses a historically available pathway toward a configuration. Continuational viability concerns whether such a transition can occur while preserving sufficient capacity for further reconfiguration. The paper introduces the concept of modal meta-capacity, defined as the capacity of a finite structure to preserve the conditions under which future configurations remain generable, accessible, and viable. This concept extends the distinction between capacity and meta-capacity developed within the ontology of finite continuance into the domain of modal metaphysics. The resulting framework explains how a configuration may remain modally possible while becoming inaccessible to a historically determinate entity through erosion, temporal asymmetry, hysteresis, and loss of connectivity. The paper argues that counterpart theory and finite continuance address different explanatory relations and can therefore be placed in systematic dialogue. The proposed framework contributes to discussions of modality, persistence, identity, accessibility, and the metaphysics of change by shifting attention from the inventory of alternative states toward the preservation of the conditions under which future alternatives remain accessible. Keywords: finite continuance; modality; counterpart theory; David Lewis; possible worlds; persistence; reconfiguration; meta-capacity; modal accessibility; erosion; identity.

items.title: THE BODY WITHOUT COMMANDS XenoBody: Eight Operational Axes, Embodied Access, and Human Operational Anatomy Xeno-Embodied Askesis and Fourteen Operational Cuts.
items.abstract: This monograph investigates how an instruction can participate in the formation of a bodily capacity and later cease to be required, while the material, observational and normative conditions of that capacity continue to change. A human-readable cue supplies a tractable intervention; it does not define a universal body. The human study remains prospective. The wider XenoBody architecture asks how a body-relevant organization forms, acquires access, changes its partitions and redistributes dependencies across human and nonhuman configurations. A material bodily organization, an ordinarily warranted body attribution, a locally warranted activation of Xenobodiment and an exclusive explanatory ontology are distinct. V19 made a protected, task-relative contribution beyond specified body-free comparators necessary for Xenobodiment as a research concept; R36 restores that condition rather than reclassifying it as a merely optional bonus. This does not entail that a living body ceases to exist when its functioning can be explained mechanistically. A still stronger claim of irreducibility to every possible rival requires a different argument and is not established. These levels, their failure conditions and their relation to the original source are kept explicit throughout the book. The architecture begins before operation or body is granted. A provisional target-side order distinguishes real difference, physical transformation of difference, discriminability, addressability, and access to later coupling. Operation and operational shape are introduced only when retained or recurrent organization makes consequential transitions trackable. Three checkpoints remain nonidentical: transition onset, analytic concept re-entry, and operational concept ignition. Every determination remains indexed to a local access configuration K rather than identified with an exhaustive body or final observational standpoint. Access redesign makes that indexing experimentally active. Sensor substitution, boundary perturbation, scale and interval variation, intervention-path and representation substitution, and role or medium exchange are used to test whether a body determination survives, requires restriction, splits into more than one operative unit, or expires. Reality-as-a-whole functions only as a scope and non-closure operator. Truth, access, and access-training remain distinct, and every apparent gain is separately evaluated for changed dependencies, revision capacity, and fragility transfer. The monograph adds embodied access generation as a further research object. A body-relevant configuration can be the target of measurement, part of the access arrangement through which differences become discriminable, and a carrier or transformer of later consequences. These roles must not be collapsed. Improved task performance does not establish increased access; increased access does not establish that the body concept is necessary; a local effect does not establish reality penetration.
