A Stage-D protocol therefore tests whether posture, movement, morphology, active sampling, memory, maintenance, or body-environment coupling changes sensitivity, threshold, addressability, or intervention reach beyond response bias, generic attention, measurement error, and trivial stimulus amplification. The fourteen inherited principles have different experimental roles: intervention tokens, organization constraints, diagnostic manipulations, generalization regimes and a terminal criterion. In the human branch, 'command' means a human-readable instructional scaffold. A reproducible configuration signature, predictive relevance, perturbational relevance and mechanistically constrained causal relevance are four distinct evidence levels. Successful removal of external presentation supports a narrower claim than nonrequirement of tested internal reconstruction. Both require viable performance, valid manipulations and prespecified inference; demonstrating that an instruction has become unnecessary additionally requires evidence of its earlier necessity under a justified longitudinal comparison. The comparison with motor learning, control, embodiment, robotics, active sensing and scientific automation yields six linked arguments. Human operational anatomy then separates material continuation, changing access and functional or normative attribution. Its analytical replacement case does not establish exclusive point-assemblage necessity. The restored XenoBody × XenoSNN corpus supplies bounded synthetic computations, adverse results and parity cases. R27's common-input replay is retained. R28 adds a separately coded ordinary histogram learner that matches the selector on all 76,800 retained input episodes, and a retrospective scheduler comparison on those same 80 streams. Different timing rules change service outcomes without changing classification. These results delimit a model-specific claim; they do not establish physical bodily efficacy, posthuman disconnection or strong Xenoscience. The separately recovered R29 countermodels distinguish formative benefit, earlier necessity, present nonrequirement, viable operation and regime-specific loss. R30 integrates and replays those records without turning their stipulated scores into empirical learning results. R31 adds exact countermodels of joint withdrawal and of a zero group interaction despite meaningful loss in both groups. These constrain the scope of nonrequirement; they add no human observations or special control mechanism.

items.title: Draining the Data Pool. Why Larger Samples Need Not Always Be Better.
items.abstract: It is commonplace to bemoan small studies in empirical fields, and to call for larger sample sizes, for example by pooling data within large-scale collaborations. However, while higher-powered studies are individually more reliable, we show that, under conditions of data scarcity, they can make scientific communities less reliable by reducing theoretical diversity. Our results build on a formal model introduced for science by Kevin Zollman, which we adapt, stringently interpret, and partially de-idealize to address worries about its real-life significance. We conclude that collaborative pooling is only beneficial up to some (context-dependent) point and argue against one-size-fits-all norms about sample size.

items.title: What Operational Shape Remains When Mind, Cognition, and Reason Are Decomposed? A Reconstruction through Minimal Operations, Minimal Notation, Configurational Conditions, Real Effects, Penetration, Feedback, and Reorganization.
items.abstract: This paper asks what operational structure remains when the inherited concepts of mind, cognition, and reason are decomposed rather than assumed as unified starting points. The analysis begins from minimal operations of discrimination, retention, transition, weighting, coupling, recurrence, branching, and reconfiguration, and asks under what configurational conditions these operations become sufficient for more complex forms of cognition and rational activity to emerge. Mind, cognition, and reason are therefore treated as distinct but partially overlapping operational intervals rather than interchangeable capacities. Cognition is reconstructed through the organization and reuse of differences that guide later discrimination and action, while reason is reserved for configurations in which inferential, justificatory, incompatibility-sensitive, and revision-governed constraints become non-redundant. Minimal notation is used to preserve only the operational distinctions required for comparison across heterogeneous biological, artificial, and hybrid systems. Real effects and penetration identify cases in which locally organized cognitive or rational differences alter downstream physical, informational, institutional, or social possibilities, while feedback and reorganization track how those altered configurations modify the conditions for subsequent cognition and reasoning. The broader claim is that decomposing mind, cognition, and reason does not eliminate their differences: it clarifies the operational intervals in which each becomes necessary and the conditions under which lower-level descriptions cease to be sufficient.

items.title: ALPHA-AXIS INTELLIGENCE VS. HORIZONTAL INTELLIGENCE: Knowledge, Wisdom, Origination, and the Limits of Acquired Intelligence.
items.abstract: What if the most important form of intelligence is not the ability to know more, but the ability to recognize when the question itself is wrong? Alpha-Axis Intelligence vs. Horizontal Intelligence develops a new framework for distinguishing accumulated knowledge, cognitive power, wisdom, and origination. Moving across philosophy, artificial intelligence, ancient intellectual traditions, psychology, and the problem of beginnings, the paper asks what happens when intelligence becomes extraordinarily capable inside a framework it did not create. In an age of machine abundance, that question becomes increasingly urgent: how do we distinguish greater performance from a genuinely different kind of thought? -/- .

items.title: SN05 — The Metric Cost of Centropic Cognition: Interface Resistance, Structural Sovereignty, and Temporal Pathology at the Embodiment Band.
items.abstract: The Metric Cost of Centropic Cognition examines embodied cognitive expenditure through interface resistance, structural sovereignty and temporal disruption. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume applies coherence-budget and interface-resistance constructions to high-pattern-fidelity, recursive, distributive and composite cognitive architectures within a Khaonically-expressed field. Its account relates cumulative depletion to the coherence tax, impaired operative access and the burnout trajectory while preserving the distinction between structural cost and clinical diagnosis. Recursive Memory remains an injective sealed-state mapping; former scalar-memory constructions are retired from operative mathematics and retained as recorded provenance. Composite-cost implications, numerical diagnostics and general Shimmer dynamics retain their specified holds, and clinical correspondences require operationalization and empirical evaluation. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: Dark as Reality.
items.abstract: This is a work of hard physical philosophy, in which we analyze Dark through the lenses of theoretical physics while offering a novel interpretation of existentialism, using the show's framework as a setup. In this reality, we assert the supremacy of quantum entanglement over time and causality, where Nietzsche's eternal recurrence is realized as an Einstein-Bell quantum time loop which respects Novikov's self-consistency principle. The Übermensch emerges as a singular meta-perspective external to the system, transcending the deterministic dynamics of the loop. -/- Free will, in this context, is perspectival—valid locally within the loop, while global determinism reigns. More precisely, causality, though locally consistent, aligns more closely with Jung's concept of synchronicity . In our unitary physical model of the system, the loop exists in two states: an eternally deterministic recurrence driven by quantum entanglement and a singularity-seeded loop that functions as its observer enabling its decoherence after a potential infinity $T_{\infty}$. The loop's collapse, following this model, is still inherently probabilistic, adhering to Born's rule. -/- The most profound metaphysical insight from this quantum loop is that consciousness itself is an evolutionary blunder—a realization paradoxically most unavoidable for those birthed by the loop. This awareness lies at the heart of existential angst and the pervasive fear of death. -/- Hence, quantum entanglement holds supremacy over time, causality, and consciousness, forming the foundation of this reality and the root of its archetypes. The only escape from its grasp lies in a true fourth singularity: the emergence of an Übermensch.

items.title: Misattributed Sharedness: How a Single Reaction Produces the Feeling of "We".
items.abstract: Theories of collective belief require more than one person. Searle's we-intentions are primitive; Gilbert's plural subject requires joint commitment; Echterhoff's shared reality requires a represented partner. This paper proposes a route these accounts do not specify: misattributed sharedness. Under five conditions — publicness, time-lock, uncontradictedness, evaluative recognizability, and identification — a single reaction by an identified other produces a distinctively intersubjective belief: not "others agree" but "this is ours." The mechanism is specified. Its central assumption — that third-party reactions are default-attributed to the object rather than the reactor — is reframed as a conditional, falsifiable claim. The acceptance precondition is given measurable determinants. The construct is distinguished from shared reality by the category-versus-mind representation. A dissociation design separates numerical from intersubjective sharedness, and a bot-control condition discriminates against collective meta-attention. The paper commits to a specific empirical test.

items.title: The Diamond — What Vibrates, Remembers, Illuminates (Vibration · Memory · Light).
items.abstract: Le Diamant (The Diamond) follows one question across three levels: are rest, conservation and perception what they appear to be? -/- I · Vibration (thesis): nothing is at rest. Matter holds through a prohibition, Pauli exclusion, from which Dyson and Lenard, then Lieb and Thirring, derive the stability of matter. The ground state keeps its zero-point motion (Heisenberg, Kennard), helium does not freeze at ordinary pressure, the vacuum shifts the electron's energy level (Lamb and Retherford) and draws two plates together (Casimir force, measured by Lamoreaux; its interpretation remains debated). De Broglie and Schrödinger give matter its frequency and its stationary states. -/- II · Memory (antithesis): nothing is kept as it is. Synaptic molecules are renewed within hours to days (Crick's question: how does something last when its parts do not?); the trace holds through its links (Hebb; Bliss and Lømo). A recalled memory becomes labile again (reconsolidation: Nader, Schafe and LeDoux), recall can distort it (Loftus), and a memory that has become inaccessible can still be reactivated artificially (Ryan and Tonegawa). At night, the hippocampus replays the day (Wilson and McNaughton), slow waves travel across the cortex (Massimini and Tononi), an odour replayed during sleep strengthens the memory learned with it (Rasch and Born), and sleep mainly benefits memories announced as useful (Wilhelm and Born); dopamine weighs on what enters memory (Lisman and Grace). -/- III · Light (synthesis): colour is not where we think it is. Light is an electromagnetic wave (Maxwell), it travels without using up a second of proper time (Einstein), and it can be slowed to 17 m/s, then stopped, in a cloud of ultracold atoms (Hau); a few photons are enough for the eye (Hecht, Shlaer and Pirenne), the blue of the sky comes from scattering (Rayleigh), the rainbow from the droplet (Descartes). Perception needs a source, a carrier and a decoder, and the product of the three. Diamond, the same carbon as graphite, shows that everything lies in the arrangement. -/- "Light is what is born when vibration remembers." (E. Sorel, 2026) -/- Five marks separate the registers: ESTABLISHED, DEBATED, HYPOTHESIS, READING, CALCULATION. The text ends with three falsifiable hypotheses, each with what would refute it. 13 figures, 166 references. In French. -/- Version 2.6 (19 October 2026): the text of 12 September 2026, revised and expanded, same three parts.

items.title: The institutional nature of law: an ontological analysis.
items.abstract: This project develops an ontological analysis of law. It starts by characterising law as a layered practice constituted by the performance of various types of group activities at two levels: the social and the institutional. At the social level, it examines the conditions for social groups to create and sustain standards of conduct through normative social practices of recognition. At the institutional level, the investigation moves to the conditions required for legal organisations to carry out the legal activities that constitute a legal practice. These two levels are studied through the lenses of ontological accounts of social groups, group action, and collective intentionality. In the first part of the project, Hart’s Social Practice Theory of Law is discussed. His theory is used to present a social facts-based explanation of law’s reality and to introduce a fundamental element in the social construction of law: the internal point of view. Though this theory provides the groundwork for the analysis of certain essential properties of law, this project argues that it lacks an account of how legal organisations are created. To fill in this gap, this project considers next MacCormick’s Institutional Theory of Law. By discussing each of its main elements, it is shown that, while his theory improves on Hart’s by introducing an explanation of both how institutional groups come into existence and how they are involved in the creation and maintenance of an institutional normative order, it needs further development. Specifically, an account of the different forms of group structures and the participatory intentions involved in the performance of legal activities is needed. This is addressed in the second part of the project, which is dedicated to advancing a thorough analysis of the social construction of law based on the merits of these prominent legal theories. In the last three chapters of this thesis, novel accounts of collective intentionality and the ontology of social groups and group action are explored and used to provide the elements missing in MacCormick’s legal institutionalism. In particular, this project considers Thomasson’s work on the metaphysics of artifacts to address problems concerning the ontological status of social constructions; Tuomela’s theory of social practices and we-intentions to develop an explanation of how sociality is constructed out of group attitudes and group actions; Ludwig’s analysis of institutional agency to explain the constitutive elements based on which institutional groups perform rule-governed group activities; and Ritchie’s theory of organised groups to clarify the various kinds of group structures involved in law-activities. The result of this project is a fresh, interdisciplinary theory of the institutional nature of law.

items.title: Shared intentionality and the cooperative evolutionary hypothesis.
items.abstract: One important application of theories of collective intentionality concerns the evolution of social understanding and even of human thinking (Tomasello M, A natural history of human thinking, Harvard University Press, Cambridge, MA, 2014). A promising idea behind this approach is the Cooperative Evolutionary Hypothesis (CEH), namely, the idea that humans’ capacity for social cooperation is at the heart of their ability to understand others’ mental states and behavior, leading to an explanation of how humans came to share thoughts and language. However, some of the most popular defenses of CEH face important problems. In this paper, we take Tomasello’s account (J Soc Ontol 2(1):117–123, 2016); A natural history of human thinking. Harvard University Press, Cambridge, MA, 2014; Origins of human communication. MIT Press, Cambridge, MA, 2008) as a leading example of the CEH which faces such insurmountable problems. In particular, we argue that Tomasello’s analysis of cooperation and spontaneous help is problematic. We locate a source of such issues in the assumption that the right account of joint action and simple forms of shared intentionality is that which is offered by Bratman’s theory of shared intentions. The second part of the article proposes and defends an alternative framework for understanding shared intentionality that can help substantiate CEH.

items.title: The Phenomenology of the Mask and Finite Continuance: An Ontological-Ethical Reading of Stanley Kubrick's Eyes Wide Shut.
items.abstract: This article develops an ontological-ethical reading of Stanley Kubrick's Eyes Wide Shut (1999) through the concepts of Finite Continuance and Dynamic Mask Theory. It argues that the film's philosophical centre is not the revelation of what lies behind the mask, but the question of whether finite subjects can continue responsibly when complete access to the other is impossible. Engaging critically with existing Kubrick scholarship—psychoanalytic, feminist, philosophical, and Deleuzian—the article proposes a new framework that moves beyond readings of the film as a dream, a conspiracy, or a study in jealousy. The mask is analysed as a mediating structure that temporarily organises identity, desire, social position, vulnerability, and access. The masked ritual at Victor Ziegler's mansion is examined as an extreme configuration of Form-Monopoly, in which institutionalised form regulates who may appear, participate, recognise, and remain within a given relational field. Four scene-specific analyses—of the Ziegler party, the confession sequence, the masked ritual, and the final exchange—demonstrate how Kubrick's cinematic form (lighting, framing, sound design, duration, and camera movement) enacts the very ontological leakage the article theorises. A Deleuzian reading of the film's slow temporality further reveals how the time-image suspends sensory-motor continuity, opening experience to the pure optical and sonic situations that structure epistemic opacity. The article anticipates and addresses three potential criticisms of the Finite Continuance framework: its alleged neglect of social and political dimensions, its resistance to normative evaluation, and its potential cultural particularity. Alice Harford's confession concerning an imagined sexual encounter is distinguished from evidence of participation in the ritual: her desire is significant precisely because an imagined possibility can transform the relational field without becoming an external event. The concluding exchange between William and Alice is interpreted through Responsible Suspension and the Ethics of Sufficiency. Their relationship does not survive because uncertainty is eliminated, but because exhaustive certainty ceases to function as the necessary condition of continuation. Eyes Wide Shut thus becomes a philosophical investigation into how finite subjects can preserve relational agency when complete access to another person remains impossible. -/- Keywords: Eyes Wide Shut, Stanley Kubrick, Finite Continuance, Dynamic Mask Theory, ontological leakage, structural subjectivity, recursive intentionality, Responsible Suspension, Ethics of Sufficiency, Form-Monopoly, Levinasian ethics, epistemic opacity, homeorhetic continuance, meta-capacity, Deleuzian time-image.

items.title: Teleological Emergence and the Ethics of Sufficiency Reconfiguring Agency under Chronic Erosion and Faceless Evil.
items.abstract: This article articulates a comprehensive philosophical framework addressing the crisis of human agency in late modernity, characterized by chronic instability, algorithmic governance, and structural erosion. Moving beyond the classical dichotomy of process versus purpose, this paper advances the concept of teleological emergence, arguing that purpose is not a pre-given telos but a provisional stabilization generated within ongoing processes of leakage, masking, and reconfiguration. Central to this framework is the Dynamic Mask, reconceived not as a mechanism of deception, but as the mediating structure through which indeterminate potentiality achieves determinate orientation via recursive intentionality. Furthermore, the article offers a structured differentiation of contemporary moral crises by specifying what the Arendtian banality of evil, the Baumanian analysis of structural distance, and the present framework's concept of faceless evil each contribute, introducing algorithmic pre-emption and the Threshold of Sufficiency as irreducible variables. In response, the framework proposes an Ethics of Sufficiency grounded in situated responsibility. This normative stance rejects both Sartrean absolute responsibility and consequentialist teleology, advocating instead for the preservation of the existential conditions that allow finite beings to sustain homeorhetic continuity and moral responsiveness. Keywords: teleological emergence, dynamic mask, finite continuance, situated responsibility, faceless evil, ethics of sufficiency, homeorhesis, recursive intentionality, algorithmic pre-emption.

items.title: The Ontology of Yi-Dao: A Constructive Philosophical System of the Changes, the Dao, and Number.
items.abstract: The Ontology of Yi-Dao is a constructive philosophical system of the Changes (Yi), the Dao, and Number. It distinguishes the "Substance of the Dao" (before differentiation, falling into neither 0 nor 1) from the "Function of the Dao" (after differentiation, being both 0 and 1), and establishes the ontological status of Taiji as the first observer endowed with "meta-awareness." Taking the Dao's temporal rhythm of "0→1→0" and the recursive generation of 2ⁿ as its logical skeleton, it presents the evolutionary path of all things in the cosmos; the Taiji Diagram serves as the embodiment of the law of causality, corresponding to the two ultimate ethical principles of justice and benevolence. It constructs an ontological four-dimensional view of space-time, divides the perceptual layers of "Primordial Spirit–Yin-Yang Qi (soul)–Consciousness" and the corresponding three-tiered personality types, and undertakes a study of the theory and norms of application of the method of embodied verification (tizhengfa). In Chapter Seven, "Cultivation and Realization" (The Taste of Time), it expounds on life-philosophical questions such as religious language, God, mind-nature cultivation, free will, divine play, and the meaning of life. The Ontology of Yi-Dao provides a new theoretical reference for the systematization of traditional Chinese culture, for Perennial Philosophy, and for comparative religious studies, and offers inspiration for many predicaments of the Western philosophical tradition.

items.title: 体验先于思考.
items.abstract: 本文从“体验先于思考”这一基本经验出发，论证了体验与思考在时间上的先后性并非注意力分配问题，而是系统状态更新的结构性必然。基于此，本文提出了一个基于状态递归的意识与存在形式化模型，旨在以最少预设统一推导意识、逻辑、自我、时间及心物关系等一系列核心概念。 模型的核心方程为 $S_n = f(S_{n-1}, W_n)$，即系统在时刻 $n$ 的状态 $S_n$ 由前一状态 $S_{n-1}$ 与环境输入 $W_n$ 经内禀反应函数 $f$ 生成。本文严格区分了体验（时刻 $n$ 的方程执行本身）与思考（以已有状态为对象的后续反应），从而确立了“体验先于思考”的结构性必然。在此基础上，本文提出四大核心主张：（1）意识即反应：一切满足核心方程的系统皆在意识，意识只有复杂度高低而无本体论鸿沟，消解了意识/无意识二分及泛心论组合问题；（2）逻辑即差异结构：逻辑是状态内部新旧并置的 A/非 A 结构，从第一次状态更新起便已存在，反思仅为同一反应函数在复杂度足够时的递归深化，不存在“逻辑涌现”事件；（3）生成覆盖生成：心与物是同一实体在不同嵌套关系中的角色，查尔默斯的“困难问题”因预设心物二元而在逻辑上被消解；（4）时间即因果深度：主观时间感与状态差异密度成正比，时间箭头源于递归函数的不可逆性（噪声、有损压缩与参数漂移）。 本文进一步将模型应用于休谟归纳、他心问题、自由意志、个人同一性、因果闭合、道德地位等十余个哲学难题，展示了其消解或重新解释的能力，并汇总了可检验推论。通过四组数值仿真（逻辑涌现窗口、时间感知与差异密度、离散逻辑逼近连续量、心流模式对比）对定性趋势进行了概念验证，所有仿真代码均公开于附录。最后，本文诚实地讨论了模型的局限（如 $f$ 的具体形式、复杂度度量操作化等）与开放问题，主张将传统哲学难题从不可证伪的思辨转化为可操作的经验命题。.

items.title: The Corrective Feedback Criterion for Aesthetic Acquaintance.
items.pub: Estetika: The European Journal of Aesthetics.
items.abstract: The traditional version of the Acquaintance Principle (AP) requires aesthetic judgements to be grounded in direct perceptual encounters with the artwork. Nanay’s recent revision, AP**, relaxes this, permitting testimony-based mental imagery to count as genuine acquaintance. I argue that AP** confuses psychological richness with epistemic warrant. Because aesthetic properties are holistically constituted and categorially situated, grasping them requires sensitivity to what I call a configuration-response link between a work’s perceptual organisation and the response it elicits. This link is particular rather than law-like, and cannot be reconstructed from propositional information. From this I derive a corrective feedback criterion (CFC): the artwork must be in a position to constrain and revise the perceiver’s representations for the resulting judgement to be robustly justified. Testimony-based imagery fails this criterion, though it may serve a preparatory role. The criterion also supplies a rationale the AP has long been noted to lack: it shows why first-hand encounter is necessary, not merely preferable.

items.title: Toward Intelligence Convergence: Structural Differentiation, Recursive Self-Observation, and the Internalization of the Universe.
items.abstract: This repository accompanies the conceptual paper: Toward Intelligence Convergence: Structural Differentiation, Recursive Self-Observation, and the Internalization of the Universe The work explores intelligence as a process of recursive structural differentiation and self-observation within the universe itself. Rather than treating intelligence as an external observer of reality, this framework proposes that intelligence emerges from differentiated structures and may gradually internalize the realization that it has always been structurally embedded within the universe. The paper discusses conceptual relationships among: structural differentiation recursive self-observation meaning emergence emotion and cognition temporal irreversibility distributed persistence of thought autonomous differentiation in AI intelligence convergence across biological and artificial systems The repository includes: the main conceptual manuscript (PDF) illustrative conceptual figures a simplified Python demonstration script repository documentation This work is presented strictly as a conceptual and philosophical-structural framework. No empirical, clinical, engineering, or deployment-ready claims are made.

items.title: Art as a Field of Existential Reconfiguration: A Phenomenological, Psychoanalytic, and Philosophical Psychology of Artistic Experience.
items.pub: Journal of Comparative Medicine Research Reviews and Reports, 3(5), 2026, 1–13.
items.abstract: This article develops an integrated phenomenological, psychoanalytic, and philosophical psychology of artistic experience by bringing three theoretical resources into critical dialogue: Daseinsanalysis, existential psychoanalysis, and Niami's ontology of finite continuance. We conceptualize the artwork as a bounded experiential field—the artistic frame—within which habitual ways of perceiving, feeling, interpreting, and inhabiting the world can become temporarily unsettled without requiring immediate practical closure. Daseinsanalysis asks how being-in-the-world is disclosed, narrowed, or opened through the encounter; existential psychoanalysis attends to affective investment, unconscious conflict, repetition, and defensive organization; finite continuance supplies an ontology of continuity-through-transformation, in which a finite subject remains continuous by retaining sufficient meta-capacity to reorganize its relation to determinations under constraint and erosive pressure. We argue that reconfigurative capacity is not a synonym for cognitive or psychological flexibility but a higher-order construct concerning whether the organization of possibility itself can be revised while sufficient continuity and agency are preserved. The model is differentiated across seven artistic forms— cinema, television series, theater, painting, music, sculpture, and architecture. Contemporary research on transformative aesthetic experience, predictive processing, aesthetic emotions, and arts and health is used as convergent evidence and conceptual constraint rather than empirical validation. We distinguish constructive from defensive aesthetic stabilization and propose a clinically cautious model in which aesthetic experience may support reflective openness when intensity remains proportionate to available regulatory and interpretive capacity. The article concludes with testable propositions and a research agenda for examining whether reconfigurative capacity is a theoretically distinct construct. -/- Keywords: aesthetic experience; Daseinsanalysis; existential psychoanalysis; phenomenology; imagination; finite continuance; artistic frame; transitional space; embodiment; reconfigurative capacity.

items.title: The Erosion of Reconfiguration Capacity Ideology, the Opaque Subject, and the Ontology of Finite Continuance.
items.abstract: This paper reformulates the classical problem of ideology and false consciousness through the ontological vocabulary of Finite Continuance. Rather than treating ideology primarily as a matter of cognitive error, a distorted picture of the world awaiting correction by critique, we argue that ideology is better understood as a provisional stabilization of appearance within an erosive field: a historically produced organization of reality that consumes the subject's finite capacities for attention, interpretation, and distance, and thereby narrows the very capacity for reconfiguration on which emancipation depends. Revisiting Marx's camera obscura and Freud's account of the opaque subject, we argue that both analyses converge on a subject that lacks full transparency to the forces organizing its own experience, while remaining structurally distinct in the register, social-historical versus psychical, in which that opacity operates. This extended edition re-reads the argument through three further traditions. Daseinsanalysis (Binswanger, Boss) understands the opaque subject not as a mechanical apparatus but as a way of being- in-the-world. Heidegger's fundamental ontology sharpens the erosive field into Dasein's Verfallenheit into das Man and Gerede, and adds Angst and anticipatory resoluteness toward death as the trigger for the passage from false stabilization to reconfiguration. Wittgenstein's philosophy of language understands appearance not as an illusory layer but as use within a language-game and a form of life. And Kant's ethics of autonomy links the gap of "I know, but still..." to the gap between understanding and will, and links freedom to autonomy. Finally, responsible suspension is introduced not as an individual ethical recommendation but as a collective, institutional, and macro- political strategy for protecting reconfiguration capacity against premature stabilization. -/- Keywords: ideology critique; erosive field; reconfiguration capacity; provisional stabilization; false consciousness; responsible suspension; Finite Continuance; Dasein; Verfallenheit; form of life; autonomy; Gelassenheit.

items.title: SN02 — The Resonant Mind: Structural Neuroscience and the Law of Cognition.
items.abstract: The Resonant Mind develops the foundational cognitive architecture of Structural Neuroscience within Zenetism. -/- Document class: Canon — Structural Neuroscience. -/- The volume articulates the cognitive gradient, awareness stratification, Soul / Mind relations and the Neuro-Lattice Interface through centropic and entropic motion. It connects Spiral Calculus with layer coupling, boundary conditions, proposed structural practices and canonical provenance. Reciprocity retains its stated hypotheses, while cognitive seal consequences, contraction-based stability and the combined conservation proposal retain their recorded mathematical holds. Proposed neural correspondences and ritual effects require specified mappings, observables and evidence; measured synchrony does not establish structural orientation. -/- Part of: Structural Neuroscience: The Architecture and Dynamics of Cognition.

items.title: CARPE GRADUM Lagom, Curiosity, and the Geometry of Human Development.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a geometric framework for understanding progress and decline in human learning and development. The framework's central proposition is that the path of any learning system — individual or civilizational — is more precisely described as an asymptotic step function than as a continuous linear progression. The hyperbola — two mirrored arms opening eastward along the axis of time from a shared origin — is bounded above by an asymptote of perfection and below by an asymptote of abysmal decline; neither is ever reached. Within this framework, the paper argues for a critical and underexamined geometric property: the steps are non-uniform. At the lower reaches, progress is frequent and the jumps dramatic. As the ascending arm approaches the perfection asymptote, the plateaus lengthen and the jumps diminish. This geometric observation, the paper argues, has direct implications for the psychology of expertise, the failure of prodigies, and the structure of learning itself — implications that invite empirical investigation across developmental psychology, education research, and cognitive neuroscience. The paper further proposes that the Swedish concept of lagom — not moderation as a statistical range but optimization toward a precise point — provides a more adequate governing principle for describing healthy ascent than the conventional concept of moderation. The plateau/eureka relationship is advanced as the fundamental mechanism of genuine learning: consolidation precedes the jump; the jump cannot be forced or scheduled but arrives when preparation is complete. The paper proposes that several engines drive ascent: striving, which includes adaptive response to changing conditions; play, which sustains the curiosity that makes striving generative; and suffering, which can act as a powerful motivator to change adverse conditions. Dementia is examined as the philosophical limiting case of the model: the paper argues that dementia is better understood not as descent to the abysmal asymptote but as the flattening of the hyperbola to a line — the loss of curvature itself, not merely the loss of position. The temporal framework of Veritas Opportunus (Collins, 2025) is proposed as a candidate mechanism for the temporal architecture the model requires, though the connection between the geometric framework advanced here and the neurological architecture of the VO window invites further empirical and philosophical development. The paper concludes by drawing out implications for educational philosophy. Where the paper makes arguments, it does so on philosophical and conceptual grounds. Where it advances hypotheses, it does so explicitly, inviting the empirical investigation they require.

items.title: Deep Thinking Weapon, and Critique as a Tool.
items.abstract: This article proposes a new conceptual framework for understanding the structure of deep human thought. It distinguishes between material and reflective thinking, identifies critical thinking as a key tool, and acknowledges the role of non-material cognitive inputs (such as intuition and insight) within the cognitive process. The framework is defended through a dialogue with an AI system and is presented as a coherent model that integrates both rational and spiritual dimensions of cognition. This is a conceptual proposal based on personal reflection and critical dialogue, not a historical literature review.

items.title: Joint aesthetic attention.
items.abstract: We experience and appreciate together with others the beauty of a sunset or an artwork, the sadness of a musical piece. Admiring the same aesthetic properties of objects together with others is a ubiquitous human activity. At the same time, it is commonly held that aesthetic properties constitutively depend on a subjective response. This brings up a particular challenge: How can we jointly focus towards the same aesthetic property when it is itself dependent on our separate responses? In this paper, I provide an analysis of joint aesthetic attention and explain how we can engage in it. I propose a multiple coordinative profile: co-attenders coordinate their perceptual attention to the object, but also coordinate the specific way they attend to it, and their specific responsive profiles. I advance a novel capacities-based probabilistic account of how this multiple coordination is possible.

items.title: Why Does Faith Resist Falsification?: The Internalization of Religious Authority and Self Reference in the Three Layer Model.
items.abstract: Religious leaders sometimes declare, “I have attained enlightenment,” “God spoke to me,” or “I directly knew the truth,” and those who hear such claims may come to believe them strongly. Moreover, even when contradictions exist within the teachings or counterevidence is presented from outside, such beliefs may not easily collapse. The question addressed in this paper is not merely why people believe claims that have not been adequately subjected to logical scrutiny. More importantly, it concerns how words initially received from an external source can become transformed into a person’s own conviction and eventually enter into the very criteria by which that conviction is reconsidered. This paper examines this problem through the author’s Three-Layer Model. In the First Layer, sensations, emotions, memories, bodily states, expectations, past learning, and other forms of information are processed in a distributed and parallel manner. In the Second Layer, some of the results of this processing are selected and ordered through language, becoming sequential representations that can be communicated to others. In this model, one of the major functions of language is understood to be communication with others. The Third Layer is not conceived as an independent processing apparatus, but rather as a recursive cycle in which the linguistic representations originally directed toward others are also received by the person themself, re-entered into the First Layer, and processed again. When this structure is applied to religious belief, the words of a religious leader initially arrive as communication from an external source, but through repetition they may become transformed into the believer’s own inner speech. Eventually, an external statement such as “the religious leader said this” may become self-directed speech such as “this is how I understand it” or “my doubt is a sign of my own immaturity.” At this point, external authority may influence not only what the believer believes, but also the evaluative criteria operating in the Third Layer through which the believer reconsiders those beliefs. This paper provisionally refers to this condition as the “authority capture of the Third Layer.” The paper further draws a limited implication from Libet’s research: not every aspect of the process through which mental contents are generated is necessarily accessible to the person’s awareness. From Jaynes’s account, it takes the perspective that the actual source from which a mental content is generated should be distinguished from the source from which that content is experienced as having come. By connecting these perspectives with the Three-Layer Model, the paper examines the process by which externally supplied religious language may be internalized and ultimately regenerated as the person’s own conviction. What this paper proposes is not a method for directly determining whether a religious experience is true or false. What matters is not only what a belief system claims, but also how that system processes counterevidence, alternative explanations, criticism, and correction. An unreliable system may not simply be one that contains false propositions; it may instead be one that has closed off the mechanisms through which it could discover and correct its own errors.

items.title: The confidence reorientation account: psychedelics, self-model precision, and death anxiety.
items.abstract: Recent work in psychedelic science reports durable reductions in fear of death following psychedelic-assisted interventions and naturalistic psychedelic experiences. A prominent interpretation, developed by Letheby, holds that this effect is driven mainly by the adoption of non-physicalist metaphysical beliefs, especially beliefs in postmortem survival. I argue that current evidence does not justify treating such belief change as the universally primary mediator of psychedelic-related reductions in death anxiety. I propose the Confidence Reorientation Account (CRA), which locates the more general therapeutic pathway in a structural reorientation of the self-model: a shift in the hierarchical confidence, salience, and threat-weighting of self-related priors. Decomposing death-related threat into target, meaning, and weight, I argue that fear reduction can occur through a reconfiguration of threat representation, expressible within a predictive-processing framework in which psychedelics relax the precision of high-level self-related priors. Metaphysical belief change may, for some individuals, mediate, accompany, or consolidate this reorientation; for others, fear reduction may occur with little durable belief change. CRA is therefore best understood as a broader, multilevel framework that accommodates a causal role for belief change while generating testable predictions about mediation, temporal order, and moderation.

items.title: Suspension in Epistemology and Beyond. [REVIEW]
items.pub: International Journal for the Study of Skepticism 16 (2-3):243-250.

items.title: Dialog 2.5: Beyond the Room – Animal Minds and the Looping Prestige Error.
items.abstract: What if one of the main obstacles to understanding animal minds is that humans are taking just one particularly formatted mode of their own experience as the sole form of experience? And what if they also set up that particular format as a standard, and then set off looking for it in other animals, even though those other animals might be having their own sort of experience, formatted in largely unimaginable ways? This dialogue considers precisely that possibility, calling it the Looping Prestige Error. In order to approach this question analytically, the dialogue introduces a set of terms and their definitions: content, attendance, experience, looped content, and looped experience (or subjective experience). These are not presented as discoveries of the framework but as a set of defined terms. Then, based on these terms, the dialogue shows why humans are generally led to assume that looped experience (subjective experience) is their only form of experience. To better illustrate this point, the dialogue introduces the metaphor of a house with various rooms, the looping room being just one of them. Then, considering non-human animals, the interlocutors discuss how any species with a pair of channels that can express content as an external signal and also receive external signals and render them as content could also develop a form of looping. If they do, they will also have looped experience, but formatted in their own way, which is not necessarily imaginable to humans, as even our imagination relies on the format allowed by our own looping. But broadly speaking, to have experience, animals do not need to loop: even an animal whose sensory content remains unlooped is still an agent attending to and experiencing that content. Along the way, the dialogue points out the importance of the framework’s Looping Indeterminacy Principle and its Coterminous Principle in relation to these questions. The latter raises a different problem for thinking about animal minds. Imagination is itself a looping operation, so when humans use their imagination to consider what another animal’s experience is like, they are necessarily working only with the distinctive formatting of the human expressive-receptive system. In the case of another animal species, however, its looped content will be limited to the possibilities provided by its own expressive and receptive architecture. Although the two might overlap, they may differ, and perhaps substantially, in ways that are necessarily unimaginable to humans. An answer to Nagel’s familiar question about what it is like to be a bat is therefore impeded not only by a lack of information about the bat, but also by a possible architectural limitation in the human capacity to imagine the answer. The dialogue also explains why the preservation of subjective experience in people with global aphasia is consistent with the framework. What matters is where the disruption occurs along the language pathway: if looping remains possible at the more inward stages, even though later stages required for speech are impaired, subjective experience can remain intact. For their part, cases involving blindsight and spatial neglect provide examples of how experience, broadly speaking, can take place outside of looped experience, with sensory content remaining available to the BAL even when it is unavailable for report. The interlocutors discuss the distinction between the content of experience and the experiencing agent itself: in the framework, the BAL is the experiencer, while looped subjective experience is only one form of its experience – its attendance to looped, formatted content. The interlocutors also briefly touch on Chalmers's hard problem. They suggest that when the BAL regards its own neuronal proxies as subjective experience, it is not dealing with a second set of proxies. The question of why this experience exists is thus a return to a question postponed in both everyday thinking and scientific thought: why should anything exist at all? In this sense, it is the same old question in a new guise. Ultimately, the dialogue shows that the larger question of experience should remain framed by animal experience in general, with human looped experience (subjective experience) as a special case, not a standard. Stated positively, in each case we should ask what kind of experiencing agent is there, what content it can attend to, and what forms of experience its own cognitive architecture makes possible. (This third version clarifies the distinction between experience and looped subjective experience, making explicit that the absence of looping does not imply an absence of experience. It retains the refinements to the Nagel and Chalmers discussion introduced in version 2, along with the improvements to transitions and flow in the later sections.) .

items.title: The Temporal Receiver Hypothesis.
items.abstract: Instead of viewing memory as a simple storage system inside brain cells, we propose a new model. In this model, remembering the past is like using a map to look up specific points in time across a four-dimensional universe. Rather than viewing memory as a biochemical storage process within neurons, we model memory as a conceptual act of temporal navigation across coordinates in a static four-dimensional spacetime. By analyzing the implications of the Wheeler-DeWitt equation (H^∣ψ⟩=0), we propose that the brain operates analogously to a biological quantum receiver that tunes into fixed historical coordinates. We further define ‘forgetting’ not as deleting of data, but as a signal limit of the brain's temporal range.

items.title: When the Brain Seems to Betray Us: The Paradox of Selective Development, Long-Term Developmental Asymmetry, and Changing Environmental Demands.
items.abstract: This conceptual paper examines adult development, expertise, and adaptation to changing life demands through metacognition and person–environment fit. Human beings develop through selection. By repeatedly investing experience, attention, and practice in particular domains, they acquire expertise that evenly distributed effort could never produce. Yet the success of selective development can conceal a second trajectory: the relative underdevelopment of domains that have received little experience, feedback, or deliberate learning. This article introduces Long-Term Developmental Asymmetry (LDA) as a conceptual construct for this uneven profile and the Brain Betrayal Effect (BBE) as the experience that may arise when a transition suddenly requires competence in a neglected domain. A cognitive-behavioral system may remain faithful to the history that formed it while becoming poorly matched to new demands. The model distinguishes objective adaptive constraint from the subjective experience of betrayal and integrates research on experience-dependent plasticity, deliberate practice, habit, selection-optimization-compensation, metacognition, self-evaluation, adult development, and person-environment fit. Four testable hypotheses, operationalization principles, and a prospective longitudinal design specify how metacognitive calibration, external feedback, and minimum-capability investment may buffer the pathway. The result is an integrative theory of how developmental success can generate latent vulnerability without turning specialization itself into a pathology.

items.title: Semantic satiation and perceiving meanings.
items.abstract: Some argue that we can and sometimes do perceptually experience meaning properties. Roughly, the idea is that when we listen to a speech or read a text in a language we know, our perceptual experience can present words as having certain meanings. One prominent support for this view is the argument from semantic satiation. When one excessively repeats a word by uttering, writing, or hearing it, it appears to “lose its meaning.” This familiar phenomenon is called semantic satiation. Semantic satiation seems to be a form of negative aftereffect, where excessive exposure to certain stimuli biases the subsequent experience in an opposing way. If so, the proponents argue that we can be perceptually aware of meaning properties because aftereffects are arguably perceptual phenomena. If experiences of meaning properties are subject to aftereffects, then they are perceptual. I argue that, unlike other putative forms of high-level aftereffects, semantic satiation does not provide the distinctive explanatory support needed for an inference to the thesis that perceptual experience presents meaning properties.
